1.57.s:
sanandana uvāca
vaidikaṃ laukikaṃ cāpi chando dvividhamucyate /
mātrāvarṇavibhedena taccāpi dvividhaṃ punaḥ //
1.57.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
वैदिकं लौकिकं चापि छन्दो द्विविधमुच्यते ।
मात्रावर्णविभेदेन तच्चापि द्विविधं पुनः ॥
1.57.m: Sanandana said: / Meter is said to be twofold: Vedic and classical; / and that is again twofold according to the distinction of morae and syllables.

1.57.s:
mayau rasau tajau bhanau gururlaghurapidvija /
kāraṇaṃ chandasi proktāśchandaḥśāstraviśāradaiḥ //
1.57.d:
मयौ रसौ तजौ भनौ गुरुर्लघुरपिद्विज ।
कारणं छन्दसि प्रोक्ताश्छन्दःशास्त्रविशारदैः ॥
1.57.m: M, Y, R, S, T, J, Bh, and N, and also guru and laghu, O twice-born, / are declared by scholars of metrics to be the basic elements in meter.

1.57.s:
sarvago magaṇaḥ prokto mukhalo yagaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
madhyalo ragaṇaśvaiva prāntyagaḥ sagaṇo mataḥ //
1.57.d:
सर्वगो मगणः प्रोक्तो मुखलो यगणः स्मृतः ।
मध्यलो रगणश्वैव प्रान्त्यगः सगणो मतः ॥
1.57.m: The ma-gaṇa is declared to be all long; the ya-gaṇa is known to have a short first [syllable]; / the ra-gaṇa has a short middle [syllable]; and the sa-gaṇa is considered to have a long final [syllable].

1.57.s:
tagaṇoṃ'talaghuḥ khyāto madhyago jo bhaādigaḥ /
trilaghurnagaṇaḥ proktastrikā varṇagaṇā mune //
1.57.d:
तगणोंऽतलघुः ख्यातो मध्यगो जो भआदिगः ।
त्रिलघुर्नगणः प्रोक्तस्त्रिका वर्णगणा मुने ॥
1.57.m: The ta-gaṇa is renowned for having a short end; the ja-gaṇa has a long middle; the bha-gaṇa has a long beginning; / the na-gaṇa is declared to have three short [syllables]. These triplets are the syllabic groups, O sage.

1.57.s:
caturlāstu gaṇāḥ pañca proktā āryādisaṃmatāḥ /
saṃyogaśca visargaścānusvāro laghutaḥ paraḥ //
1.57.d:
चतुर्लास्तु गणाः पञ्च प्रोक्ता आर्यादिसंमताः ।
संयोगश्च विसर्गश्चानुस्वारो लघुतः परः ॥
1.57.m: The five groups of four morae are accepted in the Āryā and other [meters]. / A conjunct consonant, a visarga, and an anusvāra following a short [vowel]

1.57.s:
laghordīrghatvamākhyāti dīrgho go lo laghurmataḥ /
pādaścaturthabhāgaḥ syādvicchedoyatirucyate //
1.57.d:
लघोर्दीर्घत्वमाख्याति दीर्घो गो लो लघुर्मतः ।
पादश्चतुर्थभागः स्याद्विच्छेदोयतिरुच्यते ॥
1.57.m: declare the heaviness of the short [syllable]; a long [syllable] is considered ‘ga’ and a short is ‘la’. / A quarter consists of a fourth part; a caesura is called a yati.

1.57.s:
samamarddhasamaṃ vṛttaṃ viṣamaṃ cāpi nārada /
tulyalakṣaṇataḥ pādacatuṣke samamucyate //
1.57.d:
सममर्द्धसमं वृत्तं विषमं चापि नारद ।
तुल्यलक्षणतः पादचतुष्के सममुच्यते ॥
1.57.m: A meter is even, half-even, or uneven, O Nārada; / it is called even when the four quarters have identical characteristics.

1.57.s:
āditrike dvicaturthe samamarddhasamaṃ tatam /
lakṣma bhinnaṃ yasya pādacatuṣke viṣamaṃ hi tat //
1.57.d:
आदित्रिके द्विचतुर्थे सममर्द्धसमं ततम् ।
लक्ष्म भिन्नं यस्य पादचतुष्के विषमं हि तत् ॥
1.57.m: When the first and third [quarters], and the second and fourth [quarters] are alike, it is half-even; / that whose four quarters have different characteristics is indeed uneven.

1.57.s:
ekākṣarātsamārabhya varṇaikaikasya vṛddhitaḥ /
ṣaḍviṃśatyakṣaraṃ yāvatpādastāvatpṛthak pṛthak //
1.57.d:
एकाक्षरात्समारभ्य वर्णैकैकस्य वृद्धितः ।
षड्विंशत्यक्षरं यावत्पादस्तावत्पृथक् पृथक् ॥
1.57.m: Beginning with one syllable and increasing by one syllable each / up to twenty-six syllables, each quarter is distinct.

1.57.s:
tatparaṃ caṇḍavṛṣṭyādidaṇḍakāḥ parikalpitāḥ /
tribhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ padairgāthāḥ śṛṇu saṃjñā yathottaram //
1.57.d:
तत्परं चण्डवृष्ट्यादिदण्डकाः परिकल्पिताः ।
त्रिभिः षड्भिः पदैर्गाथाः शृणु संज्ञा यथोत्तरम् ॥
1.57.m: Beyond that, the daṇḍakas beginning with Caṇḍavṛṣṭi are reckoned; / gāthās have three or six quarters. Hear their names in progressive order:

1.57.s:
uktātyuktā tathā madhyā pratiṣṭānyā supūrvikā /
gāyatryuṣṇiganuṣṭaṣṭapca bṛhatī paṅktireva ca //
1.57.d:
उक्तात्युक्ता तथा मध्या प्रतिष्टान्या सुपूर्विका ।
गायत्र्युष्णिगनुष्टष्टप्च बृहती पङ्क्तिरेव च ॥
1.57.m: Uktā, Atyuktā, Madhyā, Pratiṣṭhā, the one with ‘su’ before it [Supratiṣṭhā], / Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, and Paṅkti,

1.57.s:
triṣṭupca jagatī caiva tathātijagatī matā /
śakkarī sātipūrvā ca aṣṭyatyaṣṭī tataḥ smṛte //
1.57.d:
त्रिष्टुप्च जगती चैव तथातिजगती मता ।
शक्करी सातिपूर्वा च अष्ट्यत्यष्टी ततः स्मृते ॥
1.57.m: Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, and also Atijagatī is recognized; / Śakkarī, the one with ‘ati’ before it [Atiśakkarī], then Aṣṭi and Atyaṣṭi are remembered;

1.57.s:
dhṛtiśca vidhṛtiścaiva kṛtiḥ prakṛtirākṛtiḥ /
vikṛtiḥ saṃkṛtiścaiva tathātikṛtirutkṛtiḥ //
1.57.d:
धृतिश्च विधृतिश्चैव कृतिः प्रकृतिराकृतिः ।
विकृतिः संकृतिश्चैव तथातिकृतिरुत्कृतिः ॥
1.57.m: Dhṛti, Atidhṛti, Kṛti, Prakṛti, Ākṛti, / Vikṛti, Saṃkṛti, and also Atikṛti and Utkṛti.

1.57.s:
ityetāśchandasāṃ saṃjñāḥ prastārādbhedabhāgikāḥ /
pāde sarvagurau pūrvīllaghuṃ sthāpya guroradhaḥ //
1.57.d:
इत्येताश्छन्दसां संज्ञाः प्रस्ताराद्भेदभागिकाः ।
पादे सर्वगुरौ पूर्वील्लघुं स्थाप्य गुरोरधः ॥
1.57.m: These are the names of the meters divided by permutations. / In a quarter of all long [syllables], placing a short [syllable] beneath the first long [syllable],

1.57.s:
yathopari tathā śeṣamagre prāravannyasedapi /
eṣa prastāra udito yāvatsarvalaghurbhavet //
1.57.d:
यथोपरि तथा शेषमग्रे प्रारवन्न्यसेदपि ।
एष प्रस्तार उदितो यावत्सर्वलघुर्भवेत् ॥
1.57.m: and setting down the rest before it just as above— / this permutation is described, [repeating] until it consists of all short [syllables].

1.57.s:
naṣṭāṅkārddhe same laḥ syādvipam saiva sorddhagaḥ /
uddiṣṭe dviguṇānādyādaṅgānsaṃmolya lasthitān //
1.57.d:
नष्टाङ्कार्द्धे समे लः स्याद्विपम् सैव सोर्द्धगः ।
उद्दिष्टे द्विगुणानाद्यादङ्गान्संमोल्य लस्थितान् ॥
1.57.m: When half of the lost number is even, it is ‘la’; when uneven, that very [syllable] with ‘sa’ goes above. / In the indicated [permutation], having doubled the numbers from the first, summing those placed on ‘la’,

1.57.s:
kṛtvā sekānvadaitsaṃkhyāmiti prāhuḥ purāvidaḥ /
vaṇānsekānvṛttabhavānuttarādharataḥ sthitān //
1.57.d:
कृत्वा सेकान्वदैत्संख्यामिति प्राहुः पुराविदः ।
वणान्सेकान्वृत्तभवानुत्तराधरतः स्थितान् ॥
1.57.m: and adding one to them, one should state the number; so the knowers of the past have declared. / Placing the syllables derived from the meters, with one added, situated from top to bottom,

1.57.s:
ekādikramataścaikānuparyyupari vinyaset /
upāntyato nivarteta tyajannekaikamūrddhataḥ //
1.57.d:
एकादिक्रमतश्चैकानुपर्य्युपरि विन्यसेत् ।
उपान्त्यतो निवर्तेत त्यजन्नेकैकमूर्द्धतः ॥
1.57.m: one should place them one above the other in order from one onward; / one should turn back from the penultimate, dropping them one by one from above.

1.57.s:
uparyādyādgurorevamekadvyādilagakriyā /
lagakriyāṅkasaṃdohe bhavetsaṃkhyāvimiśrite //
1.57.d:
उपर्याद्याद्गुरोरेवमेकद्व्यादिलगक्रिया ।
लगक्रियाङ्कसंदोहे भवेत्संख्याविमिश्रिते ॥
1.57.m: Above the first long [syllable], in this manner, is the operation of ones, twos, and so forth, for shorts and longs; / in the sum of the digits of the operation of longs and shorts, it becomes mixed with the number.

1.57.s:
uddiṣṭāṅkasamāhāraḥ saiko vā janayedimām /
saṃkhyaiva dviguṇaikonā sadbhiradhvā prakīrtitaḥ //
1.57.d:
उद्दिष्टाङ्कसमाहारः सैको वा जनयेदिमाम् ।
संख्यैव द्विगुणैकोना सद्भिरध्वा प्रकीर्तितः ॥
1.57.m: Or the sum of the indicated digits increased by one produces this; / that very number doubled and diminished by one is proclaimed by the wise as the path.

1.57.s:
ityetatkiñcidākhyātaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ chandasāṃ nune /
prastāroktaprabhedānāṃ nāmānāṃstyaṃ pragāhate //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde saṅkṣiptacchandovarṇanaṃ nāma saptapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.57.d:
इत्येतत्किञ्चिदाख्यातं लक्षणं छन्दसां नुने ।
प्रस्तारोक्तप्रभेदानां नामानांस्त्यं प्रगाहते ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे सङ्क्षिप्तच्छन्दोवर्णनं नाम सप्तपञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.57.m:
Thus, O sage, some definition of meters has been stated. / Who can plumb the end of the names of the varieties taught in permutations?

Thus ends the fifty-seventh chapter, named ‘Brief Description of Meters’, in the second quarter of the Bṛhadupākhyāna in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.58.s:
nārada uvāca
anūcānaprasaṃgena vedāṅgānyakhilāni ca /
śrutāni tvanmukhāṃbhojātsamāsavyāsayogataḥ //
1.58.d:
नारद उवाच
अनूचानप्रसंगेन वेदाङ्गान्यखिलानि च ।
श्रुतानि त्वन्मुखांभोजात्समासव्यासयोगतः ॥
1.58.m: Nārada said: / In the course of [the discussion of] one learned in the Veda, all the limbs of the Veda / have been heard from your lotus face in concise and expanded form.

1.58.s:
śukotpattiṃ samācakṣva vistareṇa mahāmate /
sanandana uvāca
meruśṛṅge kila purā karṇikāravanāyate //
1.58.d:
शुकोत्पत्तिं समाचक्ष्व विस्तरेण महामते ।
सनन्दन उवाच
मेरुशृङ्गे किल पुरा कर्णिकारवनायते ॥
1.58.m: Relate to me the birth of Śuka at length, O noble-minded one. / Sanandana said: / Formerly, on the peak of Meru, in an expanse of Karṇikāra forests,

1.58.s:
vijahāra mahodevo bhaumaibhūtagaṇaivṛtaḥ /
śailarājasutā caiva devī tatrābhavatpurā //
1.58.d:
विजहार महोदेवो भौमैभूतगणैवृतः ।
शैलराजसुता चैव देवी तत्राभवत्पुरा ॥
1.58.m: Mahādeva was sporting, surrounded by earthly hosts of spirits; / and the goddess, daughter of the king of mountains, was also there long ago.

1.58.s:
tatra divyaṃ tapastepe kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ /
yogenātmānamāviśya yogadharmaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.58.d:
तत्र दिव्यं तपस्तेपे कृष्णद्वैपायनः प्रभुः ।
योगेनात्मानमाविश्य योगधर्मपरायणः ॥
1.58.m: There the lord Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana performed celestial asceticism, / entering into the self through yoga, devoted to the duty of yoga.

1.58.s:
dhārayansa tapastepe putrārthaṃ sunisaṃttamaḥ /
agnerbhūmestathā vāyorantarikṣasya cābhitaḥ //
1.58.d:
धारयन्स तपस्तेपे पुत्रार्थं सुनिसंत्तमः ।
अग्नेर्भूमेस्तथा वायोरन्तरिक्षस्य चाभितः ॥
1.58.m: Restraining himself, that best of sages performed asceticism for the sake of a son, / [wishing:] ‘May a son be born to me possessing virility equal to

1.58.s:
vīryeṇa saṃmataḥ putro mama bhūyāditi sma ha /
saṃkalpenātha so 'nena duṣprāpamakagṛtātmabhiḥ //
1.58.d:
वीर्येण संमतः पुत्रो मम भूयादिति स्म ह ।
संकल्पेनाथ सो ऽनेन दुष्प्रापमकगृतात्मभिः ॥
1.58.m: fire, earth, wind, and the atmosphere on all sides!’ / Then, with this resolve, which is difficult for the unrefined to attain,

1.58.s:
varayāmāsa deveśamāsthitastapa uttamam /
atiṣṭanmārutāhāraḥ śataṃ kila samāḥ prabhuḥ //
1.58.d:
वरयामास देवेशमास्थितस्तप उत्तमम् ।
अतिष्टन्मारुताहारः शतं किल समाः प्रभुः ॥
1.58.m: he, established in supreme asceticism, sought a boon from the Lord of gods. / Subsisting on wind, the master stood for a hundred years,

1.58.s:
ārādhayanmahādevaṃ bahurūpamumāpatim /
tatra brahmarṣayaścaiva sarve devarṣayastathā //
1.58.d:
आराधयन्महादेवं बहुरूपमुमापतिम् ।
तत्र ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव सर्वे देवर्षयस्तथा ॥
1.58.m: worshiping Mahādeva, the multi-formed lord of Umā. / There the celestial sages and all the divine sages,

1.58.s:
lokapālāśca sādhyāśca vasubhiścāṣṭabhiḥ saha /
ādityāścaiva rudrāśca divākaraniśākarau //
1.58.d:
लोकपालाश्च साध्याश्च वसुभिश्चाष्टभिः सह ।
आदित्याश्चैव रुद्राश्च दिवाकरनिशाकरौ ॥
1.58.m: the guardians of the world, the sādhyas together with the eight Vasus, / the Ādityas, the Rudras, the sun, and the moon,

1.58.s:
viśvā vasuśca gandharvaḥ siddhāścāpsarāsāṃgaṇāḥ /
tatra rudro mahādevaḥ karṇikāramayīṃ śubhām //
1.58.d:
विश्वा वसुश्च गन्धर्वः सिद्धाश्चाप्सरासांगणाः ।
तत्र रुद्रो महादेवः कर्णिकारमयीं शुभाम् ॥
1.58.m: the Viśvedevas, the gandharvas, the siddhas, and troops of apsarases [were present]. / There Rudra Mahādeva, wearing an auspicious garland made of karṇikāra flowers,

1.58.s:
dhārayānaḥ srajaṃ bhāti śāradīva niśākaraḥ /
tasnin divye vane ramye devadevarṣisaṃkule //
1.58.d:
धारयानः स्रजं भाति शारदीव निशाकरः ।
तस्निन् दिव्ये वने रम्ये देवदेवर्षिसंकुले ॥
1.58.m: shone like the autumn moon. / In that celestial, lovely forest crowded with gods and divine sages,

1.58.s:
āsthitaḥ paramaṃ yogaṃ vyāsaḥ putrārthamudyataḥ /
na cāsya hīyate varṇo na glānirupajāyate //
1.58.d:
आस्थितः परमं योगं व्यासः पुत्रार्थमुद्यतः ।
न चास्य हीयते वर्णो न ग्लानिरुपजायते ॥
1.58.m: Vyāsa, established in supreme yoga, strove for the sake of a son. / Neither did his complexion fade nor did weariness overcome him;

1.58.s:
trayāṇāmapilokānāṃ tadadbhutamivābhavat /
jaṭāśca tejasā tasya vaiśvānaraśikhopamāḥ //
1.58.d:
त्रयाणामपिलोकानां तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ।
जटाश्च तेजसा तस्य वैश्वानरशिखोपमाः ॥
1.58.m: it was like a marvel even to the three worlds. / His matted locks, like the flames of fire through their splendor,

1.58.s:
prajvalantyaḥ sma dṛśyante yuktasyāmitatejasaḥ /
evaṃ vidhena tapasā tasya bhaktyā ca nārada //
1.58.d:
प्रज्वलन्त्यः स्म दृश्यन्ते युक्तस्यामिततेजसः ।
एवं विधेन तपसा तस्य भक्त्या च नारद ॥
1.58.m: were seen blazing, as he remained disciplined and of boundless luster. / By such asceticism and by his devotion, O Nārada,

1.58.s:
maheśvaraḥ prasannātmā cakāra manasā matim /
uvāca cainaṃ bhagavāṃstryaṃbakaḥ prahasanniva //
1.58.d:
महेश्वरः प्रसन्नात्मा चकार मनसा मतिम् ।
उवाच चैनं भगवांस्त्र्यंबकः प्रहसन्निव ॥
1.58.m: Maheśvara, his heart pleased, formed a resolution in his mind. / And the blessed Tryambaka, as if smiling, said to him:

1.58.s:
yathā hyagniyathā vāyuryathā bhūmiryathā jalam /
yathā khe ca tathā śuddho bhaviṣyati sutastaṃva //
1.58.d:
यथा ह्यग्नियथा वायुर्यथा भूमिर्यथा जलम् ।
यथा खे च तथा शुद्धो भविष्यति सुतस्तंव ॥
1.58.m: ‘Just as fire, as wind, as earth, as water, / and as space, even so pure will your son be.

1.58.s:
tadbhāvabhāgī tadbuddhistadātmā tadupāśrayaḥ /
tejasā tasya lokāṃstrīnyaśaḥ prāpsyati kevalam //
1.58.d:
तद्भावभागी तद्बुद्धिस्तदात्मा तदुपाश्रयः ।
तेजसा तस्य लोकांस्त्रीन्यशः प्राप्स्यति केवलम् ॥
1.58.m: Sharing in their nature, having their intellect, having their essence, having recourse to them, / by his splendor he will attain undivided fame in the three worlds.’

1.58.s:
evaṃ labdhvā varaṃ devo vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ /
araṇiṃ tvatha saṃgṛhya mamanthāgnicikīrṣayā //
1.58.d:
एवं लब्ध्वा वरं देवो व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः ।
अरणिं त्वथ संगृह्य ममन्थाग्निचिकीर्षया ॥
1.58.m: Having thus received the boon, the divine Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, / then took the fire-drill, desiring to produce fire by churning.

1.58.s:
atha rūpaṃ paraṃ vipra bibhratīṃ svena tejasā /
ghṛtācīṃ nāmāpsarasaṃ dadarśa bhagavānnṛṣiḥ //
1.58.d:
अथ रूपं परं विप्र बिभ्रतीं स्वेन तेजसा ।
घृताचीं नामाप्सरसं ददर्श भगवान्नृषिः ॥
1.58.m: Then, O twice-born, the blessed sage saw an apsaras named Ghṛtācī, / displaying supreme beauty through her own luster.

1.58.s:
sa tāmapsarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā kāmamohitaḥ /
abhavadbhagavānvyāso vane tasminmunīśvara //
1.58.d:
स तामप्सरसं दृष्ट्वा सहसा काममोहितः ।
अभवद्भगवान्व्यासो वने तस्मिन्मुनीश्वर ॥
1.58.m: Seeing that apsaras, the blessed Vyāsa suddenly became bewildered by desire / in that forest, O lord of sages.

1.58.s:
sā tu kṛtvā tadā vyāsaṃ kāmasaṃvignamānasam /
śukībhūyā mahāramyā ghṛtācī samupāgamat //
1.58.d:
सा तु कृत्वा तदा व्यासं कामसंविग्नमानसम् ।
शुकीभूया महारम्या घृताची समुपागमत् ॥
1.58.m: Having thus agitated Vyāsa’s mind with desire, / that most charming Ghṛtācī, having turned into a female parrot, approached him.

1.58.s:
sa tāmapsarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpeṇānyenasaṃvṛtām /
smararājenānugataḥ sarvagātrātigena ha //
1.58.d:
स तामप्सरसं दृष्ट्वा रूपेणान्येनसंवृताम् ।
स्मरराजेनानुगतः सर्वगात्रातिगेन ह ॥
1.58.m: Seeing that apsaras disguised in another form, / he was overtaken by the king of love which pervades every limb.

1.58.s:
sa tu mahatā nigṛhṇan hṛcchayaṃ muniḥ /
na śaśāka niyantuṃ taṃ vyāsaḥ pravisṛtaṃ manaḥ //
1.58.d:
स तु महता निगृह्णन् हृच्छयं मुनिः ।
न शशाक नियन्तुं तं व्यासः प्रविसृतं मनः ॥
1.58.m: Though restraining desire with great effort, the sage Vyāsa / was unable to control his mind that had run wild.

1.58.s:
bhāvitvāñcaiva bhāvyasya ghṛtācyā vapuṣā /
hṛtam yatnānniyacchataścāpi mune etañcikīrṣayā //
1.58.d:
भावित्वाञ्चैव भाव्यस्य घृताच्या वपुषा ।
हृतम् यत्नान्नियच्छतश्चापि मुने एतञ्चिकीर्षया ॥
1.58.m: Because of what was destined to be, O sage, [his mind] was seized by the beauty of Ghṛtācī, / even as he held it back with effort out of a wish to accomplish this.

1.58.s:
araṇyāmeva sahasā tasya śukramavāpatat /
śukre nirmathyamāne 'syāṃ śuko jajñe mahātapāḥ //
1.58.d:
अरण्यामेव सहसा तस्य शुक्रमवापतत् ।
शुक्रे निर्मथ्यमाने ऽस्यां शुको जज्ञे महातपाः ॥
1.58.m: Suddenly his semen fell right onto the kindling stick; / as it was churned upon it, Śuka of great austerities was born.

1.58.s:
paramarṣirmahāyogī araṇīgarbhasaṃbhavaḥ /
yathaiva hi samiddho 'gnirbhāti havyamupāttavān //
1.58.d:
परमर्षिर्महायोगी अरणीगर्भसंभवः ।
यथैव हि समिद्धो ऽग्निर्भाति हव्यमुपात्तवान् ॥
1.58.m: A supreme sage, a great yogin, born from the womb of the kindling stick, / he shone just like a kindled fire that has received an offering.

1.58.s:
tathā rūpaḥ śuko jajñe prajvalanniva tejasā /
bibhrañcitraṃ ca viprendra rūpavarṇamanuttamam //
1.58.d:
तथा रूपः शुको जज्ञे प्रज्वलन्निव तेजसा ।
बिभ्रञ्चित्रं च विप्रेन्द्र रूपवर्णमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.58.m: Śuka was born with such a form, blazing, as it were, with fiery splendor, / bearing a wondrous and unsurpassed beauty and complexion, O best of brahmins.

1.58.s:
taṃ gaṅgāṃ saritāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ merupṛṣṭhe svarūpiṇīm /
abhyetya snāpayāmāsa vāriṇā svena nārada //
1.58.d:
तं गङ्गां सरितां श्रेष्ठां मेरुपृष्ठे स्वरूपिणीम् ।
अभ्येत्य स्नापयामास वारिणा स्वेन नारद ॥
1.58.m: The Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, arriving in her embodied form on the summit of Meru, / bathed him with her own water, O Nārada.

1.58.s:
kṛṣṇājinaṃ cāntarikṣācchukārthe bhuvyavāpatat /
jagīyanta ca gandharvā nanṛtuñcāpsarogaṇāḥ //
1.58.d:
कृष्णाजिनं चान्तरिक्षाच्छुकार्थे भुव्यवापतत् ।
जगीयन्त च गन्धर्वा ननृतुञ्चाप्सरोगणाः ॥
1.58.m: And a black antelope skin fell from the sky to the earth for Śuka's sake; / gandharvas sang and multitudes of apsarases danced.

1.58.s:
devadundubhayaścaiva prāvādyanta mahāsvanāḥ /
viśvāvasuśca gandharvastathā tuṃburunāradau //
1.58.d:
देवदुन्दुभयश्चैव प्रावाद्यन्त महास्वनाः ।
विश्वावसुश्च गन्धर्वस्तथा तुंबुरुनारदौ ॥
1.58.m: The drums of the gods, loud-sounding, were beaten; / and the gandharva Viśvāvasu, as well as Tumburu and Nārada,

1.58.s:
hāhāhūhūśca gandharvauṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ śukasaṃbhavam /
tatra śakrapurogāśca lokapālāḥ samāgatāḥ //
1.58.d:
हाहाहूहूश्च गन्धर्वौं तुष्टुवुः शुकसंभवम् ।
तत्र शक्रपुरोगाश्च लोकपालाः समागताः ॥
1.58.m: and the two gandharvas Hāhā and Hūhū praised the birth of Śuka. / The world-guardians, headed by Śakra, gathered there,

1.58.s:
devā devarṣathayaścaṭaiva tathā brahmarṣayo 'pi ca /
divyāni sarvapuṣpāṇi pravavarṣa ca mārutaḥ //
1.58.d:
देवा देवर्षथयश्चटैव तथा ब्रह्मर्षयो ऽपि च ।
दिव्यानि सर्वपुष्पाणि प्रववर्ष च मारुतः ॥
1.58.m: as well as the gods, divine seers, and brahmin seers; / and the wind showered down divine flowers of every kind.

1.58.s:
jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ caiva prahṛṣṭamabhavajjagat /
taṃ mahātmā svayaṃ prītyā devyā saha mahādyutiḥ //
1.58.d:
जङ्गमं स्थावरं चैव प्रहृष्टमभवज्जगत् ।
तं महात्मा स्वयं प्रीत्या देव्या सह महाद्युतिः ॥
1.58.m: The world, both moving and unmoving, was filled with joy. / The great-souled one of great splendor himself lovingly with the goddess

1.58.s:
jātamātraṃ muneḥ putraṃ vidhinopānayattadā /
tasya deveśvaraḥ śakto divyamadbhutadarśanam //
1.58.d:
जातमात्रं मुनेः पुत्रं विधिनोपानयत्तदा ।
तस्य देवेश्वरः शक्तो दिव्यमद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥
1.58.m: then performed the investiture ceremony according to rule for the sage's son as soon as he was born. / Śakra, the powerful lord of the gods, of wonderful appearance,

1.58.s:
dadau kamaṇḍaluṃ prītyā devā vāsāṃsi cābhitaḥ /
haṃsāśca śatapatrāśca sārasāśca sahasraśaḥ //
1.58.d:
ददौ कमण्डलुं प्रीत्या देवा वासांसि चाभितः ।
हंसाश्च शतपत्राश्च सारसाश्च सहस्रशः ॥
1.58.m: affectionately gave him a water-pot, and the gods [gave] garments all around. / And wild geese, woodpeckers, and cranes by the thousands,

1.58.s:
pradakṣiṇamavartanta śukāścāṣāśca nārada /
āraṇe yastadā divyaṃ prāpya janma mahāmuniḥ //
1.58.d:
प्रदक्षिणमवर्तन्त शुकाश्चाषाश्च नारद ।
आरणे यस्तदा दिव्यं प्राप्य जन्म महामुनिः ॥
1.58.m: along with parrots and blue jays, circumambulated him from the left, O Nārada. / Having obtained a divine birth, the great sage, the son of the kindling stick,

1.58.s:
tatraivovāsa medhāvī vratacārī samāhitaḥ /
utpannamātraṃ taṃ vedāḥ sarahasyāḥ sasaṃgrahāḥ //
1.58.d:
तत्रैवोवास मेधावी व्रतचारी समाहितः ।
उत्पन्नमात्रं तं वेदाः सरहस्याः ससंग्रहाः ॥
1.58.m: dwelt right there, wise, observing his vows, and composed. / As soon as he was born, the Vedas, with their esoteric teachings and digests,

1.58.s:
upatasthurmuniśreṣṭhaṃ yathāsya pitaraṃ tathā /
bṛhaspatiṃ sa vavre ca vedavedāṅgabhāṣyavit //
1.58.d:
उपतस्थुर्मुनिश्रेष्ठं यथास्य पितरं तथा ।
बृहस्पतिं स वव्रे च वेदवेदाङ्गभाष्यवित् ॥
1.58.m: attended upon that best of sages, just as upon his father. / Knowing the Vedas, Vedāṅgas, and their commentaries, he chose Bṛhaspati

1.58.s:
upādhyāyaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha dharmamevānucintayan /
so 'dhītya vedānakhilānsarahasyānsasaṃgrahān //
1.58.d:
उपाध्यायं द्विजश्रेष्ठ धर्ममेवानुचिन्तयन् ।
सो ऽधीत्य वेदानखिलान्सरहस्यान्ससंग्रहान् ॥
1.58.m: as his preceptor, O best of twice-born, contemplating duty alone. / Having studied all the Vedas with their esoteric teachings and digests,

1.58.s:
itihāsaṃ ca kārtsnyena vedaśāstrāṇi cābhitaḥ /
gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā samāvṛtto mahāmuniḥ //
1.58.d:
इतिहासं च कार्त्स्न्येन वेदशास्त्राणि चाभितः ।
गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा समावृत्तो महामुनिः ॥
1.58.m: and the epics entirely, and the Vedic scriptures thoroughly, / the great sage gave a fee to his teacher and completed his studies.

1.58.s:
ugraṃ tapaḥ samārebhe brahmacārī samāhitāḥ /
devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca bālye 'pi sumahātapāḥ //
1.58.d:
उग्रं तपः समारेभे ब्रह्मचारी समाहिताः ।
देवतानामृषीणां च बाल्ये ऽपि सुमहातपाः ॥
1.58.m: A student of the Veda and composed, he undertook severe austerity; / even in his childhood he was of exceedingly great austerity among gods and seers,

1.58.s:
saṃmatraṇīyo janyaśca jñānena tapasā tathā /
na tvasya ramate buddhi rāśrameṣu munīśvara //
1.58.d:
संमत्रणीयो जन्यश्च ज्ञानेन तपसा तथा ।
न त्वस्य रमते बुद्धि राश्रमेषु मुनीश्वर ॥
1.58.m: worthy of consultation and esteemed for his knowledge and austerity. / But his mind found no pleasure, O lord of sages, in the [other] stages of life,

1.58.s:
triṣu gārhasthyamūleṣu mokṣadharmānudarśinaḥ /
sa mokṣamanucintyaiva śukaḥ pitaramabhyagāt //
1.58.d:
त्रिषु गार्हस्थ्यमूलेषु मोक्षधर्मानुदर्शिनः ।
स मोक्षमनुचिन्त्यैव शुकः पितरमभ्यगात् ॥
1.58.m: the three rooted in the householder's life, since he contemplated the duties of liberation. / Reflecting only on liberation, Śuka went to his father.

1.58.s:
prāhābhivādya ca tadā śreyor'thī vinayānvitaḥ /
mokṣadharmeṣu kuśalo bhagavān prabravītu me //
1.58.d:
प्राहाभिवाद्य च तदा श्रेयोर्ऽथी विनयान्वितः ।
मोक्षधर्मेषु कुशलो भगवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे ॥
1.58.m: Then, having greeted him, seeking the highest good and endowed with modesty, he said: / 'Skilled in the duties of liberation, may the blessed one instruct me,

1.58.s:
yathaiva manasaḥ śāntiḥ paramā saṃbhavenmune /
śṛtvā putrasya vacanaṃ paramarṣiruvāca tam //
1.58.d:
यथैव मनसः शान्तिः परमा संभवेन्मुने ।
शृत्वा पुत्रस्य वचनं परमर्षिरुवाच तम् ॥
1.58.m: so that supreme peace of mind may come to be, O sage.' / Hearing the words of his son, the supreme seer said to him:

1.58.s:
adhīṣva mokṣaśāstraṃ vai dharmāṃśca vividhānapi /
piturnideśājjagrāha śuko brahmavidāṃ varaḥ //
1.58.d:
अधीष्व मोक्षशास्त्रं वै धर्मांश्च विविधानपि ।
पितुर्निदेशाज्जग्राह शुको ब्रह्मविदां वरः ॥
1.58.m: 'Study the treatise on liberation and the various duties.' / At his father's command, Śuka, the best of knowers of Brahman, mastered

1.58.s:
yogaśāstraṃ ca nikhilaṃ kāpilaṃ caiva nārada /
śataṃ brāhmyā śriyā yuktaṃ brahmatulyaparākramam //
1.58.d:
योगशास्त्रं च निखिलं कापिलं चैव नारद ।
शतं ब्राह्म्या श्रिया युक्तं ब्रह्मतुल्यपराक्रमम् ॥
1.58.m: the treatise on Yoga entirely, and the Sāṃkhya of Kapila as well, O Nārada. / Endowed with Brahmanical splendor, equal in prowess to Brahman,

1.58.s:
mene putraṃ yathā vyāso mokṣaśāstraviśāradam /
uvāca gaccheti tadā janakaṃ mithileśvaram //
1.58.d:
मेने पुत्रं यथा व्यासो मोक्षशास्त्रविशारदम् ।
उवाच गच्छेति तदा जनकं मिथिलेश्वरम् ॥
1.58.m: when Vyāsa considered his son expert in the treatise on liberation, / he then said to him: 'Go to Janaka, the ruler of Mithilā.

1.58.s:
sa te vakṣyati mokṣārthaṃ nikhilena narādhipaḥ /
piturniyogādagamajjanakaṃ methakhilaṃ nṛpam //
1.58.d:
स ते वक्ष्यति मोक्षार्थं निखिलेन नराधिपः ।
पितुर्नियोगादगमज्जनकं मेथखिलं नृपम् ॥
1.58.m: That lord of men will explain the meaning of liberation to you in its entirety.' / At his father's instruction, he went to King Janaka, the king of Mithilā,

1.58.s:
praṣṭuṃ dharmasya niṣṭāṃ vai mokṣasya ca parāyaṇam /
uktaśca mānuṣeṇa tvaṃ tathā gacchetyavismitaḥ //
1.58.d:
प्रष्टुं धर्मस्य निष्टां वै मोक्षस्य च परायणम् ।
उक्तश्च मानुषेण त्वं तथा गच्छेत्यविस्मितः ॥
1.58.m: to ask about the culmination of duty and the highest goal of liberation. / And he was instructed: 'Go there as a mortal, unastonished.

1.58.s:
na prabhāveṇa gantavyamantarikṣacareṇa vai /
ārjavenaiva gantavyaṃ na sukhāya kṣaṇāttvayā //
1.58.d:
न प्रभावेण गन्तव्यमन्तरिक्षचरेण वै ।
आर्जवेनैव गन्तव्यं न सुखाय क्षणात्त्वया ॥
1.58.m: You must not go by supernatural power, moving through the sky; / you must go straightforwardly, not for your own pleasure, in a moment.

1.58.s:
na draṣṭavyā viśeṣā hi viśeṣā hi prasaṃginaḥ /
ahṝṅkāro na kartavyo yājye tasminnarādhipe //
1.58.d:
न द्रष्टव्या विशेषा हि विशेषा हि प्रसंगिनः ।
अहॄङ्कारो न कर्तव्यो याज्ये तस्मिन्नराधिपे ॥
1.58.m: Special distinctions are not to be sought, for distinctions cause attachment; / egotism must not be displayed toward that king, who is worthy of your sacrifice.

1.58.s:
sthātavyaṃ vasathe tasya sa te chetsyati saṃśayam /
sa dharmakuśalo rājā mokṣaśāstraviśāradaḥ //
1.58.d:
स्थातव्यं वसथे तस्य स ते छेत्स्यति संशयम् ।
स धर्मकुशलो राजा मोक्षशास्त्रविशारदः ॥
1.58.m: You must stay in his dwelling; he will resolve your doubt. / That king is skilled in duty and expert in the treatise on liberation.

1.58.s:
yathā yathā ca te brūyāttatkāryamaviśaṅkayā /
evamuktaḥ sa dharmātmā jagāma mithilāṃ muniḥ //
1.58.d:
यथा यथा च ते ब्रूयात्तत्कार्यमविशङ्कया ।
एवमुक्तः स धर्मात्मा जगाम मिथिलां मुनिः ॥
1.58.m: Whatever he tells you, that must be done without hesitation.' / Addressed thus, the righteous sage set out for Mithilā.

1.58.s:
pabhdyāṃ śaktontarikṣeṇa krāntuṃ bhūmiṃ sasāgarām /
sagirīṃ ścāpyatikramya bhārataṃ varṣamāsadat //
1.58.d:
पभ्द्यां शक्तोन्तरिक्षेण क्रान्तुं भूमिं ससागराम् ।
सगिरीं श्चाप्यतिक्रम्य भारतं वर्षमासदत् ॥
1.58.m: Though capable of traversing the earth with its oceans by sky, he went on foot; / and crossing the mountains, he reached the land of Bhārata.

1.58.s:
sa deśānvividhānsphītānatikramya mahāmuniḥ /
videhānvai samāsādya janakena samāgamat //
1.58.d:
स देशान्विविधान्स्फीतानतिक्रम्य महामुनिः ।
विदेहान्वै समासाद्य जनकेन समागमत् ॥
1.58.m: Crossing various prosperous regions, the great sage / reached the Videhas and met with Janaka.

1.58.s:
rājadvāraṃ samāsādya dvārapālairnivāritaḥ //ṭa
tasthau tatra mahāyogī kṣutpipāsādivarjitaḥ //
1.58.d:
राजद्वारं समासाद्य द्वारपालैर्निवारितः ॥ट
तस्थौ तत्र महायोगी क्षुत्पिपासादिवर्जितः ॥
1.58.m: Having arrived at the royal gate and being stopped by the gatekeepers, / the great yogin stood there, free from hunger, thirst, and the like,

1.58.s:
ātape glānirahito dhyānayuktaśca nārada /
teṣāṃ tu dvārapālānāmekastatra vyavasthitaḥ //
1.58.d:
आतपे ग्लानिरहितो ध्यानयुक्तश्च नारद ।
तेषां तु द्वारपालानामेकस्तत्र व्यवस्थितः ॥
1.58.m: unwearied in the heat and engaged in meditation, O Nārada. / But one of those gatekeepers stationed there,

1.58.s:
madhyaṅgatamivādityaṃ dṛṣṭvā śukamavasthitam /
jūjayitvā yathānyāyamabhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ //
1.58.d:
मध्यङ्गतमिवादित्यं दृष्ट्वा शुकमवस्थितम् ।
जूजयित्वा यथान्यायमभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः ॥
1.58.m: seeing Śuka standing like the midday sun, / worshipped him according to rule, bowed to him with folded hands,

1.58.s:
prāveśayattataḥ kakṣaāṃ dvitīyāṃ rājaveśmanaḥ /
tatrāntaḥpurasaṃbaddhaṃ mahaccaitragthopamam //
1.58.d:
प्रावेशयत्ततः कक्षआं द्वितीयां राजवेश्मनः ।
तत्रान्तःपुरसंबद्धं महच्चैत्रग्थोपमम् ॥
1.58.m: and then ushered him into the second courtyard of the royal palace. / There, connected to the inner quarters and resembling the great Caitraratha grove,

1.58.s:
suvibhaktajalākrīḍaṃ ramyaṃ puṣpitapādapam /
darśayitvāsane sthāpya rājānaṃ ca vyajijñapat //
1.58.d:
सुविभक्तजलाक्रीडं रम्यं पुष्पितपादपम् ।
दर्शयित्वासने स्थाप्य राजानं च व्यजिज्ञपत् ॥
1.58.m: charming, with well-divided pleasure-gardens and flowering trees, / having shown it to him and placed him on a seat, he informed the king.

1.58.s:
śrutvā rājā śukaṃ prāptaṃ vārastrīḥ sa nyayuṅkta ca /
sevāyai tasya bhāvasya jñānāya munisatama //
1.58.d:
श्रुत्वा राजा शुकं प्राप्तं वारस्त्रीः स न्ययुङ्क्त च ।
सेवायै तस्य भावस्य ज्ञानाय मुनिसतम ॥
1.58.m: Hearing that Śuka had arrived, the king appointed courtesans / to serve him and to test his disposition, O best of sages.

1.58.s:
taṃ cārukeśyaḥ śuśreṇyastaruṇyaḥ priyadarśanāḥ /
sūkṣmaraktāṃbaradharāstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ //
1.58.d:
तं चारुकेश्यः शुश्रेण्यस्तरुण्यः प्रियदर्शनाः ।
सूक्ष्मरक्तांबरधरास्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः ॥
1.58.m: Those youthful women of lovely hair, fair hips, and pleasing appearance, / wearing fine red garments and ornaments of refined gold,

1.58.s:
saṃlāpālāpakuśālā bhāvajñāḥ sarvakovidāḥ /
paraṃ pañcāśatastasya pādyādīni vyakalpayan //
1.58.d:
संलापालापकुशाला भावज्ञाः सर्वकोविदाः ।
परं पञ्चाशतस्तस्य पाद्यादीनि व्यकल्पयन् ॥
1.58.m: skilled in conversation and witty talk, knowing intentions, and adept in all things, / fifty in number, provided him with water for the feet and other rites.

1.58.s:
deśa kālopapannena sādhvannenāpyatarpayan /
tasya bhuktavatastāta tāstataḥ purakānanam //
1.58.d:
देश कालोपपन्नेन साध्वन्नेनाप्यतर्पयन् ।
तस्य भुक्तवतस्तात तास्ततः पुरकाननम् ॥
1.58.m: They also satisfied him with wholesome food suited to the place and time. / When he had eaten, dear one, they then showed him the city grove,

1.58.s:
suramyaṃ darśayāmāsurekaikatvena nārada /
krīḍantyaśca hasaṃtyaśca gāyantyaścaiva tāḥ śukam //
1.58.d:
सुरम्यं दर्शयामासुरेकैकत्वेन नारद ।
क्रीडन्त्यश्च हसंत्यश्च गायन्त्यश्चैव ताः शुकम् ॥
1.58.m: very delightful, one part at a time, O Nārada, / playing, laughing, and singing around Śuka.

1.58.s:
udārasatvaṃ satvajñāḥsarvāḥ paryyacaraṃstadā /
āraṇeyastu śuddhātmā jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ //
1.58.d:
उदारसत्वं सत्वज्ञाःसर्वाः पर्य्यचरंस्तदा ।
आरणेयस्तु शुद्धात्मा जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.58.m: Knowing his nature, they all waited upon that noble-minded one. / But the son of the kindling stick, pure of mind, with anger conquered and senses controlled,

1.58.s:
dhyānastha eva satataṃ na hṛṣyati na kupyati /
pādaśaucaṃ tu kṛtvā vai śukaḥ saṃdhyāmupāsya ca //
1.58.d:
ध्यानस्थ एव सततं न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ।
पादशौचं तु कृत्वा वै शुकः संध्यामुपास्य च ॥
1.58.m: remained constantly in meditation, neither rejoicing nor growing angry. / Having washed his feet and performed the twilight devotion, Śuka

1.58.s:
niṣasādāsane puṇye tamevārthaṃ vyacintayat /
pūrvarātre tu tatrāsau bhūtvā dhyānaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.58.d:
निषसादासने पुण्ये तमेवार्थं व्यचिन्तयत् ।
पूर्वरात्रे तु तत्रासौ भूत्वा ध्यानपरायणः ॥
1.58.m: sat down on a sacred seat and reflected upon that very purpose. / Devoted to meditation there during the early part of the night,

1.58.s:
madhyarātre yathānyāyyaṃ nidrāmāhārayatprabhuḥ /
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya kṛtvā śaucamanantaram //
1.58.d:
मध्यरात्रे यथान्याय्यं निद्रामाहारयत्प्रभुः ।
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय कृत्वा शौचमनन्तरम् ॥
1.58.m: At midnight, according to rule, the master took his sleep. / Then, having risen in the morning and performed purification thereafter,

1.58.s:
strībhiḥ parivṛtto dhīmāndhyānamevānvapadyata /
anena vidhinā tatra tadahaḥśeṣamapyuta //
1.58.d:
स्त्रीभिः परिवृत्तो धीमान्ध्यानमेवान्वपद्यत ।
अनेन विधिना तत्र तदहःशेषमप्युत ॥
1.58.m: the wise one, though surrounded by women, entered into meditation alone. / In this manner, [he spent] the rest of that day,

1.58.s:
tāṃ ca rātriṃ nṛpakule vartayāmāsa nārada //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyabhāge śukapralobhanaṃ nāmāṣṭañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.58.d:
तां च रात्रिं नृपकुले वर्तयामास नारद ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयभागे शुकप्रलोभनं नामाष्टञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.58.m:
and that night, O Nārada, he dwelt in the king’s palace.

Thus ends the fifty-eighth chapter, named ‘The Temptation of Śuka’, in the Second Part of the Great Narrative in the First Section of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.59.s:
sanandana uvāca
tataḥ sa rājā sahito mantribhirdvijasattama /
puraḥ purohitaṃ kṛtvā sarvāṇyantaḥ purāṇi ca //
1.59.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
ततः स राजा सहितो मन्त्रिभिर्द्विजसत्तम ।
पुरः पुरोहितं कृत्वा सर्वाण्यन्तः पुराणि च ॥
1.59.m: Sanandana said: / Then the king, accompanied by his ministers, O best of the twice-born, / putting his family priest in front, as well as his entire inner royal household,

1.59.s:
śirasā cārdhyamādāya guruputraṃ samabhyagāt /
mahadāsanamādāya sarvaratnavibhūṣitam //
1.59.d:
शिरसा चार्ध्यमादाय गुरुपुत्रं समभ्यगात् ।
महदासनमादाय सर्वरत्नविभूषितम् ॥
1.59.m: and carrying an offering of respect with his head [bent], approached the guru’s son. / Taking a large seat adorned with every kind of gem,

1.59.s:
pradadau guruputrāya śukāya paramocitam /
tatropaviṣṭaṃ taṃ kārṣṇiśāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā //
1.59.d:
प्रददौ गुरुपुत्राय शुकाय परमोचितम् ।
तत्रोपविष्टं तं कार्ष्णिशास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥
1.59.m: he offered it to the guru’s son, Śuka, as most fitting. / To him who was seated there, the son of Kṛṣṇa [Dvaipāyana], through rites observed in scripture,

1.59.s:
pādyaṃ nivedya prathamaṃ sārghyaṃ gāṃ ca nyavedayat /
sa ca tāṃmantrataḥ pūjāṃ pratigṛhya dvijottamaḥ //
1.59.d:
पाद्यं निवेद्य प्रथमं सार्घ्यं गां च न्यवेदयत् ।
स च तांमन्त्रतः पूजां प्रतिगृह्य द्विजोत्तमः ॥
1.59.m: he first presented water for washing the feet, along with the offering of respect, and presented a cow. / And having received that worship according to mantra, that best of the twice-born

1.59.s:
paryapṛcchanmahātejārājñaḥ kuśalamavyayam /
udārasattvābhijano rājāpi gurusūnave //
1.59.d:
पर्यपृच्छन्महातेजाराज्ञः कुशलमव्ययम् ।
उदारसत्त्वाभिजनो राजापि गुरुसूनवे ॥
1.59.m: inquired after the king’s imperishable welfare, he of great splendour. / The king too, of noble nature and descent, having reported his welfare

1.59.s:
āvedya kuśalaṃ bhūmau niṣasāda tadājñayā /
so 'pi vaiyāsakiṃ bhūyaḥ pṛṣṭvā kuśalamavyayam /
kimāgamanimityeva paryapṛcchadvidhānavit //
1.59.d:
आवेद्य कुशलं भूमौ निषसाद तदाज्ञया ।
सो ऽपि वैयासकिं भूयः पृष्ट्वा कुशलमव्ययम् ।
किमागमनिमित्येव पर्यपृच्छद्विधानवित् ॥
1.59.m: to the guru’s son, sat down on the ground at his command. / Having in turn inquired after the imperishable welfare of the son of Vyāsa, / knowing proper conduct, he asked: 'For what purpose have you come?'

1.59.s:
śuka uvāca
pitrāhamukto bhadraṃ te mokṣadharmārthakovidaḥ /
videharājohyādyome janako nāma viśrutaḥ //
1.59.d:
शुक उवाच
पित्राहमुक्तो भद्रं ते मोक्षधर्मार्थकोविदः ।
विदेहराजोह्याद्योमे जनको नाम विश्रुतः ॥
1.59.m: Śuka said: / 'I was told by my father—may you prosper—who is skilled in the purpose of the duty of liberation: / "There is a king of Videha, famous by the name of Janaka, chief among the wise.

1.59.s:
tatra tvaṃ gaccha tūrṇaṃ vai sa te hṛdayasaṃśayam /
pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca sarvaṃ chetsyatyasaṃśayam //
1.59.d:
तत्र त्वं गच्छ तूर्णं वै स ते हृदयसंशयम् ।
प्रवृत्तौ च निवृत्तौ च सर्वं छेत्स्यत्यसंशयम् ॥
1.59.m: Go there swiftly; indeed, he will cut through the doubt in your heart / regarding both worldly involvement and detachment; entirely, beyond doubt."

1.59.s:
so 'haṃ piturniyogāttvā mupapraṣṭumihāgataḥ /
tanme dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha yathāvadvaktumarhasi //
1.59.d:
सो ऽहं पितुर्नियोगात्त्वा मुपप्रष्टुमिहागतः ।
तन्मे धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.59.m: So, by my father's command, I have come here to inquire of you. / Therefore, O best among upholders of duty, you ought to tell me truly:

1.59.s:
kiṃ kāryaṃ brāhmaṇeneha mokṣārthaśca kimātmakaḥ /
kathaṃ ca mokṣaḥ kartavyo jñānena tapasāpi vā //
1.59.d:
किं कार्यं ब्राह्मणेनेह मोक्षार्थश्च किमात्मकः ।
कथं च मोक्षः कर्तव्यो ज्ञानेन तपसापि वा ॥
1.59.m: What must be done by a brāhmaṇa here, and of what nature is the purpose of liberation? / And how is liberation to be attained—by knowledge or by austerity?'

1.59.s:
janaka uvāca
yatkāryaṃ brāhmaṇeneha janmaprabhṛti tacchuṇu /
kṛtopanayanastāta bhavedvedaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.59.d:
जनक उवाच
यत्कार्यं ब्राह्मणेनेह जन्मप्रभृति तच्छुणु ।
कृतोपनयनस्तात भवेद्वेदपरायणः ॥
1.59.m: Janaka said: / 'Listen to what must be done by a brāhmaṇa here from his birth onward: / Having received the sacred initiation, dear boy, he should be devoted to the Veda,

1.59.s:
tapasā guruvṛttyā ca brahmacaryeṇa cānvitaḥ /
devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca hyatṛṣṇaścānasūyakaḥ //
1.59.d:
तपसा गुरुवृत्त्या च ब्रह्मचर्येण चान्वितः ।
देवतानां पितॄणां च ह्यतृष्णश्चानसूयकः ॥
1.59.m: endowed with austerity, service to the guru, and student-chastity, / free from longing regarding gods and ancestors, and ungrudging.

1.59.s:
vedānadhītya niyato dakṣiṇāmapavartya ca /
abhyanujñāmanuprāpya samāvarteta vai dvijaḥ //
1.59.d:
वेदानधीत्य नियतो दक्षिणामपवर्त्य च ।
अभ्यनुज्ञामनुप्राप्य समावर्तेत वै द्विजः ॥
1.59.m: Having studied the Vedas, self-restrained, and having presented the sacrificial fee, / having obtained permission, the twice-born should perform the return-home ceremony.

1.59.s:
samāvṛttastu gārhasthye sadāro niyato vaset /
anasūyuryathānyāyamāhitāgniranādṛte //
1.59.d:
समावृत्तस्तु गार्हस्थ्ये सदारो नियतो वसेत् ।
अनसूयुर्यथान्यायमाहिताग्निरनादृते ॥
1.59.m: Having returned home, he should live self-restrained in householdership with a wife, / free from malice, keeping the sacred fires according to rule, without disrespect.

1.59.s:
utpādya putrapautrāṃśca vanyāśramapade vaset /
tānevāgnīnyathānyāyaṃ pūjayannatithipriyaḥ //
1.59.d:
उत्पाद्य पुत्रपौत्रांश्च वन्याश्रमपदे वसेत् ।
तानेवाग्नीन्यथान्यायं पूजयन्नतिथिप्रियः ॥
1.59.m: Having fathered sons and grandsons, he should dwell in the forest hermitage, / revering those same sacred fires according to rule, fond of guests.

1.59.s:
sarvānagnīnyathānyāyamātmanyāropya dharmavit /
nirdvandvo vītarāgātmā brahmāśramapade vaset //
1.59.d:
सर्वानग्नीन्यथान्यायमात्मन्यारोप्य धर्मवित् ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो वीतरागात्मा ब्रह्माश्रमपदे वसेत् ॥
1.59.m: Assigning all fires into himself according to rule, knower of duty, / free from the dualities, his mind free of passion, he should dwell in the station of the Brahman-stage.'

1.59.s:
śuka uvāca
utpanne jñānavijñāne pratyakṣe hṛdi śaśvate /
na vinā gurusaṃvāsājjñānasyādhigamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.59.d:
शुक उवाच
उत्पन्ने ज्ञानविज्ञाने प्रत्यक्षे हृदि शश्वते ।
न विना गुरुसंवासाज्ज्ञानस्याधिगमः स्मृतः ॥
1.59.m: Śuka said: / 'When direct and eternal knowledge and higher insight have arisen in the heart, / [since] the attainment of knowledge is recorded as not happening without residing with a guru,

1.59.s:
kimavaśyaṃ tu vastavyamāśrameṣu na vā nṛpa /
etadbhavantaṃ pṛcchāmi tadbhavānvaktumarhati //
1.59.d:
किमवश्यं तु वस्तव्यमाश्रमेषु न वा नृप ।
एतद्भवन्तं पृच्छामि तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
1.59.m: must one necessarily reside in the [successive] stages of life, or not, O king? / This I ask you; you ought to tell it to me.'

1.59.s:
janaka uvāca
na vinā jñānavijñāne mokṣasyādhigamo bhavet /.
na vinā gurusaṃbadhājjñānasyādhigamastathā //
1.59.d:
जनक उवाच
न विना ज्ञानविज्ञाने मोक्षस्याधिगमो भवेत् ॥
न विना गुरुसंबधाज्ज्ञानस्याधिगमस्तथा ॥
1.59.m: Janaka said: / 'Without knowledge and higher insight, the attainment of liberation cannot occur; / likewise, without connection to a guru, the attainment of knowledge cannot occur.

1.59.s:
ācāryaḥ plāvitā tasya jñānaṃ plava ihocyate /
vijñāya kṛtakṛtyastu tīrṇastatrobhayaṃ tyajet //
1.59.d:
आचार्यः प्लाविता तस्य ज्ञानं प्लव इहोच्यते ।
विज्ञाय कृतकृत्यस्तु तीर्णस्तत्रोभयं त्यजेत् ॥
1.59.m: The teacher is the ferryman; knowledge is called the raft here. / Having known, having achieved his purpose, having crossed over, he should abandon both.

1.59.s:
anucchedāya lokānāmanucchedāya karmaṇām /
kṛtvā śubhāśubhaṃ karma mokṣo nāmeha labhyate //
1.59.d:
अनुच्छेदाय लोकानामनुच्छेदाय कर्मणाम् ।
कृत्वा शुभाशुभं कर्म मोक्षो नामेह लभ्यते ॥
1.59.m: For the non-destruction of the worlds, for the non-destruction of actions, / having performed good and evil deeds, liberation, as it is called, is attained here.

1.59.s:
bhāvitaiḥ kāraṇaiścāryaṃ bahusaṃsārayoniṣu /
āsādayati śuddhātmā mokṣaṃ hi prathamāśrame //
1.59.d:
भावितैः कारणैश्चार्यं बहुसंसारयोनिषु ।
आसादयति शुद्धात्मा मोक्षं हि प्रथमाश्रमे ॥
1.59.m: Yet cultivated by [past] causes, O noble one, in many transmigratory wombs, / a pure-minded one attains liberation even in the first stage of life.

1.59.s:
tamāsādya tu muktasya dṛṣṭārthasya vipaścitaḥ /
tridhāśrameṣu konvartho bhavetparamabhīpsataḥ //
1.59.d:
तमासाद्य तु मुक्तस्य दृष्टार्थस्य विपश्चितः ।
त्रिधाश्रमेषु कोन्वर्थो भवेत्परमभीप्सतः ॥
1.59.m: Having attained that, for one who is liberated, who has perceived the goal, who is wise, / what purpose would there be in the three [other] stages of life, when he desires the supreme?

1.59.s:
rājasāṃstāmasāṃścaiva nityaṃ doṣānvisarjayeta /
sāttvikaṃ mārgamāsthāya paśyedātmānamātmanā //
1.59.d:
राजसांस्तामसांश्चैव नित्यं दोषान्विसर्जयेत ।
सात्त्विकं मार्गमास्थाय पश्येदात्मानमात्मना ॥
1.59.m: He should constantly cast away faults arising from passion and darkness; / resorting to the path of purity, he should see the Self by the self.

1.59.s:
sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani /
saṃpaśyannaiva lipyeta jale vāricarago yathā //
1.59.d:
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
संपश्यन्नैव लिप्येत जले वारिचरगो यथा ॥
1.59.m: Seeing the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self, / he is not stained at all, just as an aquatic creature in water.

1.59.s:
pakṣīvatpavanādvardhvamamutrānuntyaśnute /
vihāya dehaṃ nirmukto nirdvandvaḥ śubhasaṃgataḥ //
1.59.d:
पक्षीवत्पवनाद्वर्ध्वममुत्रानुन्त्यश्नुते ।
विहाय देहं निर्मुक्तो निर्द्वन्द्वः शुभसंगतः ॥
1.59.m: Like a bird [soaring] above the wind, he attains infinity in the beyond; / casting off the body, liberated, free from dualities, united with the auspicious.

1.59.s:
atra gāthāḥ purā gītāḥ śṛṇu rājñā yayātinā /
dhāryate yā dvijaistāta mokṣaśāstraviśāradaiḥ //
1.59.d:
अत्र गाथाः पुरा गीताः शृणु राज्ञा ययातिना ।
धार्यते या द्विजैस्तात मोक्षशास्त्रविशारदैः ॥
1.59.m: Here, hear the verses sung in the past by King Yayāti, / which are maintained, dear boy, by twice-born ones skilled in the scriptures of liberation:

1.59.s:
jyotiścātmani nānyatra ratnaṃ tatraiva caiva tat /
svayaṃ ca śakyaṃ taddraṣṭuṃ susamāhitarcatasā //
1.59.d:
ज्योतिश्चात्मनि नान्यत्र रत्नं तत्रैव चैव तत् ।
स्वयं च शक्यं तद्द्रष्टुं सुसमाहितर्चतसा ॥
1.59.m: "The light is in the Self, not elsewhere; and that jewel is right there; / and it can be seen by oneself through a fully concentrated mind.

1.59.s:
na bibheti paro yasmānna bibheti parācca yaḥ /
yaśca necchati na dveṣṭi brahma saṃpadyate sa tu //
1.59.d:
न बिभेति परो यस्मान्न बिभेति पराच्च यः ।
यश्च नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म संपद्यते स तु ॥
1.59.m: From whom another does not fear, and who does not fear another, / and who neither desires nor hates—he attains Brahman.

1.59.s:
yadā bhāvaṃ na kurute sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam /
pūrvairācarito dharmaścaturāśramasaṃjñakaḥ //
1.59.d:
यदा भावं न कुरुते सर्वभूतेषु पापकम् ।
पूर्वैराचरितो धर्मश्चतुराश्रमसंज्ञकः ॥
1.59.m: When he bears no evil disposition toward all beings— / the duty named the four stages of life was practiced by the ancients—

1.59.s:
anena kramayogena bahujātisukarmaṇām /
karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā //
1.59.d:
अनेन क्रमयोगेन बहुजातिसुकर्मणाम् ।
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
1.59.m: through this ordered practice of good deeds across many births, / in action, mind, and speech, he then attains Brahman.

1.59.s:
rsuyojya tapasātmānamīrṣyāmutsṛjya mohinīm /
tyaktva kāmaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca tato brahmatvamaśnute //
1.59.d:
र्सुयोज्य तपसात्मानमीर्ष्यामुत्सृज्य मोहिनीम् ।
त्यक्त्व कामं च लोभं च ततो ब्रह्मत्वमश्नुते ॥
1.59.m: Having united the self with austerity, having abandoned deluding envy, / having cast aside desire and greed, he then attains the state of Brahman.

1.59.s:
yadā śrāvye ca dṛśye ca sarvabhūteṣu cāvyayam /
samo bhavati nirdvudvo brahma saṃpadyate tadā //
1.59.d:
यदा श्राव्ये च दृश्ये च सर्वभूतेषु चाव्ययम् ।
समो भवति निर्द्वुद्वो ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
1.59.m: When toward the heard, the seen, and all beings he is the same, / imperishable, free from dualities, then he attains Brahman.

1.59.s:
yadā stuti ca rnidāṃ ca samatvena ca paśyati /
kāñcanaṃ cāyasaṃ caiva sukhaduḥkhe tathaiva ca //
1.59.d:
यदा स्तुति च र्निदां च समत्वेन च पश्यति ।
काञ्चनं चायसं चैव सुखदुःखे तथैव च ॥
1.59.m: When he looks upon praise and blame with equanimity, / and upon gold and iron, and likewise upon pleasure and pain,

1.59.s:
śītamuṣṇaṃ tathaivārthamanarnthaṃ priyamapriyam /
jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ caiva brahma saṃpadyate tadā //
1.59.d:
शीतमुष्णं तथैवार्थमनर्न्थं प्रियमप्रियम् ।
जीवितं मरणं चैव ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
1.59.m: upon cold and heat, upon gain and loss, the agreeable and the disagreeable, / and upon life and death—then he attains Brahman.

1.59.s:
prasāryeha yathāṅgāni kūrmaḥ saṃharate punaḥ /
tarthedriyāṇi manasā saṃyantavyāni bhikṣuṇā //
1.59.d:
प्रसार्येह यथाङ्गानि कूर्मः संहरते पुनः ।
तर्थेद्रियाणि मनसा संयन्तव्यानि भिक्षुणा ॥
1.59.m: Just as a tortoise, having extended its limbs here, draws them back in, / so the senses must be restrained by the mind by a mendicant.

1.59.s:
tamaḥ parigataṃ veśya yathā dīpena dṛśyate /
tathā buddhipradīpena śakya ātmā nirīkṣitum //
1.59.d:
तमः परिगतं वेश्य यथा दीपेन दृश्यते ।
तथा बुद्धिप्रदीपेन शक्य आत्मा निरीक्षितुम् ॥
1.59.m: Just as a house enveloped in darkness is seen by means of a lamp, / so the Self can be perceived by means of the lamp of the intellect.

1.59.s:
etatsarvaṃ prapaśyāmi tvayi buddhimatāṃvara /
yañcānyadapi vettavyaṃ tattvato vetti tadbhavān //
1.59.d:
एतत्सर्वं प्रपश्यामि त्वयि बुद्धिमतांवर ।
यञ्चान्यदपि वेत्तव्यं तत्त्वतो वेत्ति तद्भवान् ॥
1.59.m: All this I see in you, O best of the wise! / And whatever else is to be known, you know it in truth.

1.59.s:
brahmarṣe viditaśvāsi viṣayāntamupāgataḥ /
guroścaiva prasādena tava caivopaśikṣayā //
1.59.d:
ब्रह्मर्षे विदितश्वासि विषयान्तमुपागतः ।
गुरोश्चैव प्रसादेन तव चैवोपशिक्षया ॥
1.59.m: O seer among brāhmaṇas, you are known to me as having reached the end of the objects of sense, / both by the grace of your guru and by your own instruction.

1.59.s:
tasya caiva prasādena prādurbhūtaṃ mahāmuneḥ /
jñānaṃ divyaṃ samādīptaṃ tenāsi vidito vidito mama //
1.59.d:
तस्य चैव प्रसादेन प्रादुर्भूतं महामुनेः ।
ज्ञानं दिव्यं समादीप्तं तेनासि विदितो विदितो मम ॥
1.59.m: By the grace of that great sage, / divine, blazing knowledge has appeared [in you]; by that, you are known to me.

1.59.s:
ardhikaṃ tava vijñānamadhi kāvagatistava /
adhikaṃ ca tavaiśvaryaṃ tañca tvaṃ nāvabudhyase //
1.59.d:
अर्धिकं तव विज्ञानमधि कावगतिस्तव ।
अधिकं च तवैश्वर्यं तञ्च त्वं नावबुध्यसे ॥
1.59.m: Superior is your higher insight, superior is your comprehension, / and superior is your spiritual mastery, yet you do not recognize it.

1.59.s:
bālyādvā saṃśayādvāpi bhayādvāpi vimeṣajāt /
utpanne cāpi vijñā ne nādhigacchanti tāṅgatim //
1.59.d:
बाल्याद्वा संशयाद्वापि भयाद्वापि विमेषजात् ।
उत्पन्ने चापि विज्ञा ने नाधिगच्छन्ति ताङ्गतिम् ॥
1.59.m: Whether from childishness, from doubt, or from fear arising from hesitation, / even though higher insight has arisen, people do not reach that goal.

1.59.s:
vyavasāyena śuddhena madvidhaiśchinnasaṃśayāḥ /
vimucya hṛdayagranthīnārtimāsādayanti tām //
1.59.d:
व्यवसायेन शुद्धेन मद्विधैश्छिन्नसंशयाः ।
विमुच्य हृदयग्रन्थीनार्तिमासादयन्ति ताम् ॥
1.59.m: Those whose doubts have been severed by those like me with pure resolve, / releasing the knots of the heart, attain that [state free from] distress.'

1.59.s:
mavāṃścotpannavijñānaḥ sthirabaguddhiralolupaḥ /
vyavasāyādṛte brahmannāsādayati tatpadam //
1.59.d:
मवांश्चोत्पन्नविज्ञानः स्थिरबगुद्धिरलोलुपः ।
व्यवसायादृते ब्रह्मन्नासादयति तत्पदम् ॥
1.59.m:
And you, endowed with knowledge, firm-minded and free from greed,
attain that state, O brāhmaṇa, through firm resolve."

1.59.s:
nāsti te sukhaduḥkheṣu viśeṣo nāsti vastuṣu /
nautsukyaṃ nṛtyagīteṣu na rāga upajāyate //
1.59.d:
नास्ति ते सुखदुःखेषु विशेषो नास्ति वस्तुषु ।
नौत्सुक्यं नृत्यगीतेषु न राग उपजायते ॥
1.59.m:
"You have no distinction between pleasure and pain, none regarding objects;
there is no yearning for dancing and singing, nor does passion arise [in you].

1.59.s:
na bandhuṣu nibandhaste na bhayeṣvasti te bhayam /
paśyāmitvāṃ mahābhāga tulyanindātmasaṃstutim //
1.59.d:
न बन्धुषु निबन्धस्ते न भयेष्वस्ति ते भयम् ।
पश्यामित्वां महाभाग तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिम् ॥
1.59.m:
You have no attachment to relatives, nor do you fear amidst fears;
I see you, O fortunate one, treating blame and praise of yourself as equal.

1.59.s:
ahaṃ ca tvānupaśyāmi ye cānye 'pi manīṣiṇaḥ /
āsthitaṃ paramaṃ mārge akṣayaṃ cāpyanāmayam //
1.59.d:
अहं च त्वानुपश्यामि ये चान्ये ऽपि मनीषिणः ।
आस्थितं परमं मार्गे अक्षयं चाप्यनामयम् ॥
1.59.m:
I see you, and so do other wise men,
established on the supreme, imperishable, and sorrowless path.

1.59.s:
yatphalaṃ brāhmaṇasyeha mokṣārthaścāpadātmakaḥ /
tasminvai vartase viprakimanyatparipṛcchasi //
1.59.d:
यत्फलं ब्राह्मणस्येह मोक्षार्थश्चापदात्मकः ।
तस्मिन्वै वर्तसे विप्रकिमन्यत्परिपृच्छसि ॥
1.59.m:
The goal of a brāhmaṇa in this world, which is liberation free from calamity—
in that very [state] you abide, O vipra. What else do you ask?"

1.59.s:
sanandana uvāca
etacchutvā tu vacanaṃ katātmā kṛtaniścayaḥ /
ātmanātmānamāsthāya dṛṣṭvā cātmānamātmanā //
1.59.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
एतच्छुत्वा तु वचनं कतात्मा कृतनिश्चयः ।
आत्मनात्मानमास्थाय दृष्ट्वा चात्मानमात्मना ॥
1.59.m:
Sanandana said:
Having heard this speech, his purpose accomplished, his resolve made,
relying on the Self through the self, and seeing the Self by the self,

1.59.s:
kṛtakāryaḥ sukhī śāntastūṣṇīṃ prāyādudaṅmukhaḥ /
śaiśiraṃ girimāsādya pārāśaryaṃ dadarśa ca //
1.59.d:
कृतकार्यः सुखी शान्तस्तूष्णीं प्रायादुदङ्मुखः ।
शैशिरं गिरिमासाद्य पाराशर्यं ददर्श च ॥
1.59.m:
successful, happy, peaceful, and silent, he went northward;
having reached the cold mountain, he saw the son of Parāśara,

1.59.s:
śiṣyānadhyāpayantaṃ ca pailādīnvedasaṃhitāḥ /
ārarṇeyo viśuddhātmā divākarasamaprabhaḥ //
1.59.d:
शिष्यानध्यापयन्तं च पैलादीन्वेदसंहिताः ।
आरर्णेयो विशुद्धात्मा दिवाकरसमप्रभः ॥
1.59.m:
teaching the Vedic Saṃhitās to disciples like Paila and others.
The son of Araṇī, pure in soul, radiant as the sun,

1.59.s:
piturjagrāha pādau caja sādaraṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ /
tato nivedayāmāsa pituḥ sarvamudāradhīḥ //
1.59.d:
पितुर्जग्राह पादौ चज सादरं हृष्टमानसः ।
ततो निवेदयामास पितुः सर्वमुदारधीः ॥
1.59.m:
grasped his father's feet with reverence, his mind delighted;
then the noble-minded [Śuka] reported everything to his father—

1.59.s:
śuko janakarājena saṃvādaṃ mokṣasādhanam /
tacchatvā vedakartāsau prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā //
1.59.d:
शुको जनकराजेन संवादं मोक्षसाधनम् ।
तच्छत्वा वेदकर्तासौ प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना ॥
1.59.m:
Śuka's dialogue with King Janaka, which accomplishes liberation.
Having heard that, the creator of the Vedas, with a heart overjoyed,

1.59.s: samāliṅgya sutaṃ vyāsaḥ svapārśvasthaṃ cakāra ca //
1.59.d: समालिङ्ग्य सुतं व्यासः स्वपार्श्वस्थं चकार च ॥
1.59.m: embraced his son, and Vyāsa made him sit beside him.

1.59.s:
tataḥ pailādayo viprā vedān vyāsādadhītya ca /
śailaśṛṅgādbhuvaṃ prāptā yājanādhyāpane ratāḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne ekonaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.59.d:
ततः पैलादयो विप्रा वेदान् व्यासादधीत्य च ।
शैलशृङ्गाद्भुवं प्राप्ता याजनाध्यापने रताः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने एकोनषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
1.59.m:
Then the vipras, Paila and others, having studied the Vedas from Vyāsa,
descended from the mountain peak to the earth, intent on sacrificing and teaching.

Thus ends the fifty-ninth chapter in the major narrative of the first part in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.60.s:
sanadana uvāca
avatīrṇeṣu vipreṣu yāsaḥ putrasahāyavān /
tūrṣṇīṃ dhyānaparo dhīmānekānte samupāviśat //
1.60.d:
सनदन उवाच
अवतीर्णेषु विप्रेषु यासः पुत्रसहायवान् ।
तूर्ष्णीं ध्यानपरो धीमानेकान्ते समुपाविशत् ॥
1.60.m:
Sanandana said:
When the vipras had departed, Vyāsa, accompanied by his son,
wise and devoted to meditation, sat down in silence in solitude.

1.60.s:
tamuvācāśarī rī vāk vyāsaṃ putrasamanvitam /
bho bho maharṣe bāsiṣṭha brahmaghoṣo na vartate //
1.60.d:
तमुवाचाशरी री वाक् व्यासं पुत्रसमन्वितम् ।
भो भो महर्षे बासिष्ठ ब्रह्मघोषो न वर्तते ॥
1.60.m:
A bodiless voice spoke to Vyāsa, who was with his son:
"O great sage, descendant of Vasiṣṭha! The chanting of Brahman does not proceed.

1.60.s:
eko dhyānaparastūṣṇī kimāḥse cintayanniva /
brahmaghoṣairvirahitaḥ parvato 'yaṃ na śobhate //
1.60.d:
एको ध्यानपरस्तूष्णी किमाःसे चिन्तयन्निव ।
ब्रह्मघोषैर्विरहितः पर्वतो ऽयं न शोभते ॥
1.60.m:
Why do you sit alone, devoted to meditation, silent, as if in contemplation?
Deprived of the chants of Brahman, this mountain does not shine.

1.60.s:
tasmādadhīṣva bhagavansārddha putreṇa dhīmatā /
vedānvedavidā caiva suprasannamanāḥ sadā //
1.60.d:
तस्मादधीष्व भगवन्सार्द्ध पुत्रेण धीमता ।
वेदान्वेदविदा चैव सुप्रसन्नमनाः सदा ॥
1.60.m:
Therefore, study the Vedas, O lord, together with your wise son,
who knows the Vedas, your mind ever exceedingly serene."

1.60.s:
tacchutvā vacanaṃ vyāso nabhovāṇīsamīritam /
śukena saha putreṇa vedābhyāsamathākarot //
1.60.d:
तच्छुत्वा वचनं व्यासो नभोवाणीसमीरितम् ।
शुकेन सह पुत्रेण वेदाभ्यासमथाकरोत् ॥
1.60.m:
Hearing that speech uttered by the celestial voice,
Vyāsa then practiced the Vedas along with his son Śuka.

1.60.s:
tayorabhyasatorevaṃ bahukālaṃ dvijottama /
vāto 'timātraṃ pravavau samudrānilavījitaḥ //
1.60.d:
तयोरभ्यसतोरेवं बहुकालं द्विजोत्तम ।
वातो ऽतिमात्रं प्रववौ समुद्रानिलवीजितः ॥
1.60.m:
As the two were thus practicing for a long time, O best of the twice-born,
a wind blew excessively, fanned by the oceanic air.

1.60.s:
tato 'nadhyāya iti taṃ vyāsaḥ putramavārayat /
śuko vāritamātrastu kautūhalasamanvitaḥ //
1.60.d:
ततो ऽनध्याय इति तं व्यासः पुत्रमवारयत् ।
शुको वारितमात्रस्तु कौतूहलसमन्वितः ॥
1.60.m:
Then Vyāsa stopped his son, saying, 'It is an unpropitious time for study.'
Śuka, having just been stopped, filled with curiosity,

1.60.s:
apṛcchatpitaraṃ tatra kuto vāyurabhūdayam /
ākhyātumarhati bhavānsarvaṃ vāyorvicaiṣṭitam //
1.60.d:
अपृच्छत्पितरं तत्र कुतो वायुरभूदयम् ।
आख्यातुमर्हति भवान्सर्वं वायोर्विचैष्टितम् ॥
1.60.m:
asked his father there: "From where did this wind arise?
You ought to explain to me the entire activity of the wind."

1.60.s:
śukasyaitadvacaḥ śrutvā vyāsaḥ paramavismitaḥ /
anadhyāyanimitta'sminnidaṃ vacanaṃ mabravīt //
1.60.d:
शुकस्यैतद्वचः श्रुत्वा व्यासः परमविस्मितः ।
अनध्यायनिमित्तऽस्मिन्निदं वचनं मब्रवीत् ॥
1.60.m:
Hearing these words of Śuka, Vyāsa was extremely amazed;
on this occasion of non-study, he spoke these words:

1.60.s:
divyaṃ te cakṣurutpannaṃ svasthaṃ te niścalaṃ manaḥ /
tamasā rajasā cāpi tyaktaḥ satye vyavasthitaḥ //
1.60.d:
दिव्यं ते चक्षुरुत्पन्नं स्वस्थं ते निश्चलं मनः ।
तमसा रजसा चापि त्यक्तः सत्ये व्यवस्थितः ॥
1.60.m:
"A divine eye has arisen in you; your mind is poised and unmoving;
you are abandoned by tamas and rajas, and established in sattva.

1.60.s:
tasyātmani svayaṃ vedānbuddhvā samanucintaya /
devayānacaro viṣṇoḥ pitṛyānaśca tāmasaḥ //
1.60.d:
तस्यात्मनि स्वयं वेदान्बुद्ध्वा समनुचिन्तय ।
देवयानचरो विष्णोः पितृयानश्च तामसः ॥
1.60.m:
Contemplate having understood the Vedas directly in the Self:
the path of the gods moving to Viṣṇu, and the path of the ancestors connected to darkness.

1.60.s:
dvāvetau pratyayaṃ yātau divaṃ cādhaśca gacchataḥ /
pithivyāmantarikṣe ca yataḥ saṃyānti vāyavaḥ //
1.60.d:
द्वावेतौ प्रत्ययं यातौ दिवं चाधश्च गच्छतः ।
पिथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे च यतः संयान्ति वायवः ॥
1.60.m:
These two, having attained certainty, go to heaven and below,
where the winds move on earth and in the intermediate space.

1.60.s:
sapta te vāyumārgā vai tānnibodhānupūrvaśaḥ /
tatra devagaṇāḥ sādhyāḥ samabhūvanmahābalāḥ //
1.60.d:
सप्त ते वायुमार्गा वै तान्निबोधानुपूर्वशः ।
तत्र देवगणाः साध्याः समभूवन्महाबलाः ॥
1.60.m:
Those are seven wind-paths; learn them in due order:
There, the Sādhyas, hosts of gods of great strength, came into being.

1.60.s:
teṣāmapyabhavatputraḥ samāno nāma durjayaḥ /
udānastasya putro 'bhūvdyānastasyābhavatsutaḥ //
1.60.d:
तेषामप्यभवत्पुत्रः समानो नाम दुर्जयः ।
उदानस्तस्य पुत्रो ऽभूव्द्यानस्तस्याभवत्सुतः ॥
1.60.m:
They had a son named Samāna, who is invincible;
Udāna was his son, and Vyāna was his son.

1.60.s:
apānaśca tato jajñe prāṇaścāpi tataḥ param /
anapatyo 'bhavatprāṇo durddharṣaḥ śatrumardanaḥ //
1.60.d:
अपानश्च ततो जज्ञे प्राणश्चापि ततः परम् ।
अनपत्यो ऽभवत्प्राणो दुर्द्धर्षः शत्रुमर्दनः ॥
1.60.m:
Apāna was born from him, and Prāṇa thereafter;
Prāṇa remained childless, unassailable, and the crusher of foes.

1.60.s:
pṛtharkkṃmāṇi teṣāṃ tu pravakṣyāmi yathā tathā /
prāṇināṃ sarvato vāyuśceṣṭā vartayate pṛthak //
1.60.d:
पृथर्क्क्ंमाणि तेषां तु प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा तथा ।
प्राणिनां सर्वतो वायुश्चेष्टा वर्तयते पृथक् ॥
1.60.m:
I shall explain their distinct functions just as they are:
the wind everywhere impels the individual movements of living beings.

1.60.s:
prīṇanāñcaiva sarveṣāṃ prāṇa ityabhidhīyate /
preṣayatyabhrasaṃghātāndhūmajāṃścoṣmajāṃstathā //
1.60.d:
प्रीणनाञ्चैव सर्वेषां प्राण इत्यभिधीयते ।
प्रेषयत्यभ्रसंघातान्धूमजांश्चोष्मजांस्तथा ॥
1.60.m:
Because it pleases all, it is called Prāṇa;
it drives the masses of clouds born of smoke and heat.

1.60.s:
prathamaḥ prathame mārge pravaho nāma so 'nilaḥ /
aṃbare snehamātrebhyastaḍidbhyaścottamadyutiḥ //
1.60.d:
प्रथमः प्रथमे मार्गे प्रवहो नाम सो ऽनिलः ।
अंबरे स्नेहमात्रेभ्यस्तडिद्भ्यश्चोत्तमद्युतिः ॥
1.60.m:
The first wind in the first path is named Pravaha;
of excellent luster, [rising] from measures of moisture and lightning in the sky,

1.60.s:
āvaho nāma so 'bhyeti dvitīyaḥ śvasano nadan /
udayaṃ jyotiṣāṃ śaśvatsomādīnāṃ karoti yaḥ //
1.60.d:
आवहो नाम सो ऽभ्येति द्वितीयः श्वसनो नदन् ।
उदयं ज्योतिषां शश्वत्सोमादीनां करोति यः ॥
1.60.m:
the second wind, named Āvaha, arrives roaring,
which constantly causes the rising of the luminaries such as the moon,

1.60.s:
antardeheṣu codānaṃ yaṃ vadanti manīṣiṇaḥ /
yaścaturbhyaḥ samudrebhyo vāyurddhārayate jalam //
1.60.d:
अन्तर्देहेषु चोदानं यं वदन्ति मनीषिणः ।
यश्चतुर्भ्यः समुद्रेभ्यो वायुर्द्धारयते जलम् ॥
1.60.m:
and which the wise call Udāna within bodies.
The wind that sustains water from the four oceans,

1.60.s:
uddhṛtya dadate cāpo jīmūtebhyo vane 'nilaḥ /
yo 'ddhiḥ saṃyojya jīmūtānparjanyāya prayacchatī //
1.60.d:
उद्धृत्य ददते चापो जीमूतेभ्यो वने ऽनिलः ।
यो ऽद्धिः संयोज्य जीमूतान्पर्जन्याय प्रयच्छती ॥
1.60.m:
and lifting it up, gives water to the clouds in the sky,
which, uniting the clouds with waters, presents them to Parjanya,

1.60.s:
udvaho nāma baṃhiṣṭhastṛtīyaḥ sa sadāgatiḥ /
saṃnīyamānā bahudhā yena nīlā mahāghanāḥ //
1.60.d:
उद्वहो नाम बंहिष्ठस्तृतीयः स सदागतिः ।
संनीयमाना बहुधा येन नीला महाघनाः ॥
1.60.m:
is the third wind, exceedingly strong, named Udvaha;
by which the great dark clouds, being gathered together in many ways,

1.60.s:
varṣamokṣakṛtāraṃbhāste bhavanti ghanāghanāḥ /
yo 'sau vahati devānāṃ vimānāni vihāyasā //
1.60.d:
वर्षमोक्षकृतारंभास्ते भवन्ति घनाघनाः ।
यो ऽसौ वहति देवानां विमानानि विहायसा ॥
1.60.m:
become rain-clouds undertaking the discharge of rain;
and that which carries the aerial chariots of the gods through the sky,

1.60.s:
caturthaḥ saṃvaho nāma vāyuḥ sa girimardanaḥ /
yena vegavatā rugṇāḥ kriyante tarujā rasāḥ //
1.60.d:
चतुर्थः संवहो नाम वायुः स गिरिमर्दनः ।
येन वेगवता रुग्णाः क्रियन्ते तरुजा रसाः ॥
1.60.m:
is the fourth wind, named Saṃvaha, the crusher of mountains;
by which, mighty in speed, the saps born of trees are broken.

1.60.s:
pañcamaḥ sa mahāvego vivaho nāma mārutaḥ /
yasminpariplave divyā vahṝntyāpo vihāyasā //
1.60.d:
पञ्चमः स महावेगो विवहो नाम मारुतः ।
यस्मिन्परिप्लवे दिव्या वहॄन्त्यापो विहायसा ॥
1.60.m:
The fifth wind, possessing great speed, is named Vivaha;
in which floating [stream] the celestial waters flow through the sky,

1.60.s:
puṇyaṃ cākāśagaṅgāyāstoyaṃ tiṣṭati tiṣṭati /
dūrātpratihato yasminnekaraśmirdivākaraḥ //
1.60.d:
पुण्यं चाकाशगङ्गायास्तोयं तिष्टति तिष्टति ।
दूरात्प्रतिहतो यस्मिन्नेकरश्मिर्दिवाकरः ॥
1.60.m:
and the sacred water of the celestial Gaṅgā stands continuously;
in which the sun, with single rays repelled from afar,

1.60.s:
yoniraṃśusahasrasya yena yāti vasuṃdharām /
yasmādāpyāyate somo nidhirdivyo 'mṛtasya ca //
1.60.d:
योनिरंशुसहस्रस्य येन याति वसुंधराम् ।
यस्मादाप्यायते सोमो निधिर्दिव्यो ऽमृतस्य च ॥
1.60.m:
the source of a thousand rays, goes to the earth;
from which the moon, the divine treasure of nectar, is nourished.

1.60.s:
ṣaṣṭhaḥ parivaho nāma sa vāyurjīvatāṃ varaḥ /
sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ prāṇārnyo 'takāle nirasyati //
1.60.d:
षष्ठः परिवहो नाम स वायुर्जीवतां वरः ।
सर्वप्राणभृतां प्राणार्न्यो ऽतकाले निरस्यति ॥
1.60.m:
The sixth wind, named Parivaha, is the best among the living;
which casts out the vital breaths of all living beings at the time of death,

1.60.s:
yasya dharme 'nuvartete mṛtyuvevasvatāvubhau /
samyaganvīkṣatā buddhyā śāntayādhyātmanityayā //
1.60.d:
यस्य धर्मे ऽनुवर्तेते मृत्युवेवस्वतावुभौ ।
सम्यगन्वीक्षता बुद्ध्या शान्तयाध्यात्मनित्यया ॥
1.60.m:
in whose law both Death and Vivasvat's son operate;
which, for those who investigate properly with a tranquil intellect, constant in the self,

1.60.s:
dhyānābhyāsābhirāmāṇāṃ yo 'mṛtatvāya kalpate /
yaṃ samāsādya vegena diśāmantaṃ prapedire //
1.60.d:
ध्यानाभ्यासाभिरामाणां यो ऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ।
यं समासाद्य वेगेन दिशामन्तं प्रपेदिरे ॥
1.60.m:
and delighting in the practice of meditation, leads to immortality;
reaching which with speed, the ten thousand sons of Dakṣa Prajāpati

1.60.s:
dakṣasya daśa putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi prajāpateḥ /
yena vṛṣṭyā parābhūtastoyānyena nivartate //
1.60.d:
दक्षस्य दश पुत्राणां सहस्राणि प्रजापतेः ।
येन वृष्ट्या पराभूतस्तोयान्येन निवर्तते ॥
1.60.m:
reached the end of the directions;
by which, defeated by rain, the waters are turned back—

1.60.s:
parīvaho nāma varo vāyuḥ sa duratikramaḥ /
evamete diteḥ putrā marutaḥ paramādbhutāḥ //
1.60.d:
परीवहो नाम वरो वायुः स दुरतिक्रमः ।
एवमेते दितेः पुत्रा मरुतः परमाद्भुताः ॥
1.60.m:
that excellent wind is named Parīvaha, hard to surpass.
Thus these sons of Diti, the Maruts, are extremely marvelous,

1.60.s:
anāramantaḥ sarvāṅgāḥ sarvacāriṇaḥ /
etattu mahadāścaryaṃ yadayaṃ parvatottamaḥ //
1.60.d:
अनारमन्तः सर्वाङ्गाः सर्वचारिणः ।
एतत्तु महदाश्चर्यं यदयं पर्वतोत्तमः ॥
1.60.m:
unresting, possessing all limbs, moving everywhere.
This indeed is a great wonder: that this best of mountains

1.60.s:
kaṃpitaḥ sahasā tena pavamānena vāyunā /
viṣṇorniḥśvāsavāto 'yaṃ yadā vegasamīritaḥ //
1.60.d:
कंपितः सहसा तेन पवमानेन वायुना ।
विष्णोर्निःश्वासवातो ऽयं यदा वेगसमीरितः ॥
1.60.m:
was suddenly shaken by that purifying wind.
When this breath-wind of Viṣṇu, impelled by speed,

1.60.s:
sahasodīryate tāta jagatpravyathate tadā /
tasmādbrahmavido brahma na paṭhantyativāyutaḥ //
1.60.d:
सहसोदीर्यते तात जगत्प्रव्यथते तदा ।
तस्माद्ब्रह्मविदो ब्रह्म न पठन्त्यतिवायुतः ॥
1.60.m:
is suddenly stirred up, O dear one, then the world trembles;
therefore, the knowers of Brahman do not recite the Veda because of excessive wind.

1.60.s:
vāyorvāyubhayaṃ hyuktaṃ brahma tatpīḍitaṃ bhavet /
etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ parāśarasutaḥ prabhuḥ //
1.60.d:
वायोर्वायुभयं ह्युक्तं ब्रह्म तत्पीडितं भवेत् ।
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं पराशरसुतः प्रभुः ॥
1.60.m:
For fear of wind is spoken of regarding the wind; the Veda would be afflicted."
Having spoken these words, the powerful son of Parāśara...

1.60.s:
uktvā putramadhīṣveti vyomagaṅgāmagāttadā /
tato vyāse gate snātuṃ śuko brahmavidāṃ varaḥ //
1.60.d:
उक्त्वा पुत्रमधीष्वेति व्योमगङ्गामगात्तदा ।
ततो व्यासे गते स्नातुं शुको ब्रह्मविदां वरः ॥
1.60.m: Having said to his son, “Study!”, he then went to the heavenly Gaṅgā. / Then, when Vyāsa had gone to bathe, Śuka, the foremost of knowers of Brahman,

1.60.s:
svādhyāyamakarodbrahmanvedavedāṅgapāragaḥ /
tatra svādhyāyasaṃsaktaṃ śukaṃ vyāsasutaṃ mune //
1.60.d:
स्वाध्यायमकरोद्ब्रह्मन्वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ।
तत्र स्वाध्यायसंसक्तं शुकं व्याससुतं मुने ॥
1.60.m: recited his Vedic texts, O brāhmaṇa, having mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. / There, to Śuka, the son of Vyāsa, absorbed in Vedic study, O sage,

1.60.s:
sanatkumāro bhagavānekānte samupāgataḥ /
utthāya satkṛtastena brahmaputro hi kārṣṇinā //
1.60.d:
सनत्कुमारो भगवानेकान्ते समुपागतः ।
उत्थाय सत्कृतस्तेन ब्रह्मपुत्रो हि कार्ष्णिना ॥
1.60.m: the blessed Sanatkumāra approached in solitude. / Rising up, the son of Brahmā was honored by him, the son of Kṛṣṇa [Dvaipāyana].

1.60.s:
tataḥ provāca viprendra śukaṃ vidāṃ varaḥ /
kiṃ karoṣi mahābhāga vyāsaputra mahādyute //
1.60.d:
ततः प्रोवाच विप्रेन्द्र शुकं विदां वरः ।
किं करोषि महाभाग व्यासपुत्र महाद्युते ॥
1.60.m: Then, O foremost of the twice-born, the best among knowers spoke to Śuka: / “What are you doing, O fortunate one, son of Vyāsa of great splendor?”

1.60.s:
śuka uvāca
svādhyāye saṃpravṛtto 'haṃ brahmaputrādhunā sthitaḥ /
tvaddarśanamanuprāptaḥ kenāpi sukṛtena ca //
1.60.d:
शुक उवाच
स्वाध्याये संप्रवृत्तो ऽहं ब्रह्मपुत्राधुना स्थितः ।
त्वद्दर्शनमनुप्राप्तः केनापि सुकृतेन च ॥
1.60.m: Śuka said: / “Engaged in Vedic study, O son of Brahmā, I am now residing here, / and by some good deed I have obtained your sight.

1.60.s:
kiñcittvāṃ praṣṭumicchāmi tattvaṃ mokṣārthasādhanam /
tadvadasva mahābhāga yathā ta jjñānamāpnuyām //
1.60.d:
किञ्चित्त्वां प्रष्टुमिच्छामि तत्त्वं मोक्षार्थसाधनम् ।
तद्वदस्व महाभाग यथा त ज्ज्ञानमाप्नुयाम् ॥
1.60.m: I wish to ask you something about the truth that accomplishes liberation. / Speak that, O fortunate one, so that I may attain that knowledge.”

1.60.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
nāsti vidyāsamaṃ cakṣurnāsti vidyāsamaṃ tapaḥ /
nāsti rāgasamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti tyāgasamaṃ sukham //
1.60.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति विद्यासमं तपः ।
नास्ति रागसमं दुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम् ॥
1.60.m: Sanatkumāra said: / “There is no eye equal to knowledge, there is no asceticism equal to knowledge; / there is no suffering equal to passion, there is no happiness equal to renunciation.

1.60.s:
nivṛttiḥ karmaṇaḥ pāpātsatataṃ puṇyaśīlatā /
sadvṛttiḥ samudācāraḥ śreya etadanuttamam //
1.60.d:
निवृत्तिः कर्मणः पापात्सततं पुण्यशीलता ।
सद्वृत्तिः समुदाचारः श्रेय एतदनुत्तमम् ॥
1.60.m: Abstinence from sinful action, constant habit of virtue, / right livelihood, and proper conduct—this is the unsurpassable good.

1.60.s:
mānuṣyamasukhaṃ prāpya yaḥ sajjati sa muhyati /
nālaṃ sa duḥkhamokṣāya saṃgo vai duḥkhalakṣaṇaḥ //
1.60.d:
मानुष्यमसुखं प्राप्य यः सज्जति स मुह्यति ।
नालं स दुःखमोक्षाय संगो वै दुःखलक्षणः ॥
1.60.m: Having attained human birth, which is painful, he who becomes attached is deluded; / he is not capable of release from suffering, for attachment is indeed the mark of suffering.

1.60.s:
saktasya buddharbhavati mohajālavivarddhinī /
mohajālāvṛto duḥkhamihāmutra tathāśnute //
1.60.d:
सक्तस्य बुद्धर्भवति मोहजालविवर्द्धिनी ।
मोहजालावृतो दुःखमिहामुत्र तथाश्नुते ॥
1.60.m: The intellect of one who is attached promotes the snare of delusion; / enveloped by the snare of delusion, he experiences suffering here and in the hereafter.

1.60.s:
sarvopāyena kāmasya krodhasya ca vinigrahaḥ /
kāryaḥ śreyorthinā tau hi śreyoghātārthamudyatau //
1.60.d:
सर्वोपायेन कामस्य क्रोधस्य च विनिग्रहः ।
कार्यः श्रेयोर्थिना तौ हि श्रेयोघातार्थमुद्यतौ ॥
1.60.m: By every means, restraint of desire and anger / should be practiced by one who seeks the good; for those two are bent on destroying the good.

1.60.s:
nityaṃ krodhāttapo rakṣecchriyaṃ rakṣeñca matsarāt /
vidyāṃ mānāvamānābhyāmātmānaṃ tu pramādataḥ //
1.60.d:
नित्यं क्रोधात्तपो रक्षेच्छ्रियं रक्षेञ्च मत्सरात् ।
विद्यां मानावमानाभ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः ॥
1.60.m: One should always guard asceticism from anger, guard prosperity from envy, / guard learning from pride and dishonor, and guard oneself from heedlessness.

1.60.s:
ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmaḥ kṣamā ca paramaṃ balam /
ātmajñānaṃ paraṃ jñānaṃ satyaṃ hi paramaṃ hitam //
1.60.d:
आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः क्षमा च परमं बलम् ।
आत्मज्ञानं परं ज्ञानं सत्यं हि परमं हितम् ॥
1.60.m: Harmlessness is the highest virtue, and patience is the supreme strength; / knowledge of the Self is the highest knowledge, and truth is indeed the supreme benefit.

1.60.s:
yena sarvaṃ parityaktaṃ sa vidvānsa ca paṇḍitaḥ /
indriyairindriyārthebhyaścaratyātmavaśairiha //
1.60.d:
येन सर्वं परित्यक्तं स विद्वान्स च पण्डितः ।
इन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियार्थेभ्यश्चरत्यात्मवशैरिह ॥
1.60.m: He by whom all has been renounced is learned and wise; / he moves in this world with his senses restrained, kept under his own control away from sense-objects,

1.60.s:
asajjamānaḥ śāntātmā nirvikāraḥ samāhitaḥ /
ātmabhūtairatadbhūtaḥ saha caiva vinaiva ca //
1.60.d:
असज्जमानः शान्तात्मा निर्विकारः समाहितः ।
आत्मभूतैरतद्भूतः सह चैव विनैव च ॥
1.60.m: unattached, tranquil in mind, free from agitation, concentrated, / becoming identical with all beings, yet different from them, with them and yet without them.

1.60.s:
sa vimuktaḥ paraṃ śreyo na cireṇādhigacchati /
adarśanamasaṃsparśastathaivābhāṣāṇaṃ sadā //
1.60.d:
स विमुक्तः परं श्रेयो न चिरेणाधिगच्छति ।
अदर्शनमसंस्पर्शस्तथैवाभाषाणं सदा ॥
1.60.m: He, fully liberated, attains the supreme good before long. / Not seeing, not touching, and likewise never speaking [evilly]

1.60.s:
yasya bhūtaiḥ saha mune sa śreyo vindate mahat /
na hiṃsyātsarvabhūtāni bhūtairmaitrāyaṇaścaret //
1.60.d:
यस्य भूतैः सह मुने स श्रेयो विन्दते महत् ।
न हिंस्यात्सर्वभूतानि भूतैर्मैत्रायणश्चरेत् ॥
1.60.m: with living beings, O sage, he obtains the great good. / One should not injure any living beings; one should act with friendliness toward creatures.

1.60.s:
nedaṃ janma samāsādya vairaṃ kurvīta kena cit /
ākiñcanyaṃ susaṃtoṣo nirāśiṣṭvamacāpalam //
1.60.d:
नेदं जन्म समासाद्य वैरं कुर्वीत केन चित् ।
आकिञ्चन्यं सुसंतोषो निराशिष्ट्वमचापलम् ॥
1.60.m: Having attained this birth, one should not bear enmity toward anyone. / Absence of possessions, perfect contentment, desirelessness, freedom from fickleness—

1.60.s:
etadāhuḥ paraṃ śreya ātmajñasya jitātmanaḥ /
parigrahaṃ parityajya bhava tātajitendriyaḥ //
1.60.d:
एतदाहुः परं श्रेय आत्मज्ञस्य जितात्मनः ।
परिग्रहं परित्यज्य भव तातजितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.60.m: this they call the supreme good for the knower of the Self whose self is conquered. / Having abandoned all acquisition, dear boy, be one whose senses are mastered.

1.60.s:
aśokaṃ sthānamātiṣṭa iha cāmutra cābhayam /
nirāśiṣo na śocanti tyajedāśiṣamātmanaḥ //
1.60.d:
अशोकं स्थानमातिष्ट इह चामुत्र चाभयम् ।
निराशिषो न शोचन्ति त्यजेदाशिषमात्मनः ॥
1.60.m: Resort to the sorrowless state, fearless both here and hereafter; / those free of desires do not grieve; one should renounce one's own desire.

1.60.s:
parityajyāśiṣaṃ saumya duḥkhagrāmādvimokṣyase /
taparonityena dāntena muninā saṃyatātmanā //
1.60.d:
परित्यज्याशिषं सौम्य दुःखग्रामाद्विमोक्ष्यसे ।
तपरोनित्येन दान्तेन मुनिना संयतात्मना ॥
1.60.m: Renouncing desire, gentle one, you will be released from the multitude of sorrows. / Intent on asceticism, subdued, a sage with restrained mind,

1.60.s:
ajitaṃ jetukāmena bhāvyaṃ saṃgeṣvasaṃginā /
guṇasaṃgeṣveṣvanāsakta ekacaryā rataḥ sadā //
1.60.d:
अजितं जेतुकामेन भाव्यं संगेष्वसंगिना ।
गुणसंगेष्वेष्वनासक्त एकचर्या रतः सदा ॥
1.60.m: desiring to conquer the unconquered, should remain unattached amidst attachments; / unattached in these contacts with the qualities, always delighting in solitary wandering,

1.60.s:
brāhmaṇo na cirādeva sukhamāyātyanuttamam /
dvandvārāmeṣu bhūteṣu varāko ramate muniḥ //
1.60.d:
ब्राह्मणो न चिरादेव सुखमायात्यनुत्तमम् ।
द्वन्द्वारामेषु भूतेषु वराको रमते मुनिः ॥
1.60.m: the brāhmaṇa attains unsurpassable happiness before long. / While living beings delight in pairs of opposites, the wretched sage takes delight [elsewhere].

1.60.s:
kiñcinprajñānatṛpto 'sau jñānatṛpto na śocati /
śubhairlabheta devatvaṃ vyāmiśrairjanma mānuṣam //
1.60.d:
किञ्चिन्प्रज्ञानतृप्तो ऽसौ ज्ञानतृप्तो न शोचति ।
शुभैर्लभेत देवत्वं व्यामिश्रैर्जन्म मानुषम् ॥
1.60.m: Satisfied with a little understanding, [yet] satisfied with knowledge, he does not grieve. / Through auspicious deeds one may obtain divine status; through mixed deeds, human birth;

1.60.s:
aśubhaiścāpyadho janma karmabhirlabhate 'vaśaḥ /
tatra mṛtyujarāduḥkhaiḥ satataṃ samabhidrutam //
1.60.d:
अशुभैश्चाप्यधो जन्म कर्मभिर्लभते ऽवशः ।
तत्र मृत्युजरादुःखैः सततं समभिद्रुतम् ॥
1.60.m: and through inauspicious deeds, helpless, one attains lower birth. / A creature sees that cycle of rebirth there, constantly beset

1.60.s:
saṃsāraṃ paśyate jantustatkathaṃ nāvabudhse /
ahite hitasaṃjñastvamadhruve dhruvasaṃjñakaḥ //
1.60.d:
संसारं पश्यते जन्तुस्तत्कथं नावबुध्से ।
अहिते हितसंज्ञस्त्वमध्रुवे ध्रुवसंज्ञकः ॥
1.60.m: by the sufferings of death and old age—how do you not perceive it? / You see the beneficial in what is unbeneficial, the permanent in what is impermanent,

1.60.s:
anarthe vārthasaṃjñastvaṃ kimarthaṃ nāvabudhyase /
saṃveṣṭyamānaṃ bahubhirmohatantubhirātmajaiḥ //
1.60.d:
अनर्थे वार्थसंज्ञस्त्वं किमर्थं नावबुध्यसे ।
संवेष्ट्यमानं बहुभिर्मोहतन्तुभिरात्मजैः ॥
1.60.m: or you see value in what is worthless—why do you not understand? / Being enveloped by many threads of delusion born of yourself,

1.60.s:
kośakāravadātmānaṃ veṣṭito nāvabudhyase /
alaṃ parigraheṇeha doṣavān hi parigrahaḥ //
1.60.d:
कोशकारवदात्मानं वेष्टितो नावबुध्यसे ।
अलं परिग्रहेणेह दोषवान् हि परिग्रहः ॥
1.60.m: like a silkworm, you are entwined and do not understand. / Enough with possessions here, for possession is indeed full of fault.

1.60.s:
kṛmirhi kośakārastu badhyate svaparigrahāt /
putradārakuṭuṃbeṣu saktāḥ sīdanti jantavaḥ //
1.60.d:
कृमिर्हि कोशकारस्तु बध्यते स्वपरिग्रहात् ।
पुत्रदारकुटुंबेषु सक्ताः सीदन्ति जन्तवः ॥
1.60.m: The worm, the silkworm, is bound by its own creation of a cocoon; / creatures attached to children, wife, and family perish,

1.60.s:
saraḥpaṅkārṇave magnā jīrṇā vanagajā iva /
mohajālasamākṛṣṭānpaśyajantūnsuduḥkhitān //
1.60.d:
सरःपङ्कार्णवे मग्ना जीर्णा वनगजा इव ।
मोहजालसमाकृष्टान्पश्यजन्तून्सुदुःखितान् ॥
1.60.m: like old forest elephants sunk in an ocean of lake-mud. / Behold living beings, deeply afflicted, dragged by the snare of delusion,

1.60.s:
kuṭuṃbaṃ putradāraṃ ca śarīraṃ dravyasaṃcayam /
pārakyamadhruvaṃ sarvaṃ kiṃ svaṃ sukṛtaduṣkṛte //
1.60.d:
कुटुंबं पुत्रदारं च शरीरं द्रव्यसंचयम् ।
पारक्यमध्रुवं सर्वं किं स्वं सुकृतदुष्कृते ॥
1.60.m: family, children, wife, body, and accumulation of wealth. / All is belonging to another, all is impermanent—what is one's own except good and bad deeds?

1.60.s:
yadā sarvaṃ parityajya gantavyamavaśena vai /
anarthe kiṃ prasaktastvaṃ svamarthaṃ nānutiṣṭasi //
1.60.d:
यदा सर्वं परित्यज्य गन्तव्यमवशेन वै ।
अनर्थे किं प्रसक्तस्त्वं स्वमर्थं नानुतिष्टसि ॥
1.60.m: When one must inevitably depart helplessly, leaving everything behind, / why are you absorbed in what is worthless, and do not attend to your own true goal?

1.60.s:
aviśrāntamanālaṃbamapātheyamadaiśikam /
tamaḥ karttāramadhvānaṃ kathameko gamiṣyasi //
1.60.d:
अविश्रान्तमनालंबमपाथेयमदैशिकम् ।
तमः कर्त्तारमध्वानं कथमेको गमिष्यसि ॥
1.60.m: Without rest, without support, without provisions, without a guide, / how will you go alone on the path that produces darkness?

1.60.s:
nahi tvāṃ prasthitaṃ kaścitpṛṣṭato 'nugamiṣyati /
sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ ca tvāṃ gacchantamanuyāsyataḥ //
1.60.d:
नहि त्वां प्रस्थितं कश्चित्पृष्टतो ऽनुगमिष्यति ।
सुकृतं दुष्कृतं च त्वां गच्छन्तमनुयास्यतः ॥
1.60.m: No one will follow behind you once you have departed; / your good deeds and bad deeds will follow you as you go.

1.60.s:
vidyā karma ca śauryaṃ ca jñānaṃ ca bahuvistaram /
arthārthamanuśīryante siddhārthastu vimucyate //
1.60.d:
विद्या कर्म च शौर्यं च ज्ञानं च बहुविस्तरम् ।
अर्थार्थमनुशीर्यन्ते सिद्धार्थस्तु विमुच्यते ॥
1.60.m: Learning, action, heroism, and widely extensive knowledge / are worn away for the sake of wealth, but one who has achieved the true goal is liberated.

1.60.s:
nibandhinī rajjureṣā yā grāme vasato ratiḥ /
chitvaināṃ sukṛto yānti naināṃ chindanti duṣkṛtaḥ //
1.60.d:
निबन्धिनी रज्जुरेषा या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः ।
छित्वैनां सुकृतो यान्ति नैनां छिन्दन्ति दुष्कृतः ॥
1.60.m: This attachment to living in a village is a binding rope; / cutting it, the virtuous depart, but the evil-doers do not cut it.

1.60.s:
tulyajātivayorūpān hṛtānpasyasi mṛtyunā /
na ca nāmāsti nirvedo lohaṃ hi hṛdayaṃ tava //
1.60.d:
तुल्यजातिवयोरूपान् हृतान्पस्यसि मृत्युना ।
न च नामास्ति निर्वेदो लोहं हि हृदयं तव ॥
1.60.m: You see those of equal caste, age, and appearance snatched away by death, / and yet there is no disgust in you; your heart is surely made of iron!

1.60.s:
rūpakūlāṃ manaḥ srotāṃ sparśadvīpāṃ rasāvahām /
gandhapaṅkāṃ śabdajalāṃ svargamārgadurāruhām //
1.60.d:
रूपकूलां मनः स्रोतां स्पर्शद्वीपां रसावहाम् ।
गन्धपङ्कां शब्दजलां स्वर्गमार्गदुरारुहाम् ॥
1.60.m: With forms as its banks, the mind as its current, touch as its islands, taste as its flow, / smell as its mud, sound as its water, difficult to ascend on the path to heaven,

1.60.s:
kṣamāritrāṃ satyamayīṃ dharmasthairyakarākarām /
tyāgavātādhvagāṃ śīghrāṃ buddhināvaṃ nadīṃ taret //
1.60.d:
क्षमारित्रां सत्यमयीं धर्मस्थैर्यकराकराम् ।
त्यागवाताध्वगां शीघ्रां बुद्धिनावं नदीं तरेत् ॥
1.60.m: one should cross the river with the swift boat of intellect, having forbearance as its rudder, consisting of truth, made of the steady mines of righteousness, and driven by the wind of renunciation.

1.60.s:
tyaktvā dharmamadharmaṃ ca hyubhe satyānṛte tyaja /
tyaja dharmamasaṃkalpādadharmaṃ cāpyahiṃsayā //
1.60.d:
त्यक्त्वा धर्ममधर्मं च ह्युभे सत्यानृते त्यज ।
त्यज धर्ममसंकल्पादधर्मं चाप्यहिंसया ॥
1.60.m: Abandoning both righteousness and unrighteousness, renounce both truth and falsehood; / abandon righteousness through non-intention, and unrighteousness through non-injury;

1.60.s:
ubhe satyānṛte buddhiṃ paramaniścayāt /
asthisthūṇaṃ snāyuyutaṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepanam //
1.60.d:
उभे सत्यानृते बुद्धिं परमनिश्चयात् ।
अस्थिस्थूणं स्नायुयुतं मांसशोणितलेपनम् ॥
1.60.m: [abandon] both truth and falsehood by intellect, through supreme ascertainment. / Having bones for pillars, bound with sinews, plastered with flesh and blood,

1.60.s:
dharmāvanaddhaṃ durgandhiṃ pūrṇaṃ mūtrapurīṣayoḥ /
jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ rogāyatanamasthiram //
1.60.d:
धर्मावनद्धं दुर्गन्धिं पूर्णं मूत्रपुरीषयोः ।
जराशोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनमस्थिरम् ॥
1.60.m: covered with skin, foul-smelling, filled with urine and feces, / overcome by old age and grief, an abode of disease, unstable,

1.60.s:
rajasvalamanityaṃ ca bhūtāvāsaṃ samutsṛja /
idaṃ viśvaṃ jagatsarvamajagañcāpi yadbhavet //
1.60.d:
रजस्वलमनित्यं च भूतावासं समुत्सृज ।
इदं विश्वं जगत्सर्वमजगञ्चापि यद्भवेत् ॥
1.60.m: subject to defilement and transient, cast off this dwelling of the elements! / This entire universe, both moving and unmoving, that exists,

1.60.s:
mahābhūtātmakaṃ sarvamasmādyatparamāṇumat /
indriyāṇi ca pañcaiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajastathā //
1.60.d:
महाभूतात्मकं सर्वमस्माद्यत्परमाणुमत् ।
इन्द्रियाणि च पञ्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥
1.60.m: all consists of the great elements, and what is subtler than this; / the five sense-organs, and tamas, sattva, and rajas,

1.60.s:
ityeṣa saptadaśako rāśikhyaktasaṃjñakaḥ /
sarvairihendriyārthaiśca vyaktāvyaktairhi hitam //
1.60.d:
इत्येष सप्तदशको राशिख्यक्तसंज्ञकः ।
सर्वैरिहेन्द्रियार्थैश्च व्यक्ताव्यक्तैर्हि हितम् ॥
1.60.m: thus this group of seventeen is known as the manifest; / along with all sense-objects here, manifest and unmanifest, it is established.

1.60.s:
pañcaviṃśaka ityeṣa vyaktāvyaktamayo gaṇaḥ /
etaiḥ sarvaiḥ samāyuktamanityamabhidhīyate //
1.60.d:
पञ्चविंशक इत्येष व्यक्ताव्यक्तमयो गणः ।
एतैः सर्वैः समायुक्तमनित्यमभिधीयते ॥
1.60.m: This group of twenty-five consists of the manifest and unmanifest; / combined with all these, it is declared to be impermanent.

1.60.s:
