trivargo 'tra sukhaṃ duḥkha jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā /
ya idaṃ veda tattvena sasa veda prabhavāpyayau //
1.60.d:
त्रिवर्गो ऽत्र सुखं दुःख जीवितं मरणं तथा ।
य इदं वेद तत्त्वेन सस वेद प्रभवाप्ययौ ॥
1.60.m: Herein lie the three aims of life, pleasure, pain, life, and death. / He who knows this in truth, knows the origin and dissolution [of all].’

1.60.s:
indriyairgṛhyate yadyattadvyaktamabhidhīyate /
avyaktamatha tajjñeyaṃ liṅgagrāhyamatīndriyam //
1.60.d:
इन्द्रियैर्गृह्यते यद्यत्तद्व्यक्तमभिधीयते ।
अव्यक्तमथ तज्ज्ञेयं लिङ्गग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् ॥
1.60.m: Whatever is grasped by the senses is called the manifest; / but that which is to be grasped by inference, beyond the senses, should be known as the unmanifest.

1.60.s:
indriyairniyatairdehī dhārābhiriva tarpyate /
loke vihitamātmānaṃ lokaṃ cātmani paśyati //
1.60.d:
इन्द्रियैर्नियतैर्देही धाराभिरिव तर्प्यते ।
लोके विहितमात्मानं लोकं चात्मनि पश्यति ॥
1.60.m: When the senses are restrained, the embodied soul is satisfied as if by streams [of rain]; / he sees himself established in the world and the world in himself.

1.60.s:
parāvaradṛśaḥ śaktirjñānavelāṃ na paśyati /
paśyataḥ sarvabhūtāni sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā //
1.60.d:
परावरदृशः शक्तिर्ज्ञानवेलां न पश्यति ।
पश्यतः सर्वभूतानि सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा ॥
1.60.m: The power of one who sees the higher and the lower sees no boundary to knowledge, / as he sees all beings in all states at all times.

1.60.s:
brahmabhūtasya saṃyogo nāśubhenopapadyate /
jñānena vividhātkleśānna nivṛttiśca dehajāt //
1.60.d:
ब्रह्मभूतस्य संयोगो नाशुभेनोपपद्यते ।
ज्ञानेन विविधात्क्लेशान्न निवृत्तिश्च देहजात् ॥
1.60.m: For one who has become Brahman, association with what is inauspicious does not occur; / nor through knowledge is there failure of cessation from the manifold afflictions born of the body.

1.60.s:
lokabuddhiprakāśena lokamārgo na riṣyati /
anādinidhanaṃ jantumātmani sthitamavyayam //
1.60.d:
लोकबुद्धिप्रकाशेन लोकमार्गो न रिष्यति ।
अनादिनिधनं जन्तुमात्मनि स्थितमव्ययम् ॥
1.60.m: By the light of worldly understanding, the course of the world is not impaired; / the living being, without beginning or end, stands undecaying within the Self.

1.60.s:
akartāramamūḍhaṃ ca bhagavānāha tīrtavit /
yo jantuḥ svakṛtaistaistaiḥ karmabhirnityaduḥkhitaḥ //
1.60.d:
अकर्तारममूढं च भगवानाह तीर्तवित् ।
यो जन्तुः स्वकृतैस्तैस्तैः कर्मभिर्नित्यदुःखितः ॥
1.60.m: A non-agent and undeluded, the Lord, knower of the sacred fords, has said. / Whichever creature is perpetually tormented by its various deeds performed by itself,

1.60.s:
svaduḥkhapratighātārthaṃ hṝnti janturanekadhā /
tataḥ karma samādatte punaranyannavaṃ bahu //
1.60.d:
स्वदुःखप्रतिघातार्थं हॄन्ति जन्तुरनेकधा ।
ततः कर्म समादत्ते पुनरन्यन्नवं बहु ॥
1.60.m: To counteract its own sorrow, that creature struggles in various ways; / then it undertakes again another vast, new karma.

1.60.s:
tapyate 'tha punastena bhuktvāpathyamivāturaḥ /
ajasrameva mohānto duḥkheṣu sukhasaṃjñitaḥ //
1.60.d:
तप्यते ऽथ पुनस्तेन भुक्त्वापथ्यमिवातुरः ।
अजस्रमेव मोहान्तो दुःखेषु सुखसंज्ञितः ॥
1.60.m: Tormented then again by that, like a sick person who has eaten unwholesome food, / perpetually blinded by delusion, having notions of happiness amidst sorrows,

1.60.s:
vadhyate tapyate caiva bhayavatyarmabhiḥ sadā /
tato nivṛtto bandhātsvātkarmaṇāmudayādiha //
1.60.d:
वध्यते तप्यते चैव भयवत्यर्मभिः सदा ।
ततो निवृत्तो बन्धात्स्वात्कर्मणामुदयादिह ॥
1.60.m: One is slain and tormented always by fearful actions; / having ceased from that, one is freed here from the bondage of one's own actions through their fruition.

1.60.s:
paribhramati saṃsāre cakravadbāhuvarjitaḥ /
saṃyamena ca saṃbandhānnivṛttyā tapaso balāt //
1.60.d:
परिभ्रमति संसारे चक्रवद्बाहुवर्जितः ।
संयमेन च संबन्धान्निवृत्त्या तपसो बलात् ॥
1.60.m: It wanders in saṃsāra like a wheel, deprived of arms. / But through self-restraint and detachment from attachments, by the power of asceticism,

1.60.s:
samprāptā bahavaḥ siddhiṃ avyābādhāṃ sukhodayām //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde bṛhadupākhyāne ṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.60.d:
सम्प्राप्ता बहवः सिद्धिं अव्याबाधां सुखोदयाम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे बृहदुपाख्याने षष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
1.60.m:
Many have attained perfection, unhindered and yielding happiness.

Thus ends the sixtieth chapter in the Great Narrative, in the second quarter of the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.61.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
aśokaṃ śokanāśārthaṃ śāstraṃ śāntikaraṃ śivam /
niśamya labhyate buddhirlabdhāyāṃ sukhamedhate //
1.61.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अशोकं शोकनाशार्थं शास्त्रं शान्तिकरं शिवम् ।
निशम्य लभ्यते बुद्धिर्लब्धायां सुखमेधते ॥
1.61.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Hearing the griefless, auspicious scripture that destroys sorrow and brings peace, / understanding is obtained; when it is obtained, happiness flourishes.

1.61.s:
harṣasthānasahasrāṇi śokasthānaśatāni ca /
divase divase mūḍhamāviśanti na paṇḍitam //
1.61.d:
हर्षस्थानसहस्राणि शोकस्थानशतानि च ।
दिवसे दिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम् ॥
1.61.m: Thousands of occasions for joy and hundreds of occasions for sorrow / enter day after day into the fool, but not into the wise man.

1.61.s:
aniṣṭasaṃpraṃyogāśca viprayogātpriyasya ca /
manuṣyā mānasairduḥkhairyujyante ye 'lpabuddhayaḥ //
1.61.d:
अनिष्टसंप्रंयोगाश्च विप्रयोगात्प्रियस्य च ।
मनुष्या मानसैर्दुःखैर्युज्यन्ते ये ऽल्पबुद्धयः ॥
1.61.m: From association with what is unpleasant and separation from what is dear, / men of small intellect are joined to mental griefs.

1.61.s:
dravyeṣu samatīteṣu ye guṇāstenna cindayet /
tānanādriyamāṇaśca snehabandhādvimucyate //
1.61.d:
द्रव्येषु समतीतेषु ये गुणास्तेन्न चिन्दयेत् ।
ताननाद्रियमाणश्च स्नेहबन्धाद्विमुच्यते ॥
1.61.m: When possessions are gone, one should not contemplate the qualities they had; / and by disregarding them, one is freed from the bond of affection.

1.61.s:
doṣadarśī bhavettatra yatra rāgaḥ pravarttate /
aniṣṭabuddhitāṃ yacchettataḥ kṣipraṃ virājate //
1.61.d:
दोषदर्शी भवेत्तत्र यत्र रागः प्रवर्त्तते ।
अनिष्टबुद्धितां यच्छेत्ततः क्षिप्रं विराजते ॥
1.61.m: One should see faults where attachment arises; / one should view it as undesirable, and then quickly shines forth.

1.61.s:
nārtho na dharmo na yaśo yo 'tītamanuśocati /
asyābhāvena yujyetaṃ tañcāsya tu nivartate //
1.61.d:
नार्थो न धर्मो न यशो यो ऽतीतमनुशोचति ।
अस्याभावेन युज्येतं तञ्चास्य तु निवर्तते ॥
1.61.m: Neither wealth, nor dharma, nor fame comes to him who grieves over the past; / he would be afflicted by its absence, yet it does not return to him.

1.61.s:
guṇairbhūtāni yujyante tathaiva ca na yujyate /
sarvāṇi naitadekasya śokasthānaṃ hi vidyate //
1.61.d:
गुणैर्भूतानि युज्यन्ते तथैव च न युज्यते ।
सर्वाणि नैतदेकस्य शोकस्थानं हि विद्यते ॥
1.61.m: Beings are joined with qualities, and likewise they are not joined; / this entire state is not an occasion of grief for a single person alone.

1.61.s:
mṛtaṃ vā yadi vā naṣṭaṃ yo 'tītamanuśocati /
duḥkhena labhate duḥkhaṃ mahānarthe prapadyate //
1.61.d:
मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं यो ऽतीतमनुशोचति ।
दुःखेन लभते दुःखं महानर्थे प्रपद्यते ॥
1.61.m: Whoever grieves over the past, whether dead or lost, / gains sorrow from sorrow, and falls into a great calamity.

1.61.s:
duḥkhopaghāte śārīre mānase cāpyupasthite /
yasminna śakyate kartuṃ yatnastannānurcitayet //
1.61.d:
दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते ।
यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुर्चितयेत् ॥
1.61.m: When physical pain or mental affliction is present, / in whatever matter effort cannot be made, one should not brood upon it.

1.61.s:
bhaiṣajyametaddaḥkhasya yadetannānucintayet /
cintyamānaṃ hi na vyeti bhūyaścābhipravarddhate //
1.61.d:
भैषज्यमेतद्दःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् ।
चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चाभिप्रवर्द्धते ॥
1.61.m: This is the medicine for sorrow: that one should not dwell upon it; / for when dwelled upon, it does not depart, but grows even more.

1.61.s:
prajñayā mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ hanyācchārīramauṣadhaiḥ /
etadvijñāya sāmarthyaṃ na vānyaiḥ samatāmiyāt //
1.61.d:
प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः ।
एतद्विज्ञाय सामर्थ्यं न वान्यैः समतामियात् ॥
1.61.m: One should slay mental sorrow with wisdom, and physical [pain] with medicines; / knowing this capacity, one would not attain equality with others.

1.61.s:
anityaṃ jīvitaṃ rūpaṃ yauvanaṃ dravyasañcayaḥ /
ārogyaṃ priyasaṃvāsaṃ na mṛdhyetpaṇḍitaḥ kvacit //
1.61.d:
अनित्यं जीवितं रूपं यौवनं द्रव्यसञ्चयः ।
आरोग्यं प्रियसंवासं न मृध्येत्पण्डितः क्वचित् ॥
1.61.m: Life, beauty, youth, accumulation of wealth, / health, and living with loved ones are impermanent; a wise man should never take pleasure in them.

1.61.s:
nājñānaprabhavaṃ duḥkhamekaṃ śocitumarhati /
aśocanpratikurvīta yadi paśyedupakramam //
1.61.d:
नाज्ञानप्रभवं दुःखमेकं शोचितुमर्हति ।
अशोचन्प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम् ॥
1.61.m: One ought not to grieve over a single sorrow born of ignorance; / without grieving, one should counter it if one perceives a remedy.

1.61.s:
sukhātpriyataraṃ duḥkhaṃ jīvite nātra saṃśayaḥ /
jarāmaraṇaduḥkhebhyaḥ priyamātmānamuddharet //
1.61.d:
सुखात्प्रियतरं दुःखं जीविते नात्र संशयः ।
जरामरणदुःखेभ्यः प्रियमात्मानमुद्धरेत् ॥
1.61.m: In life, sorrow is dearer than happiness, without doubt here; / from the sorrows of old age and death, one should deliver one's dear self.

1.61.s:
bhajanti hi śārīrāṇi rogāḥ śarīramānasāḥ /
sāyakā iva tīkṣṇāgrāḥ prayuktā dṛḍhadhanvibhiḥ //
1.61.d:
भजन्ति हि शारीराणि रोगाः शरीरमानसाः ।
सायका इव तीक्ष्णाग्राः प्रयुक्ता दृढधन्विभिः ॥
1.61.m: For bodily and mental illnesses afflict physical beings, / like sharp-pointed arrows shot by sturdy archers.

1.61.s:
vyādhitasya cikitsābhistrasyato jīvitaiṣiṇaḥ /
āmayasya vināśāya śarīramanukṛṣyate //
1.61.d:
व्याधितस्य चिकित्साभिस्त्रस्यतो जीवितैषिणः ।
आमयस्य विनाशाय शरीरमनुकृष्यते ॥
1.61.m: Through medical treatments for the diseased person who trembles and longs for life, / the body is dragged down in order to destroy the sickness.

1.61.s:
sraṃsaṃti na nivartante srotāṃsi saritāmiva /
āyurādāya martyānāṃ rātryahāni punaḥpunaḥ //
1.61.d:
स्रंसंति न निवर्तन्ते स्रोतांसि सरितामिव ।
आयुरादाय मर्त्यानां रात्र्यहानि पुनःपुनः ॥
1.61.m: Nights and days fall away and do not turn back, like the currents of rivers, / taking away the lifespan of mortals again and again.

1.61.s:
apayantyayamatyantaṃ pakṣayoḥ śuklakṛṣṇayoḥ /
jātaṃ martyaṃ jarayati nimiṣaṃ nāvatiṣṭate //
1.61.d:
अपयन्त्ययमत्यन्तं पक्षयोः शुक्लकृष्णयोः ।
जातं मर्त्यं जरयति निमिषं नावतिष्टते ॥
1.61.m: This departure of the bright and dark fortnights is absolute; / it ages the born mortal, pausing not even for a twinkling of an eye.

1.61.s:
sukhaduḥkhābhibhūtānāmajaro jarayatyasūn /
ādityo hyastamabhyeti punaḥ punarudeti ca //
1.61.d:
सुखदुःखाभिभूतानामजरो जरयत्यसून् ।
आदित्यो ह्यस्तमभ्येति पुनः पुनरुदेति च ॥
1.61.m: The ageless [sun] wears away the lives of those overcome by happiness and sorrow; / for the sun sets, and rises again and again.

1.61.s:
adṛṣṭapūrvānādāya bhāvānapariśaṅkitān /
iṣṭāniṣṭā manuṣyāṇāṃ mataṃ gacchanti rātrayaḥ //
1.61.d:
अदृष्टपूर्वानादाय भावानपरिशङ्कितान् ।
इष्टानिष्टा मनुष्याणां मतं गच्छन्ति रात्रयः ॥
1.61.m: Bringing about states never seen before and unforeseen, / pleasant and unpleasant, the nights pass according to men's destiny.

1.61.s:
yo yadicchedyathākāmaṃ kāmānāṃ tattadāpnuyāt /
yadi syānna parādhīnaṃ puruṣasya kriyāphalam //
1.61.d:
यो यदिच्छेद्यथाकामं कामानां तत्तदाप्नुयात् ।
यदि स्यान्न पराधीनं पुरुषस्य क्रियाफलम् ॥
1.61.m: Whatever desires one wished at will, those very desires one would attain, / if the fruit of an action of a person were not dependent on another.

1.61.s:
saṃyatāścaiva takṣāśca matimantaśca mānavāḥ /
dṛśyante niṣphalāḥ saṃtaḥ prahīnāśca svakarmabhiḥ //
1.61.d:
संयताश्चैव तक्षाश्च मतिमन्तश्च मानवाः ।
दृश्यन्ते निष्फलाः संतः प्रहीनाश्च स्वकर्मभिः ॥
1.61.m: Restrained, skillful, and intelligent men / are seen to be destitute of results, ruined by their own deeds.

1.61.s:
apare niṣphalāḥ santo nirguṇāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ /
āśābhiraṇyasaṃyuktā dṛśyante sarvakāminaḥ //
1.61.d:
अपरे निष्फलाः सन्तो निर्गुणाः पुरुषाधमाः ।
आशाभिरण्यसंयुक्ता दृश्यन्ते सर्वकामिनः ॥
1.61.m: Others, destitute of good deeds, devoid of virtue, the lowest of men, / are seen possessing hopes and gold, fulfilling every desire.

1.61.s:
bhūtānāmaparaḥ kaściddhiṃsāyāṃ satatotthitaḥ /
vañcanāyāṃ ca lokeṣu sasukheṣveva jīyate //
1.61.d:
भूतानामपरः कश्चिद्धिंसायां सततोत्थितः ।
वञ्चनायां च लोकेषु ससुखेष्वेव जीयते ॥
1.61.m: Another person is constantly intent upon harm to living beings / and upon deceit in the world, yet lives in mere pleasure.

1.61.s:
aceṣṭamānamāsīnaṃ śrīḥ kañcidupatiṣṭati /
kaścitkarmāṇi kurute na prāpyamadhigacchati //
1.61.d:
अचेष्टमानमासीनं श्रीः कञ्चिदुपतिष्टति ।
कश्चित्कर्माणि कुरुते न प्राप्यमधिगच्छति ॥
1.61.m: Prosperity attends someone who sits inactive; / another performs actions and does not attain what is to be reached.

1.61.s:
aparādhānsamācṣṭuṃ puruṣasya svabhāvataḥ /
śukramanyatra saṃbhūtaṃ punaranyatra gacchati //
1.61.d:
अपराधान्समाच्ष्टुं पुरुषस्य स्वभावतः ।
शुक्रमन्यत्र संभूतं पुनरन्यत्र गच्छति ॥
1.61.m: To announce the offences of a man by nature, / semen produced in one place goes again to another.

1.61.s:
tasya yonau prasaktasya garbho bhavati mānavaḥ /
āmrapuṣpopamā yasya nivṛttirupalabhyate //
1.61.d:
तस्य योनौ प्रसक्तस्य गर्भो भवति मानवः ।
आम्रपुष्पोपमा यस्य निवृत्तिरुपलभ्यते ॥
1.61.m: From its attachment in the womb, an embryo becomes a human being, / whose cessation is seen to be like a mango flower.

1.61.s:
keṣāñcitputrakāmānāmanusantānamicchatām /
siddhau prayatamānānāṃ naivāṇḍamupajāyate //
1.61.d:
केषाञ्चित्पुत्रकामानामनुसन्तानमिच्छताम् ।
सिद्धौ प्रयतमानानां नैवाण्डमुपजायते ॥
1.61.m: For some who desire sons and long for a lineage, / though striving for success, not even an embryo is born.

1.61.s:
garbhādudvijamānānāṃ kruddhādaśīviṣādiva /
āyuṣmān jāyate putraḥ kathaṃ pretaḥ piteva saḥ //
1.61.d:
गर्भादुद्विजमानानां क्रुद्धादशीविषादिव ।
आयुष्मान् जायते पुत्रः कथं प्रेतः पितेव सः ॥
1.61.m: For those who shrink from the womb as from an angry venomous snake, / a long-lived son is born, while the father is like one departed.

1.61.s:
devāniṣṭvā tapastaptvā kṛpaṇaiḥ putrahetubhiḥ /
daśamāsānparidhṛtā jāyate kulapāṃsanāḥ //
1.61.d:
देवानिष्ट्वा तपस्तप्त्वा कृपणैः पुत्रहेतुभिः ।
दशमासान्परिधृता जायते कुलपांसनाः ॥
1.61.m: Having sacrificed to the gods and performed austerities for the sake of sons, by wretched people, / those borne for ten months are born as disgrace to the family.

1.61.s:
apare dhanadhānyāni bhogāṃśca pitṛsaṃcitān /
vimalānabhijāyante labdhvā taireva maṅgalaiḥ //
1.61.d:
अपरे धनधान्यानि भोगांश्च पितृसंचितान् ।
विमलानभिजायन्ते लब्ध्वा तैरेव मङ्गलैः ॥
1.61.m: Others are born having obtained immaculate wealth, grains, / and pleasures accumulated by their fathers through those very auspicious merits.

1.61.s:
anyonya samabhipretya maithunasya samāgame /
upadravaivādṛṣṭo yonau garbhaḥ prapadyate //
1.61.d:
अन्योन्य समभिप्रेत्य मैथुनस्य समागमे ।
उपद्रवैवादृष्टो योनौ गर्भः प्रपद्यते ॥
1.61.m: Mutually desiring one another in the union of sexual intercourse, / an unseen calamity, as it were, enters the womb as an embryo.

1.61.s:
snigdhatvādindriyārtheṣu mohānmaraṇamapriyam /
parityajati yo duḥkhaṃ sukhamapyubhayaṃ naraḥ //
1.61.d:
स्निग्धत्वादिन्द्रियार्थेषु मोहान्मरणमप्रियम् ।
परित्यजति यो दुःखं सुखमप्युभयं नरः ॥
1.61.m: Because of attachment to sense objects, death is unwelcome due to delusion; / the man who abandons both sorrow and happiness,

1.61.s:
atyeti brahma so 'tyantaṃ sukhamapyaśnute param /
duḥkhamarthā hi tyajyante pālane ca na te sukhāḥ //
1.61.d:
अत्येति ब्रह्म सो ऽत्यन्तं सुखमप्यश्नुते परम् ।
दुःखमर्था हि त्यज्यन्ते पालने च न ते सुखाः ॥
1.61.m: He completely transcends to Brahman, and enjoys supreme bliss; / for worldly goods are abandoned with sorrow, and they are not pleasant in guarding them.

1.61.s:
śrutvaiva nādhigamanaṃ nāśameṣāṃ na cintayet /
anyāmanyāṃ dhanāvasthāṃ prāpya vaiśeṣikā narāḥ //
1.61.d:
श्रुत्वैव नाधिगमनं नाशमेषां न चिन्तयेत् ।
अन्यामन्यां धनावस्थां प्राप्य वैशेषिका नराः ॥
1.61.m: Merely upon hearing it, one should not think of non-attainment nor of their destruction; / men having distinctions, upon attaining various states of wealth,

1.61.s:
atṛptā yānti vidhvaṃsaṃ santoṣaṃ yānti paṇḍitāḥ /
sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ //
1.61.d:
अतृप्ता यान्ति विध्वंसं सन्तोषं यान्ति पण्डिताः ।
सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः ॥
1.61.m: being unsatisfied, go to destruction, while the wise find contentment. / All accumulations end in depletion; all elevations end in a fall.

1.61.s:
saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam /
anto nāsti pipāsāyāstuṣṭistu paramaṃ sukham //
1.61.d:
संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं हि जीवितम् ।
अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायास्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम् ॥
1.61.m: Unions end in separation, and life indeed ends in death; / there is no end to thirst, but contentment is supreme happiness.

1.61.s:
tasmātsaṃtoṣameveha dhanaṃ śaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ /
nimeṣamātramapi hi yo 'dhigacchanna tiṣṭati //
1.61.d:
तस्मात्संतोषमेवेह धनं शंसन्ति पण्डिताः ।
निमेषमात्रमपि हि यो ऽधिगच्छन्न तिष्टति ॥
1.61.m: Therefore, the wise praise contentment alone as wealth in this world. / For he who, attaining [objects], does not remain stable even for the twinkling of an eye,

1.61.s:
saśarīreṣvanityeṣu nityaṃ kimanucintayet /
bhūteṣu bhāvaṃ saṃcintya ye buddhyā tamasaḥ param //
1.61.d:
सशरीरेष्वनित्येषु नित्यं किमनुचिन्तयेत् ।
भूतेषु भावं संचिन्त्य ये बुद्ध्या तमसः परम् ॥
1.61.m: what eternal thing could he contemplate in non-eternal bodies? / Having contemplated the true state among beings, those who through intellect [see] beyond darkness,

1.61.s:
na śocanti gatādhvānaḥ paśyanti paramāṃ gatim /
saṃcinvannekamevainaṃ kāmānāvitṛptakam //
1.61.d:
न शोचन्ति गताध्वानः पश्यन्ति परमां गतिम् ।
संचिन्वन्नेकमेवैनं कामानावितृप्तकम् ॥
1.61.m: having reached the end of the road, do not grieve; they see the supreme goal. / Accumulating only this one thing, an insatiable consumer of desires,

1.61.s:
vyāghra paśumivāsādya mṛtyurādāya gacchati /
athāpyupāyaṃ saṃpaśyedduḥkhasyāsya vimokṣaṇe //
1.61.d:
व्याघ्र पशुमिवासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति ।
अथाप्युपायं संपश्येद्दुःखस्यास्य विमोक्षणे ॥
1.61.m: Death, having approached like a tiger toward a beast, takes him and departs. / Yet one should perceive the means for deliverance from this sorrow.

1.61.s:
aśocannārabhennaiva yuktaścāvyasanī bhavet /
śabde sparśe rase rūpe gandhe ca paramaṃ tathā //
1.61.d:
अशोचन्नारभेन्नैव युक्तश्चाव्यसनी भवेत् ।
शब्दे स्पर्शे रसे रूपे गन्धे च परमं तथा ॥
1.61.m: not grieving, he should never undertake [fruitless acts]; disciplined, he should be free of addiction. / In sound, touch, taste, form, and smell—likewise in the highest—

1.61.s:
nopabhogātparaṃ kiñciddhanino vādhanasya vā /
vāksaṃprayogādbhṛtānāṃ nāsti duḥkhamanāmayam //
1.61.d:
नोपभोगात्परं किञ्चिद्धनिनो वाधनस्य वा ।
वाक्संप्रयोगाद्भृतानां नास्ति दुःखमनामयम् ॥
1.61.m: there is nothing beyond enjoyment, whether for the wealthy or the poor. / For those sustained by the exercise of speech, there is no pain without disease.

1.61.s:
viprayogaśca sarvasya na vācā na ca vidyayā /
praṇayaṃ parisaṃhṛtya saṃstuteṣvitareṣu ca //
1.61.d:
विप्रयोगश्च सर्वस्य न वाचा न च विद्यया ।
प्रणयं परिसंहृत्य संस्तुतेष्वितरेषु च ॥
1.61.m: And separation belongs to everything, not prevented by speech nor by learning. / Withdrawing affection both toward those who are praised and toward others,

1.61.s:
vicaredasamunnaddhaḥ sa sukhī sa ca paṇḍitaḥ /
adhyātmagatamālīno nirapekṣo nirāmiṣaḥ //
1.61.d:
विचरेदसमुन्नद्धः स सुखी स च पण्डितः ।
अध्यात्मगतमालीनो निरपेक्षो निरामिषः ॥
1.61.m: one who walks about without haughtiness is happy, and he is wise. / Resting in what pertains to the self, impartial, free of greed,

1.61.s:
ātmanaiva sahāyena caścaretsa sukhī bhavet /
sukhaduḥkhaviparyāso yadā samupapadyate //
1.61.d:
आत्मनैव सहायेन चश्चरेत्स सुखी भवेत् ।
सुखदुःखविपर्यासो यदा समुपपद्यते ॥
1.61.m: he who walks with the Self alone as his companion becomes happy. / When the reversal of pleasure and pain occurs,

1.61.s:
nainaṃ prajñā suniyataṃ trāyate nāpi pauruṣam /
svabhāvādyatnamātiṣṭhedyatnavānnāvasīdati //
1.61.d:
नैनं प्रज्ञा सुनियतं त्रायते नापि पौरुषम् ।
स्वभावाद्यत्नमातिष्ठेद्यत्नवान्नावसीदति ॥
1.61.m: neither well-disciplined wisdom nor human effort protects him. / By nature one should undertake exertion; one endowed with effort does not sink down.

1.61.s:
upadrava ivāniṣṭo yoniṃ garbhaḥ prapadyate /
tāni pūrvaśarīrāṇi nityamekaṃ śarīriṇam //
1.61.d:
उपद्रव इवानिष्टो योनिं गर्भः प्रपद्यते ।
तानि पूर्वशरीराणि नित्यमेकं शरीरिणम् ॥
1.61.m: Like an unwanted calamity, the embryo enters the womb. / Those previous bodies [belong] always to a single embodied being.

1.61.s:
prāṇināṃ prāṇasaṃrodhe māṃsaśleṣmaviceṣṭitam /
nirdagdhaṃ paradehena paradeṃhaṃ balābalam //
1.61.d:
प्राणिनां प्राणसंरोधे मांसश्लेष्मविचेष्टितम् ।
निर्दग्धं परदेहेन परदेंहं बलाबलम् ॥
1.61.m: When the breath of living beings is obstructed, agitated by flesh and phlegm, / burned up by another body, another body is strong or weak;

1.61.s:
vinaśyati vināśānte nāvi nāvamivācalām /
saṃgatyā jaṭhare nyastaṃ retobindumacetanam //
1.61.d:
विनश्यति विनाशान्ते नावि नावमिवाचलाम् ।
संगत्या जठरे न्यस्तं रेतोबिन्दुमचेतनम् ॥
1.61.m: it perishes at the end of destruction, like an unsteady boat upon a boat. / Deposited in the womb by intercourse, an unconscious drop of semen—

1.61.s:
kena yatnena jīvantaṃ garbhaṃ tvamiha paśyasi /
annapānāni jīryante yatra bhakṣyāśca bhakṣitāḥ //
1.61.d:
केन यत्नेन जीवन्तं गर्भं त्वमिह पश्यसि ।
अन्नपानानि जीर्यन्ते यत्र भक्ष्याश्च भक्षिताः ॥
1.61.m: by what effort do you see the embryo living here? / Where food and drink, and whatever foods are eaten, are digested,

1.61.s:
tasminnevodare garbhaḥ kiṃ nānnamiva jīryati /
garbhe mūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ svabhāvaniyatā gatiḥ //
1.61.d:
तस्मिन्नेवोदरे गर्भः किं नान्नमिव जीर्यति ।
गर्भे मूत्रपुरीषाणां स्वभावनियता गतिः ॥
1.61.m: in that very belly, why does the embryo not digest like food? / In the womb, the course of urine and feces is determined by nature;

1.61.s:
dhāraṇe vā visarge ca na kartuṃ vidyate 'vaśaḥ /
prabhavantyudare garbhā jāyamānāstathāpare //
1.61.d:
धारणे वा विसर्गे च न कर्तुं विद्यते ऽवशः ।
प्रभवन्त्युदरे गर्भा जायमानास्तथापरे ॥
1.61.m: helpless, one has no power to retain or discharge them. / Embryos develop in the belly, and others are born;

1.61.s:
āgamena mahānyeṣāṃ vināśa upapadyate /
etasmādyonisaṃbandhādyo jīvanparimucyate //
1.61.d:
आगमेन महान्येषां विनाश उपपद्यते ।
एतस्माद्योनिसंबन्धाद्यो जीवन्परिमुच्यते ॥
1.61.m: with their arrival, great destruction falls upon others. / He who, while living, is freed from this connection with the womb,

1.61.s:
pūjāṃ na labhate kāñcitpunarddhandveṣu majjati /
garbhasya saha jātasya saptamīmīdṛśīṃ daśām //
1.61.d:
पूजां न लभते काञ्चित्पुनर्द्धन्द्वेषु मज्जति ।
गर्भस्य सह जातस्य सप्तमीमीदृशीं दशाम् ॥
1.61.m: receives no honor [here], and sinks back into the pairs of opposites. / Of the embryo born along with it, [the wise reach] such a seventh state;

1.61.s:
prāpnuvanti tataḥ pañca na bhavanti śatāyuṣaḥ /
nābhyutthāne manuṣyāṇāṃ yogāḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.61.d:
प्राप्नुवन्ति ततः पञ्च न भवन्ति शतायुषः ।
नाभ्युत्थाने मनुष्याणां योगाः स्युर्नात्र संशयः ॥
1.61.m: then the five reach [death], not living to a hundred years. / In human enterprise there would be successes, no doubt about it;

1.61.s:
vyādhibhiśca vivadhyante vyāghraiḥ kṣudramṛgā iva /
vyādhibhirbhakṣyamāṇānāṃ tyajatāṃ vipulandhanam //
1.61.d:
व्याधिभिश्च विवध्यन्ते व्याघ्रैः क्षुद्रमृगा इव ।
व्याधिभिर्भक्ष्यमाणानां त्यजतां विपुलन्धनम् ॥
1.61.m: yet they are struck down by diseases, like small deer by tigers. / For those being devoured by diseases, even as they spend abundant wealth,

1.61.s: vedanā nāpakarṣanti yatamānāścikitsakāḥ //
1.61.d: वेदना नापकर्षन्ति यतमानाश्चिकित्सकाः ॥
1.61.m: physicians, though striving, do not take away the pain.

1.61.s:
te cāpi vividhā vaidyāḥ kuśalā saṃmatauṣadhāḥ /
vyādhibhiḥ parikṛṣyante mṛgā jyāghrairivārditāḥ //
1.61.d:
ते चापि विविधा वैद्याः कुशला संमतौषधाः ।
व्याधिभिः परिकृष्यन्ते मृगा ज्याघ्रैरिवार्दिताः ॥
1.61.m: And even those various skillful physicians, experienced in medicines, / are dragged down by diseases, like deer tormented by tigers.

1.61.s:
te pibanti kaṣāyāṃśca sarpīṣi vividhāni ca /
dṛśyante jarayā bhagnā nāgairnāgā ivottamāḥ //
1.61.d:
ते पिबन्ति कषायांश्च सर्पीषि विविधानि च ।
दृश्यन्ते जरया भग्ना नागैर्नागा इवोत्तमाः ॥
1.61.m: They drink decoctions and various kinds of clarified butter, / yet they are seen broken by old age, like excellent elephants by [other] elephants.

1.61.s:
kairvā bhuvi cikitsyenta rogārttā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ /
śvāpadāśca daridrāśca prāyo nārtā bhavanti te //
1.61.d:
कैर्वा भुवि चिकित्स्येन्त रोगार्त्ता मृगपक्षिणः ।
श्वापदाश्च दरिद्राश्च प्रायो नार्ता भवन्ति ते ॥
1.61.m: Or by whom on earth are beasts and birds, afflicted with sickness, treated? / And beasts of prey and the destitute are generally not afflicted.

1.61.s:
ghorānapi durādharṣānnṛpatīnugratejasa /
ākramya roga ādatte paśūnpaśupaco yathā //
1.61.d:
घोरानपि दुराधर्षान्नृपतीनुग्रतेजस ।
आक्रम्य रोग आदत्ते पशून्पशुपचो यथा ॥
1.61.m: Attacking even terrible, invincible kings of fierce splendor, / disease seizes them, as a butcher does beasts.

1.61.s:
iti lokamanākrandaṃ mohaśokapariplutam /
srotasā mahasā kṣipraṃ hriyamāṇaṃ balīyasā //
1.61.d:
इति लोकमनाक्रन्दं मोहशोकपरिप्लुतम् ।
स्रोतसा महसा क्षिप्रं ह्रियमाणं बलीयसा ॥
1.61.m: Thus the world, destitute of refuge, overwhelmed by delusion and grief, / is quickly swept away by a great, mighty current.

1.61.s:
na dhanena na rājyena nogreṇa tapasā tathā /
svabhāvā hyativartante ye nirmuktāḥ śarīriṣu //
1.61.d:
न धनेन न राज्येन नोग्रेण तपसा तथा ।
स्वभावा ह्यतिवर्तन्ते ये निर्मुक्ताः शरीरिषु ॥
1.61.m: Neither by wealth nor by kingdom, nor by fierce austerity, / do inborn natures surpass those [afflictions] that are released upon embodied beings.

1.61.s:
uparyapari lokasya sarvo bhavitumicchati /
yatate ca yathāśakti na ca tadvartate tathā //
1.61.d:
उपर्यपरि लोकस्य सर्वो भवितुमिच्छति ।
यतते च यथाशक्ति न च तद्वर्तते तथा ॥
1.61.m: Everyone wishes to be higher and higher than the world, / and strives according to his power; yet it does not turn out so.

1.61.s:
na mriyerannajīryeransarve syuḥ sārvakāmikāḥ /
nāpriyaṃ pratipadyerannutthānasya phalaṃ prati //
1.61.d:
न म्रियेरन्नजीर्येरन्सर्वे स्युः सार्वकामिकाः ।
नाप्रियं प्रतिपद्येरन्नुत्थानस्य फलं प्रति ॥
1.61.m: They would not die, they would not age, all would have all desires fulfilled, / and they would never encounter what is unpleasant as the fruit of their enterprise!

1.61.s:
aiśvaryamadamattāśca mānānmayamadena ca /
apramattāḥ śaṭhāḥ krūrā vikrāntāḥ paryupāsate //
1.61.d:
ऐश्वर्यमदमत्ताश्च मानान्मयमदेन च ।
अप्रमत्ताः शठाः क्रूरा विक्रान्ताः पर्युपासते ॥
1.61.m: Drunk with the pride of sovereignty and with the pride of conceit, / the vigilant, the deceitful, the cruel, and the valiant wait upon [rulers].

1.61.s:
śokāḥ pratinivartante keṣāñcidasamīkṣatām /
svaṃ svaṃ ca punaranyeṣāṃ na kañcidatigacchati //
1.61.d:
शोकाः प्रतिनिवर्तन्ते केषाञ्चिदसमीक्षताम् ।
स्वं स्वं च पुनरन्येषां न कञ्चिदतिगच्छति ॥
1.61.m: For some, griefs turn back without their having anticipated them; / and each [destiny] of others does not bypass anyone.

1.61.s:
mahañca phalavaiṣamyaṃ dṛśyate karmasaṃdhiṣu /
vahṝnti śibikāmanye yāntyanye śibikāruhaḥ //
1.61.d:
महञ्च फलवैषम्यं दृश्यते कर्मसंधिषु ।
वहॄन्ति शिबिकामन्ये यान्त्यन्ये शिबिकारुहः ॥
1.61.m: A great disparity of fruits is seen in the junctures of actions: / some carry a palanquin, while others ride upon the palanquin.

1.61.s:
sarveṣāmṛddhikāmānāmanye rathapuraḥ sarāḥ /
manujāśca gataśrīkāḥ śataśo vividhāḥ striyāḥ //
1.61.d:
सर्वेषामृद्धिकामानामन्ये रथपुरः सराः ।
मनुजाश्च गतश्रीकाः शतशो विविधाः स्त्रियाः ॥
1.61.m: While all desire prosperity, others run before chariots; / and there are men bereft of fortune, and hundreds of diverse women.

1.61.s:
dvandvārāmeṣu bhūteṣu gacchantyekaikaśo narāḥ /
idamanyatparaṃ paśya nātra mohaṃ kariṣyasi //
1.61.d:
द्वन्द्वारामेषु भूतेषु गच्छन्त्येकैकशो नराः ।
इदमन्यत्परं पश्य नात्र मोहं करिष्यसि ॥
1.61.m: Among beings delighting in pairs of opposites, men depart one by one. / See this other, supreme truth; herein you will not fall into delusion:

1.61.s:
dharmaṃ cāpi tyajā dharmaṃ tyaja satyānṛtāṃ dhiyam /
sarvaṃ tyaktvā svarūpasthaḥ sukhī bhava nirāmayaḥ //
1.61.d:
धर्मं चापि त्यजा धर्मं त्यज सत्यानृतां धियम् ।
सर्वं त्यक्त्वा स्वरूपस्थः सुखी भव निरामयः ॥
1.61.m: Renounce righteousness and unrighteousness; renounce the intellect bound to truth and falsehood; / having abandoned everything, established in your own nature, be happy and free from disease.

1.61.s:
etatte paramaṃ guhyamākhyātamṛṣisattama /
yena devāḥ parityajya bhartyalokaṃ divaṃ gatāḥ //
1.61.d:
एतत्ते परमं गुह्यमाख्यातमृषिसत्तम ।
येन देवाः परित्यज्य भर्त्यलोकं दिवं गताः ॥
1.61.m: This supreme secret has been declared to you, O best of sages, / by which the gods, having abandoned the mortal world, went to heaven.

1.61.s:
sanandana uvāca
ityuktvā vyāsatanayaṃ samāpṛcchya mahāmuniḥ /
sanatkumāraḥ prayayau pūjitastena sādaram //
1.61.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
इत्युक्त्वा व्यासतनयं समापृच्छ्य महामुनिः ।
सनत्कुमारः प्रययौ पूजितस्तेन सादरम् ॥
1.61.m: Sanandana said: / Having spoken thus to Vyāsa's son and taken his leave, the great sage / Sanatkumāra departed, respectfully honored by him.

1.61.s:
śuko 'pi yogināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ samyagjñātvā hyavasthitam /
brahmaṇaḥ padamanveṣṭumutsukaḥ pitaraṃ yayau //
1.61.d:
शुको ऽपि योगिनां श्रेष्ठः सम्यग्ज्ञात्वा ह्यवस्थितम् ।
ब्रह्मणः पदमन्वेष्टुमुत्सुकः पितरं ययौ ॥
1.61.m: Śuka too, the best of yogins, having fully known what is established, / went to his father, eager to seek the state of Brahman.

1.61.s:
tataḥ pitrā samāgamya praṇamya ca mahāmuniḥ /
śukaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yayau kailāsaparvatam //
1.61.d:
ततः पित्रा समागम्य प्रणम्य च महामुनिः ।
शुकः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ययौ कैलासपर्वतम् ॥
1.61.m: Then, having met his father and bowed to him, the great sage / Śuka circumambulated him and went to Mount Kailāsa.

1.61.s:
vyāsastadvirahāddūnaḥ putrasnehasamāvṛtaḥ /
kṣaṇaikaṃ sthīyatāṃ putra iti ca krośa durmanāḥ //
1.61.d:
व्यासस्तद्विरहाद्दूनः पुत्रस्नेहसमावृतः ।
क्षणैकं स्थीयतां पुत्र इति च क्रोश दुर्मनाः ॥
1.61.m: Vyāsa, distressed by separation from him and overcome with affection for his son, / cried out, dejected in mind: "Stay for a single moment, my son!"

1.61.s:
nirapekṣaḥ śuko bhūtvā niḥsneho muktabandhanaḥ /
mokṣamevānusaṃcitya gata eva paraṃ padam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde ekaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.61.d:
निरपेक्षः शुको भूत्वा निःस्नेहो मुक्तबन्धनः ।
मोक्षमेवानुसंचित्य गत एव परं पदम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे एकषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
1.61.m:
Becoming detached, free of affection, his bonds severed, / meditating only upon liberation, Śuka went indeed to the supreme abode.

Thus ends the sixty-first chapter in the Second Quarter of the Great Narrative in the First Part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.62.s:
sūta uvāca
etacchrṛtvā tu vacanaṃ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ /
punaḥ papraccha taṃ vipra śukābhipatanaṃ munim //
1.62.d:
सूत उवाच
एतच्छ्रृत्वा तु वचनं नारदो भगवानृषिः ।
पुनः पप्रच्छ तं विप्र शुकाभिपतनं मुनिम् ॥
1.62.m: Sūta said: / Hearing this speech, the lordly sage Nārada / questioned that muni once again, O brāhmaṇa, concerning Śuka's flight.

1.62.s:
nārada uvāca
bhagavansarvamākhyātaṃ tvayātikaruṇātmanā /
yacchrṛtvā mānasaṃ me 'dya śāntimagryāmupāgatam //
1.62.d:
नारद उवाच
भगवन्सर्वमाख्यातं त्वयातिकरुणात्मना ।
यच्छ्रृत्वा मानसं मे ऽद्य शान्तिमग्र्यामुपागतम् ॥
1.62.m: Nārada said: / O lord, everything has been related by you, whose nature is exceedingly compassionate; / hearing this today, my mind has attained supreme peace.

1.62.s:
punaśca mokṣaśāstraṃ me tvamādiśa mahāmune /
nahi sampūrṇatāmeti tṛṣṇā kṛṣṇaguṇārṇave //
1.62.d:
पुनश्च मोक्षशास्त्रं मे त्वमादिश महामुने ।
नहि सम्पूर्णतामेति तृष्णा कृष्णगुणार्णवे ॥
1.62.m: Teach me once again, O great sage, the treatise on liberation; / thirst never reaches fulfillment in the ocean of Kṛṣṇa's virtues.

1.62.s:
ye tu saṃsāranirmuktā mokṣa śāstraparāyaṇāḥ /
kutra te nivasaṃtīha saṃśayo me mahānayam //
1.62.d:
ये तु संसारनिर्मुक्ता मोक्ष शास्त्रपरायणाः ।
कुत्र ते निवसंतीह संशयो मे महानयम् ॥
1.62.m: Those who are released from saṃsāra and dedicated to the scripture of liberation, / where do they dwell here? This is my great doubt.

1.62.s:
taṃ chindhi sumahābhāgatvatto nānyo vidāṃvaraḥ /
sanaṃ.u
dhārayāmāsa cātmānaṃ yathāśāstraṃ mahāmuniḥ //
1.62.d:
तं छिन्धि सुमहाभागत्वत्तो नान्यो विदांवरः ।
सनं।उ
धारयामास चात्मानं यथाशास्त्रं महामुनिः ॥
1.62.m: Cut through it, O highly fortunate one; none other is best among the knowers than you. / Sanatkumāra said: / The great sage held his self [in meditation] according to the sacred precepts,

1.62.s:
pādātprabhṛti gātreṣu krameṇa kramayogavit /
tataḥ sa prāṅmukho vidvānādityena virocite //
1.62.d:
पादात्प्रभृति गात्रेषु क्रमेण क्रमयोगवित् ।
ततः स प्राङ्मुखो विद्वानादित्येन विरोचिते ॥
1.62.m: beginning from the feet through the limbs in succession, knowing the successive yoga. / Then, facing east, that wise one, in [the spot] illuminated by the sun,

1.62.s:
pāṇipādaṃ samādhāya vinītavadupāviśat /
na tatra pakṣisaṃghāto na śabdo na ca darśanam //
1.62.d:
पाणिपादं समाधाय विनीतवदुपाविशत् ।
न तत्र पक्षिसंघातो न शब्दो न च दर्शनम् ॥
1.62.m: composed his hands and feet and sat down like one disciplined. / There was no flock of birds there, no sound, and no sight,

1.62.s:
yatra vaiyāsakirddhāmni yoktuṃ samupacakrame /
sa dadarśa tadātmānaṃ sarvasaṃgaviniḥsṛtaḥ //
1.62.d:
यत्र वैयासकिर्द्धाम्नि योक्तुं समुपचक्रमे ।
स ददर्श तदात्मानं सर्वसंगविनिःसृतः ॥
1.62.m: where the son of Vyāsa in his radiant abode undertook to practice yoga. / Then, freed from all attachments, he beheld the Self.

1.62.s:
prajahāsa tato hāsaṃ śukaḥ samprekṣya bhāskaram /
sa punaryogamāsthāya mokṣamārgopalabdhaye //
1.62.d:
प्रजहास ततो हासं शुकः सम्प्रेक्ष्य भास्करम् ।
स पुनर्योगमास्थाय मोक्षमार्गोपलब्धये ॥
1.62.m: Then Śuka laughed a laugh, gazing upon the sun; / once more having resorted to yoga for the attainment of the path of liberation,

1.62.s:
mahāyogīśvaro bhūtvā so 'tyakrāmadvihāyasam /
antarīkṣacaraḥ śrīmānvyāsaputraḥ suniścitaḥ //
1.62.d:
महायोगीश्वरो भूत्वा सो ऽत्यक्रामद्विहायसम् ।
अन्तरीक्षचरः श्रीमान्व्यासपुत्रः सुनिश्चितः ॥
1.62.m: becoming a master of great yoga, he crossed beyond the sky. / Moving through the atmosphere, the glorious son of Vyāsa was firmly resolved.

1.62.s:
tamundyantaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ vainateyasamadyutim /
dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni manomārutaraṃhasam //
1.62.d:
तमुन्द्यन्तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं वैनतेयसमद्युतिम् ।
ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि मनोमारुतरंहसम् ॥
1.62.m: All beings beheld that best of the twice-born ascending, / having a splendor equal to the son of Vinatā, with the speed of mind and wind.

1.62.s:
yathāśakti yathānyāyaṃ pūjayāñcakrire tathā /
puṣpa varṣaiśca divyaistamavacakrurdivaukasaḥ //
1.62.d:
यथाशक्ति यथान्यायं पूजयाञ्चक्रिरे तथा ।
पुष्प वर्षैश्च दिव्यैस्तमवचक्रुर्दिवौकसः ॥
1.62.m: According to their ability and according to propriety, they worshipped him thus, / and the denizens of heaven showered him with celestial showers of flowers.

1.62.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāḥ sarve gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ /
ṛṣayaścaiva saṃsiddhāḥ ko 'yaṃ siddhimupāgataḥ //
1.62.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताः सर्वे गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ।
ऋषयश्चैव संसिद्धाः को ऽयं सिद्धिमुपागतः ॥
1.62.m: Seeing him, all the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases were astonished, / as well as the accomplished sages: “Who is this that has attained perfection?”

1.62.s:
tato 'sau svāhrayaṃ tebhyaḥ kathayāmāsa nārada /
uvāca ca mahātejāstānṛṣīnsaṃpraharṣitaḥ //
1.62.d:
ततो ऽसौ स्वाह्रयं तेभ्यः कथयामास नारद ।
उवाच च महातेजास्तानृषीन्संप्रहर्षितः ॥
1.62.m: Then he proclaimed his own name to them, O Nārada, / and, possessing great splendor, addressed those sages, fully delighted:

1.62.s:
pitā yadyanugacchenmāṃ krośamānaḥ śuketi vai /
tasmai prativacodeyaṃ bhavadbhistu samāhitaiḥ //
1.62.d:
पिता यद्यनुगच्छेन्मां क्रोशमानः शुकेति वै ।
तस्मै प्रतिवचोदेयं भवद्भिस्तु समाहितैः ॥
1.62.m: “If my father should follow me, crying out indeed, ‘O Śuka!’, / an answer should be given to him by you with composed minds.”

1.62.s:
bāḍhamuktastatastaistu lokānhitvā caturvidhān /
tamo hyaṣṭavidhaṃ tyaktvā jahau pañcavidhaṃ rajaḥ //
1.62.d:
बाढमुक्तस्ततस्तैस्तु लोकान्हित्वा चतुर्विधान् ।
तमो ह्यष्टविधं त्यक्त्वा जहौ पञ्चविधं रजः ॥
1.62.m: Being told “Certainly” by them, having abandoned the four types of worlds, / having cast off the eightfold darkness, he discarded the fivefold passion.

1.62.s:
tataḥ satvaṃ jahau dhīmāṃstadadbhutamivābhavat /
tatastasminpade nitye nirguṇe liṅgapūjite //
1.62.d:
ततः सत्वं जहौ धीमांस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ।
ततस्तस्मिन्पदे नित्ये निर्गुणे लिङ्गपूजिते ॥
1.62.m: Then the wise one discarded purity; that was like a wonder. / Then, in that eternal, attributeless realm worshipped by the signs—

1.62.s:
tataḥ sa śṛṅge 'pratime himavanmerusannibhe /
saṃśliṣṭe śvetapīte ca rukmarūpyamaye śubhe //
1.62.d:
ततः स शृङ्गे ऽप्रतिमे हिमवन्मेरुसन्निभे ।
संश्लिष्टे श्वेतपीते च रुक्मरूप्यमये शुभे ॥
1.62.m: then he, [facing] the two peerless peaks resembling the Himālaya and Meru, / joined together, white and yellow, auspicious, composed of gold and silver,

1.62.s:
śatayojanavistāre tiryāgūrddhca nārada /
so 'viśaṅkena manasā tathaivābhyapatacchukaḥ //
1.62.d:
शतयोजनविस्तारे तिर्यागूर्द्ध्च नारद ।
सो ऽविशङ्केन मनसा तथैवाभ्यपतच्छुकः ॥
1.62.m: a hundred yojanas in extent across and upwards, O Nārada, / Śuka flew straight against them with a fearless mind.

1.62.s:
te śṛṅge 'tyantasaṃśliṣṭe sahasaiva dvidhākṛte /
adṛśyetāṃ dvijaśreṣṭha tadadbhutamivābhavat //
1.62.d:
ते शृङ्गे ऽत्यन्तसंश्लिष्टे सहसैव द्विधाकृते ।
अदृश्येतां द्विजश्रेष्ठ तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥
1.62.m: Those two peaks, tightly conjoined, were suddenly split in two; / they were seen [so], O best of the twice-born; that was like a wonder.

1.62.s:
tataḥ parvataśṛṅgābhyāṃ sahasaiva viniḥsṛtaḥ /
na ca pratijaghānāsya sa gatiṃ parvatottamaḥ //
1.62.d:
ततः पर्वतशृङ्गाभ्यां सहसैव विनिःसृतः ।
न च प्रतिजघानास्य स गतिं पर्वतोत्तमः ॥
1.62.m: Then, having suddenly issued from the two mountain peaks, / that best of mountains did not obstruct his path.

1.62.s:
tato mandākinīṃ divyā mupariṣṭādabhivrajan /
śuko dadarśa dharmātmā puṣpitadrumakānanam //
1.62.d:
ततो मन्दाकिनीं दिव्या मुपरिष्टादभिव्रजन् ।
शुको ददर्श धर्मात्मा पुष्पितद्रुमकाननम् ॥
1.62.m: Then, proceeding above the celestial Mandākinī, / the righteous Śuka saw a grove of flowering trees.

1.62.s:
tasyāṃ krīḍāsu niratāḥ snānti caivāpsarogaṇāḥ /
nirākāraṃ tu sākārādadṛśustaṃ vivāsasaḥ //
1.62.d:
तस्यां क्रीडासु निरताः स्नान्ति चैवाप्सरोगणाः ।
निराकारं तु साकाराददृशुस्तं विवाससः ॥
1.62.m: In it, devoted to amusements, the hosts of apsarases were bathing; / they, possessing forms and naked, beheld him who was formless.

1.62.s:
taṃ prakramantamājñāya pitā snehasamanvitaḥ /
uttamāṃ gatimāsthāya pṛṣṭato 'nusasāra ha //
1.62.d:
तं प्रक्रमन्तमाज्ञाय पिता स्नेहसमन्वितः ।
उत्तमां गतिमास्थाय पृष्टतो ऽनुससार ह ॥
1.62.m: Knowing that he was departing, his father, filled with affection, / resorting to an excellent course, followed behind.

1.62.s:
śukastu mārutādūrddhvaṃ gatiṃ kṛtvāṃ tarikṣagām /
darśayitvā prabhāvaṃ svaṃ sarvabhūto 'bhavattadā //
1.62.d:
शुकस्तु मारुतादूर्द्ध्वं गतिं कृत्वां तरिक्षगाम् ।
दर्शयित्वा प्रभावं स्वं सर्वभूतो ऽभवत्तदा ॥
1.62.m: Śuka, however, taking a path moving through the sky above the wind, / having displayed his power, then became the self of all beings.

1.62.s:
atha yogagatiṃ vyāsaḥ samāsthāya mahātapāḥ /
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa śukābhipatanaṃ yayau //
1.62.d:
अथ योगगतिं व्यासः समास्थाय महातपाः ।
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण शुकाभिपतनं ययौ ॥
1.62.m: Then Vyāsa of great austerities, resorting to the course of yoga, / went in the mere interval of a twinkling of an eye to Śuka's place of ascent.

1.62.s:
sa dadarśa dvidhā kṛtvā parvatāgraṃ gataṃ śukam /
śaśaṃsurmunayaḥ siddhā gatiṃ tasmai sutasya tām //
1.62.d:
स ददर्श द्विधा कृत्वा पर्वताग्रं गतं शुकम् ।
शशंसुर्मुनयः सिद्धा गतिं तस्मै सुतस्य ताम् ॥
1.62.m: He saw that Śuka had gone, having split the mountain crest in two; / the perfected sages declared that course of his son to him.

1.62.s:
tataḥ śuketiśabdena dīrgheṇa kranditaṃ tadāḥ /
svayaṃ pitrā svareṇoñcaistrīṃllokānanunādya vai //
1.62.d:
ततः शुकेतिशब्देन दीर्घेण क्रन्दितं तदाः ।
स्वयं पित्रा स्वरेणोञ्चैस्त्रींल्लोकाननुनाद्य वै ॥
1.62.m: Then, with the long cry “O Śuka!”, a weeping was made then / by the father himself with a loud voice, making the three worlds resound.

1.62.s:
śukaḥ sarvagatirbhūtvā sarvātmā sarvatomukhaḥ /
pratyabhāṣata dharmātmā bhoḥ śabdenānunādayan //
1.62.d:
शुकः सर्वगतिर्भूत्वा सर्वात्मा सर्वतोमुखः ।
प्रत्यभाषत धर्मात्मा भोः शब्देनानुनादयन् ॥
1.62.m: Śuka, having become the goal of all, the self of all, facing everywhere, / the righteous one answered, making [the worlds] resound with the sound “bhoḥ”.

1.62.s:
tata ekākṣaraṃ nādaṃ bhorityevamudīrayan /
pratyāharajjagatsarvamuñcaiḥ sthāvarajaṅgamam //
1.62.d:
तत एकाक्षरं नादं भोरित्येवमुदीरयन् ।
प्रत्याहरज्जगत्सर्वमुञ्चैः स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
1.62.m: Then, uttering that single-syllable sound, “bhoḥ!”, / the entire universe, moving and unmoving, echoed loudly in return.

1.62.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti vādyāpi śabdānuñcāritānpṛthak /
girigahvarapṛṣṭeṣu vyājahāra śukaṃ prati //
1.62.d:
ततः प्रभृति वाद्यापि शब्दानुञ्चारितान्पृथक् ।
गिरिगह्वरपृष्टेषु व्याजहार शुकं प्रति ॥
1.62.m: From that time onwards, even today, the separate uttered sounds / in mountain caves and mountain ridges reply in response to Śuka.

1.62.s:
antarhitaprabhāvaṃ taṃ darśayitvā śukastadā /
guṇānsaṃtyajya sattvādīnpadamadhyagamatparam //
1.62.d:
अन्तर्हितप्रभावं तं दर्शयित्वा शुकस्तदा ।
गुणान्संत्यज्य सत्त्वादीन्पदमध्यगमत्परम् ॥
1.62.m: Having shown that hidden power, Śuka then, / having discarded the qualities such as sattva, attained the supreme abode.

1.62.s:
mahimānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā putrasyāmitatejasaḥ /
so 'nunīto bhagavatā vyāso rudreṇa nārada //
1.62.d:
महिमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रस्यामिततेजसः ।
सो ऽनुनीतो भगवता व्यासो रुद्रेण नारद ॥
1.62.m: Seeing that greatness of his son of boundless splendor, / that Vyāsa was consoled, O Nārada, by the lord Rudra:

1.62.s:
kimu tvaṃ tāmyasi mune putraṃ prati samākulaḥ /
paśyasi vipra nāyāntaṃ brahmabhūtaṃ nijāntire //
1.62.d:
किमु त्वं ताम्यसि मुने पुत्रं प्रति समाकुलः ।
पश्यसि विप्र नायान्तं ब्रह्मभूतं निजान्तिरे ॥
1.62.m: “Why do you grieve, O sage, agitated on account of your son? / Do you not see, O brāhmaṇa, that he who has become Brahman is not returning, [though] within yourself?”

1.62.s:
ityevamanunīto 'sau vyāsaḥ punaruprāvrajat /
śvāśramaṃ sa śuko brahmabhūto lokāṃścacāra ha //
1.62.d:
इत्येवमनुनीतो ऽसौ व्यासः पुनरुप्राव्रजत् ।
श्वाश्रमं स शुको ब्रह्मभूतो लोकांश्चचार ह ॥
1.62.m: Consoled in this manner, that Vyāsa returned / to his own hermitage, while that Śuka, having become Brahman, roamed the worlds.

1.62.s:
tata kālāntare brahmanvyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ /
naranārāyaṇau draṣṭuṃ yayau badarikāśramam //
1.62.d:
तत कालान्तरे ब्रह्मन्व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः ।
नरनारायणौ द्रष्टुं ययौ बदरिकाश्रमम् ॥
1.62.m: Then, in the course of time, O brāhmaṇa, Vyāsa the son of Satyavatī / went to Badarikāśrama to see Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

1.62.s:
tatra dṛṣṭvā tu tau devau tapyamāno mahattapaḥ /
svayaṃ ca tatra tapasi sthitaḥ śukamanusmaran //
1.62.d:
तत्र दृष्ट्वा तु तौ देवौ तप्यमानो महत्तपः ।
स्वयं च तत्र तपसि स्थितः शुकमनुस्मरन् ॥
1.62.m: Seeing those two gods there, practicing great austerities, / he himself remained there in asceticism, remembering Śuka.

1.62.s:
yāvattatra sthito vyāsaḥ śukaḥ paramayogavit /
śvetadvīpaṃ gatastāta yatra tvamagamaḥ purā //
1.62.d:
यावत्तत्र स्थितो व्यासः शुकः परमयोगवित् ।
श्वेतद्वीपं गतस्तात यत्र त्वमगमः पुरा ॥
1.62.m: While Vyāsa remained there, Śuka, the knower of supreme yoga, / went to Śvetadvīpa, dear one, where you had gone of old.

1.62.s:
tatra dṛṣṭaprabhāvastu śrīmānnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ /
dṛṣṭaḥ śrutivimṛgyo hi devadevo janārdanaḥ //
1.62.d:
तत्र दृष्टप्रभावस्तु श्रीमान्नारायणः प्रभुः ।
दृष्टः श्रुतिविमृग्यो हि देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
1.62.m: There, the glorious Lord Nārāyaṇa, whose power was witnessed, / was seen—the god of gods, Janārdana, who is sought by the Vedic scriptures.

1.62.s:
stutaśca śukadevena prasannaḥ prāha nārada /
śrībhagavānuvāca
tvayā dṛṣṭo 'smi yogīndra sarvadevarahaḥsthitaḥ //
1.62.d:
स्तुतश्च शुकदेवेन प्रसन्नः प्राह नारद ।
श्रीभगवानुवाच
त्वया दृष्टो ऽस्मि योगीन्द्र सर्वदेवरहःस्थितः ॥
1.62.m: Praised by Śukadeva, being pleased, he said, O Nārada: / The Holy Lord said: / “I have been seen by you, O lord of yogins, I who dwell in secret from all gods.

1.62.s:
sanatkumārādiṣṭena siddho yogena vāḍava /
tvaṃ sadāgatimārgastho lokānpaśya yathecchayā //
1.62.d:
सनत्कुमारादिष्टेन सिद्धो योगेन वाडव ।
त्वं सदागतिमार्गस्थो लोकान्पश्य यथेच्छया ॥
1.62.m: You have become perfected through the yoga instructed by Sanatkumāra, O brāhmaṇa; / standing on the path of the wind, behold the worlds as you please.”

1.62.s:
ityukto vāsudevena taṃ natvāraṇisaṃbhavaḥ /
vaikuṇṭhaṃ prayayau vipra sarvalokanamaskṛtam //
1.62.d:
इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन तं नत्वारणिसंभवः ।
वैकुण्ठं प्रययौ विप्र सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् ॥
1.62.m: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, bowing to him, the one born from the fire-kindling stick / set out for Vaikuṇṭha, O brāhmaṇa, which is worshipped by all the worlds,

1.62.s:
vaimānikaiḥ surairjuṣṭaṃ virajāpariceṣṭitam /
yaṃ bhāntamanubhāntyete lokāḥ sarve 'pi nārada //
1.62.d:
वैमानिकैः सुरैर्जुष्टं विरजापरिचेष्टितम् ।
यं भान्तमनुभान्त्येते लोकाः सर्वे ऽपि नारद ॥
1.62.m: served by gods in celestial chariots, surrounded by the Virajā, / in whose shining all these worlds shine after, O Nārada;

1.62.s:
yatra vidumasopānāḥ svarṇaratnavicitritāḥ /
vāpya utpalaṃsaṃchannāḥ surastrīkrīḍanākulāḥ //
1.62.d:
यत्र विदुमसोपानाः स्वर्णरत्नविचित्रिताः ।
वाप्य उत्पलंसंछन्नाः सुरस्त्रीक्रीडनाकुलाः ॥
1.62.m: where there are coral steps variegated with gold and gems, / ponds covered with blue lotuses and crowded with the sports of celestial women,

1.62.s:
divyairhaṃsakulairghuṣṭāḥ svacchāṃbunibhṛtāḥ sadā /
tatra dvāḥsthaiścaturhastenārnābharaṇabhūṣitaiḥ //
1.62.d:
दिव्यैर्हंसकुलैर्घुष्टाः स्वच्छांबुनिभृताः सदा ।
तत्र द्वाःस्थैश्चतुर्हस्तेनार्नाभरणभूषितैः ॥
1.62.m: resounded by flocks of heavenly swans, always filled with clear water. / There, by the four-armed gatekeepers adorned with various ornaments,

1.62.s:
viṣvaksenānugaiḥ siddhaiḥ kumudādyairavā ritaḥ /
praviśyābhyāntaraṃ tatra devadevaṃ caturbhujam //
1.62.d:
विष्वक्सेनानुगैः सिद्धैः कुमुदाद्यैरवा रितः ।
प्रविश्याभ्यान्तरं तत्र देवदेवं चतुर्भुजम् ॥
1.62.m: the perfected followers of Viṣvaksena such as Kumuda and others, unimpeded, / entering inside, [he saw] there the four-armed god of gods,

1.62.s:
śāntaṃ prasannavadanaṃ pītakauśeyavāsasam /
śaṅkhacakragadāpadmairmūrtimadbhirupāsitam //
1.62.d:
शान्तं प्रसन्नवदनं पीतकौशेयवाससम् ।
शङ्खचक्रगदापद्मैर्मूर्तिमद्भिरुपासितम् ॥
1.62.m: peaceful, with a cheerful face, clad in yellow silk, / served by his conch, discus, mace, and lotus in personified forms.

1.62.s:
vakṣasthalasthayā lakṣmyā kaustubhena virājitam /
kaṭīsūtrabrahmasūtrakaṭakāṅgadabhūṣitam //
1.62.d:
वक्षस्थलस्थया लक्ष्म्या कौस्तुभेन विराजितम् ।
कटीसूत्रब्रह्मसूत्रकटकाङ्गदभूषितम् ॥
1.62.m: resplendent with Lakṣmī resting upon his chest and with the Kaustubha jewel, / adorned with a waist-cord, sacred thread, bracelets, and armlets,

1.62.s:
bhrājatkirīṭavalayaṃ maṇinūpuraśobhitam /
dadarśa siddhani karaiḥ sevyamānamaharniśam //
1.62.d:
भ्राजत्किरीटवलयं मणिनूपुरशोभितम् ।
ददर्श सिद्धनि करैः सेव्यमानमहर्निशम् ॥
1.62.m: wearing a radiant crown and wristlets, adorned with gemmed anklets; / he saw him being served day and night by hosts of Siddhas.

1.62.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktibhāvena tuṣṭāva madhusūdanam /
śuka uvāca
namaste vāsudevāya sarvalokaikasākṣiṇe //
1.62.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा भक्तिभावेन तुष्टाव मधुसूदनम् ।
शुक उवाच
नमस्ते वासुदेवाय सर्वलोकैकसाक्षिणे ॥
1.62.m: Having seen him, he praised Madhusūdana with devotion: / Śuka said: / "Obeisance to you, Vāsudeva, sole witness of all worlds,

1.62.s:
jagadbījasvarūpāya pūrṇāya nibhṛtātmane /
haraye vāsukisthāya śvetadvīpanivāsine //
1.62.d:
जगद्बीजस्वरूपाय पूर्णाय निभृतात्मने ।
हरये वासुकिस्थाय श्वेतद्वीपनिवासिने ॥
1.62.m: whose essential nature is the seed of the universe, complete, composed of self, / to Hari who rests upon Vāsuki, dweller in Śvetadvīpa!

1.62.s:
haṃsāya matsyarūpāya vārāhatanudhāriṇe /
nṛsiṃhāya dhruvejyāya sāṃkhyayogeśvarāya ca //
1.62.d:
हंसाय मत्स्यरूपाय वाराहतनुधारिणे ।
नृसिंहाय ध्रुवेज्याय सांख्ययोगेश्वराय च ॥
1.62.m: To Haṃsa, to him whose form is the Fish, who bears the boar's body, / to Nṛsiṃha, to him who is constantly worshipped, and master of Sāṅkhya and Yoga!

1.62.s:
catuḥsanāya kūrmāya pṛthave svasuravātmane /
nābheyāya jagaddhātre vidhātreṃ'takāraya ca //
1.62.d:
चतुःसनाय कूर्माय पृथवे स्वसुरवात्मने ।
नाभेयाय जगद्धात्रे विधात्रेंऽतकारय च ॥
1.62.m: To the four Sanas, to Kūrma, to Pṛthu, the self-existent spirit, / to the son of Nābhi, sustainer of the world, creator, and bringer of the end!

1.62.s:
bhārgavendrāya rāmāya rāghavāya parāya ca /
kṛṣṇāya vedakartre ca buddhakalkisvarūpiṇe //
1.62.d:
भार्गवेन्द्राय रामाय राघवाय पराय च ।
कृष्णाय वेदकर्त्रे च बुद्धकल्किस्वरूपिणे ॥
1.62.m: To the foremost descendant of Bhṛgu, to Rāma, to Rāghava, and to the Supreme, / to Kṛṣṇa, creator of the Vedas, having the forms of Buddha and Kalkin!

1.62.s:
caturvyuhāya vedyāya dhyeyāya paramātmane /
naranārāyaṇākhyāya śiṣiviṣṭāya viṣṇave //
1.62.d:
चतुर्व्युहाय वेद्याय ध्येयाय परमात्मने ।
नरनारायणाख्याय शिषिविष्टाय विष्णवे ॥
1.62.m: To him of fourfold manifestation, to be known, to be meditated upon, the Supreme Self, / known as Nara-Nārāyaṇa, to Śipiviṣṭa, to Viṣṇu!

1.62.s:
ṛtadhāmne vidhāmne ca suparṇāya svarociṣe /
ṛbhave suvratākhyāya sudhāmne cājitāya ca //
1.62.d:
ऋतधाम्ने विधाम्ने च सुपर्णाय स्वरोचिषे ।
ऋभवे सुव्रताख्याय सुधाम्ने चाजिताय च ॥
1.62.m: To him whose abode is truth, whose abode is manifold, to Suparṇa, self-luminous, / to Ṛbhu, named Suvrata, Sudhāman, and the unconquered Ajita!

1.62.s:
viśvarūpāya viśvāya sṛṣṭisthityantakāriṇe /
yajñāya yajñabhokte ca sthaviṣṭhāyāṇave 'rthine //
1.62.d:
विश्वरूपाय विश्वाय सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तकारिणे ।
यज्ञाय यज्ञभोक्ते च स्थविष्ठायाणवे ऽर्थिने ॥
1.62.m: To him whose form is all, to the universe, author of creation, maintenance, and destruction, / to the sacrifice, the enjoyer of sacrifice, the grossest, the subtlest, the seeker!

1.62.s:
ādityasomanetrāya sahaojobalāya ca /
ījyāya sākṣiṇe 'jāyabahuśīrṣāṅghribāhave //
1.62.d:
आदित्यसोमनेत्राय सहओजोबलाय च ।
ईज्याय साक्षिणे ऽजायबहुशीर्षाङ्घ्रिबाहवे ॥
1.62.m: To him whose eyes are sun and moon, possessing endurance, strength, and power, / worthy of worship, the witness, unborn, having many heads, feet, and arms!

1.62.s:
śrīśāya śrīnivāsāya bhaktavaśyāya śārṅgiṇe /
aṣṭaprakṛtyadhīśāya brahmaṇe 'nantasaktaye //
1.62.d:
श्रीशाय श्रीनिवासाय भक्तवश्याय शार्ङ्गिणे ।
अष्टप्रकृत्यधीशाय ब्रह्मणे ऽनन्तसक्तये ॥
1.62.m: To the Lord of Śrī, abode of Śrī, conquered by devotion, wielder of the bow Śārṅga, / sovereign of the eightfold material nature, to Brahman of infinite power!

1.62.s:
bṛhadāraṇyavedyāya hṛṣīkeśāya vedhase /
puṇḍarīkanibhākṣāya kṣetrajñāya vibhāsine //
1.62.d:
बृहदारण्यवेद्याय हृषीकेशाय वेधसे ।
पुण्डरीकनिभाक्षाय क्षेत्रज्ञाय विभासिने ॥
1.62.m: To him known through the Bṛhadāraṇyaka, to Hṛṣīkeśa, to the Ordainer, / whose eyes resemble lotuses, the knower of the field, the radiant one!

1.62.s:
govindāya jagatkartre jagannāthāya yogine /
satyāya satyasaṃdhāya vaikuṇṭhāyācyutāya ca //
1.62.d:
गोविन्दाय जगत्कर्त्रे जगन्नाथाय योगिने ।
सत्याय सत्यसंधाय वैकुण्ठायाच्युताय च ॥
1.62.m: To Govinda, maker of the universe, lord of the universe, yogin, / truth, true to his promise, to Vaikuṇṭha, and to Acyuta!

1.62.s:
adhokṣajāya dharmāya vāmanāya tridhātave /
ghṛtārciṣe viṣṇave te 'nantāya kapilāyaya ca //
1.62.d:
अधोक्षजाय धर्माय वामनाय त्रिधातवे ।
घृतार्चिषे विष्णवे ते ऽनन्ताय कपिलायय च ॥
1.62.m: To Adhokṣaja, to Dharma, to Vāmana, to the threefold element, / whose rays are butter, to Viṣṇu, to infinite Kapila!

1.62.s:
viriñcaye trikakude ṛgyajuḥsāmarūpiṇe /
ekaśṛṅgāya ca śuciśravase śāstrayonaye //
1.62.d:
विरिञ्चये त्रिककुदे ऋग्यजुःसामरूपिणे ।
एकशृङ्गाय च शुचिश्रवसे शास्त्रयोनये ॥
1.62.m: To Viriñci, three-crested, embodied as Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman, / to the one-horned, of pure fame, the source of sacred teachings!

1.62.s:
vṛṣākapaya ṛddhāya prabhave viśvakarmaṇe /
bhūrbhuvuḥsvaḥsvarūpāya daityaghne nirguṇāya ca //
1.62.d:
वृषाकपय ऋद्धाय प्रभवे विश्वकर्मणे ।
भूर्भुवुःस्वःस्वरूपाय दैत्यघ्ने निर्गुणाय च ॥
1.62.m: To Vṛṣākapi, prosperous, powerful, Viśvakarman, / whose nature is earth, atmosphere, and heaven, slayer of Daityas, beyond qualities!

1.62.s:
nirañjanāya nityāya hyavyayāyākṣarāya ca /
namaste pāhi māmīśa śaraṇāgatavatsala //
1.62.d:
निरञ्जनाय नित्याय ह्यव्ययायाक्षराय च ।
नमस्ते पाहि मामीश शरणागतवत्सल ॥
1.62.m: To the untainted, eternal, imperishable, and immutable! / Obeisance to you! Protect me, O Lord, compassionate to those seeking refuge!"

1.62.s:
iti stutaḥ sa bhagavāñcchaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
āraṇeyamuvācedaṃ bhṛśaṃ praṇatavatsalaḥ //
1.62.d:
इति स्तुतः स भगवाञ्च्छङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ।
आरणेयमुवाचेदं भृशं प्रणतवत्सलः ॥
1.62.m: Thus praised, the Blessed One, holding conch, discus, and mace, / deeply affectionate to the bowed, spoke thus to the son of Araṇī:

1.62.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
vyāsaputra mahābhāga prīto 'smi tava suvrata /
vidyāmāpnuhi bhaktiṃ ca jñānī tvaṃ mama rūpadhṛk //
1.62.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
व्यासपुत्र महाभाग प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव सुव्रत ।
विद्यामाप्नुहि भक्तिं च ज्ञानी त्वं मम रूपधृक् ॥
1.62.m: The Blessed One said: / "O son of Vyāsa, highly fortunate, faithful to vows, I am pleased with you; / obtain knowledge and devotion; you are a sage bearing my form.

1.62.s:
yadrūpaṃ mama dṛṣṭaṃ prāk śvetadvīpe tvayā dvija /
so 'hamevāvatārārthaṃ sthito viśvaṃbharātmakaḥ //
1.62.d:
यद्रूपं मम दृष्टं प्राक् श्वेतद्वीपे त्वया द्विज ।
सो ऽहमेवावतारार्थं स्थितो विश्वंभरात्मकः ॥
1.62.m: The form of mine that was seen formerly by you in Śvetadvīpa, O twice-born, / that very one am I, abiding as the sustainer of the world for the sake of incarnation.

1.62.s:
siddho 'si tvaṃ mahābhāga mokṣadharmānunucintayā /
varalokānyathā vāyuryathā ravaṃ savitā tathā //
1.62.d:
सिद्धो ऽसि त्वं महाभाग मोक्षधर्मानुनुचिन्तया ।
वरलोकान्यथा वायुर्यथा रवं सविता तथा ॥
1.62.m: You are perfected, O highly fortunate one, through meditation on the duties of liberation, / moving through the excellent worlds like the wind, as the sun moves through space.

1.62.s:
nityamuktasvarūpastvaṃ pūjyamānaḥ surairnaraiḥ /
bhaktirhi durlabhā loke mayi sarvaparāyaṇe //
1.62.d:
नित्यमुक्तस्वरूपस्त्वं पूज्यमानः सुरैर्नरैः ।
भक्तिर्हि दुर्लभा लोके मयि सर्वपरायणे ॥
1.62.m: Your nature is ever-liberated, worshipped by gods and men; / devotion indeed is rare in the world toward me, the supreme refuge of all.

1.62.s:
tāṃ labdhvā nāparaṃ kiñcillabdhavyamavaśiṣyate /
ākalpāntaḥ tapaḥ saṃsthau naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī //
1.62.d:
तां लब्ध्वा नापरं किञ्चिल्लब्धव्यमवशिष्यते ।
आकल्पान्तः तपः संस्थौ नरनारायणावृषी ॥
1.62.m: Having obtained it, nothing else remains to be attained; / abiding in austerity until the end of the aeon are the two ṛṣis, Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

1.62.s:
tayornideśato vyāso janaka stava suvrataḥ /
kartā bhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ tadadhīṣva bhuvaṃ vraja //
1.62.d:
तयोर्निदेशतो व्यासो जनक स्तव सुव्रतः ।
कर्ता भागवतं शास्त्रं तदधीष्व भुवं व्रज ॥
1.62.m: By their command, your father Vyāsa, faithful to vows, / will compose the Bhāgavata scripture; study that and go to earth.

1.62.s:
sa tapyati tapastvadya parvate gandhamādane /
tvadviyogena khinnātmā taṃ prasādaya matpriyam //
1.62.d:
स तप्यति तपस्त्वद्य पर्वते गन्धमादने ।
त्वद्वियोगेन खिन्नात्मा तं प्रसादय मत्प्रियम् ॥
1.62.m: He now performs austerity on Mount Gandhamādana, / dejected in heart through separation from you; propitiate him who is dear to me."

1.62.s:
evamuktaḥ śuko vipra namaskṛtya caturbhujam /
yathāgataṃ nivṛtto 'sau piturantikamāgamat //
1.62.d:
एवमुक्तः शुको विप्र नमस्कृत्य चतुर्भुजम् ।
यथागतं निवृत्तो ऽसौ पितुरन्तिकमागमत् ॥
1.62.m: Thus addressed, O brāhmaṇa, Śuka bowed to the four-armed [Lord], / and returning the way he had come, went into the presence of his father.

1.62.s:
atha taṃ svantike dṛṣṭvā pārāśaryyaḥ pratāpavān /
putraṃ prāpya prahṛṣṭātmā tapaso nivavarta ha //
1.62.d:
अथ तं स्वन्तिके दृष्ट्वा पाराशर्य्यः प्रतापवान् ।
पुत्रं प्राप्य प्रहृष्टात्मा तपसो निववर्त ह ॥
1.62.m: Then, seeing him near him, the glorious son of Parāśara, / rejoiced in heart on regaining his son, ceased from his austerity.

1.62.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam /
āraṇeyasamāyuktaḥ svāśramaṃ samupāgamat //
1.62.d:
नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम् ।
आरणेयसमायुक्तः स्वाश्रमं समुपागमत् ॥
1.62.m: Having bowed to Nārāyaṇa and to Nara, best of men, / accompanied by the son of Araṇī, he came to his own hermitage.

1.62.s:
nārāyaṇaniyogāttu tvanmukhena munīśvara /
cakāra saṃhitāṃ divyāṃ nānākhyānasamanvitām //
1.62.d:
नारायणनियोगात्तु त्वन्मुखेन मुनीश्वर ।
चकार संहितां दिव्यां नानाख्यानसमन्विताम् ॥
1.62.m: By Nārāyaṇa's appointment, however, through your mouth, O best of sages, / he composed a divine collection filled with diverse tales,

1.62.s:
vedatulyāṃ bhāgavatīṃ haribhaktivivarddhinīm /
nivṛttinirataṃ putraṃ śukamadhyāpayañca tām //
1.62.d:
वेदतुल्यां भागवतीं हरिभक्तिविवर्द्धिनीम् ।
निवृत्तिनिरतं पुत्रं शुकमध्यापयञ्च ताम् ॥
1.62.m: equal to the Vedas, related to the Lord, promoting devotion to Hari, / and he taught it to his son Śuka, devoted to renunciation.

1.62.s:
ātmārāmo 'pi bhagavānpārāśaryātmajaḥ śukaḥ /
adhītavānsaṃhitāṃ vai nityaṃ viṣṇujanapriyām //
1.62.d:
आत्मारामो ऽपि भगवान्पाराशर्यात्मजः शुकः ।
अधीतवान्संहितां वै नित्यं विष्णुजनप्रियाम् ॥
1.62.m: Though rejoicing in the Self, the blessed Śuka, son of Parāśara, / studied this collection, ever dear to the people of Viṣṇu.

1.62.s:
evamete samākhyātā mokṣadharmāstavānadha /
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ cāpi haribhaktivivarddhanāḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde bṛhadupākhyāne mokṣadharṃmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dviṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.62.d:
एवमेते समाख्याता मोक्षधर्मास्तवानध ।
पठतां शृण्वतां चापि हरिभक्तिविवर्द्धनाः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे बृहदुपाख्याने मोक्षधर्ंमनिरूपणं नाम द्विषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
1.62.m:
Thus these duties of liberation have been proclaimed to you, O sinless one; / they promote devotion to Hari for both those who recite and those who listen.

Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, named 'Ascertainment of the Duties of Liberation' in the Great Narrative in the second quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.63.s:
samāptaścāyaṃ dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ /
śaunaka uvāca
sūta sādho ciraṃ jīva sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ /
yattvayā pāyitā vidvanvayaṃ kṛṣṇakathāmṛtam //
1.63.d:
समाप्तश्चायं द्वितीयः पादः ।
शौनक उवाच
सूत साधो चिरं जीव सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः ।
यत्त्वया पायिता विद्वन्वयं कृष्णकथामृतम् ॥
1.63.m: And concluded is this second quarter. / Śaunaka said: / "O virtuous Sūta, adept in all scriptures, live long, / since by you, O learned one, we have been made to drink the nectar of tales of Kṛṣṇa!

1.63.s:
śrutvā tu mokṣadharmānvai nārado bhagavatpriyaḥ /
sanandanamukhodgītānkiṃ papracchaṃ tataḥ param //
1.63.d:
श्रुत्वा तु मोक्षधर्मान्वै नारदो भगवत्प्रियः ।
सनन्दनमुखोद्गीतान्किं पप्रच्छं ततः परम् ॥
1.63.m: Having heard the duties of liberation, dear to the Blessed One, / sung from the mouth of Sanandana, what did Nārada ask after that?

1.63.s:
mānasā brahmaṇaḥ putrāḥ sanakādyā munīśvarāḥ /
caranti lokānantasiddhā lokoddharaṇatatparāḥ //
1.63.d:
मानसा ब्रह्मणः पुत्राः सनकाद्या मुनीश्वराः ।
चरन्ति लोकानन्तसिद्धा लोकोद्धरणतत्पराः ॥
1.63.m: The mind-born sons of Brahmā, Sanaka and the other foremost sages, / perfected ones, roam the infinite worlds, intent on elevating the world.

1.63.s:
nārado 'pi mahābhāga nityaṃ kṛṣṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
teṣāṃ samāgame bhadrā kā kathā lokapāvanī //
1.63.d:
नारदो ऽपि महाभाग नित्यं कृष्णपरायणः ।
तेषां समागमे भद्रा का कथा लोकपावनी ॥
1.63.m: Nārada too, O highly fortunate one, is ever devoted to Kṛṣṇa; / at their meeting, what auspicious tale, purifying the world, [took place]?"

1.63.s:
sūta uvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ mahābhāga tvayā lokopakāriṇā /
kathayiṣyāmi tatsarvaṃ yatpṛṣṭa nāradarṣiṇā //
1.63.d:
सूत उवाच
साधु पृष्टं महाभाग त्वया लोकोपकारिणा ।
कथयिष्यामि तत्सर्वं यत्पृष्ट नारदर्षिणा ॥
1.63.m: Sūta said: / "Well asked by you, O highly fortunate one, benefactor of the world! / I will relate all that was asked by the sage Nārada.

1.63.s:
śrutvā sanandanaproktānmokṣadharmānsanātanān /
nārado bhārgavaśreṣṭha punaḥ papraccha tānmunīn //
1.63.d:
श्रुत्वा सनन्दनप्रोक्तान्मोक्षधर्मान्सनातनान् ।
नारदो भार्गवश्रेष्ठ पुनः पप्रच्छ तान्मुनीन् ॥
1.63.m: Having heard the eternal duties of liberation spoken by Sanandana, / Nārada, O best of the descendants of Bhṛgu, questioned those sages again.

1.63.s:
nārada uvāca
sarvadeveśvaro viṣṇurvede tantre ca kīrtitaḥ /
samārādhyaḥ sa evātra sarvaiḥ sarvārthakāṅkṣibhiḥ //
1.63.d:
नारद उवाच
सर्वदेवेश्वरो विष्णुर्वेदे तन्त्रे च कीर्तितः ।
समाराध्यः स एवात्र सर्वैः सर्वार्थकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥
1.63.m: Nārada said: / 'Viṣṇu, Lord of all gods, is celebrated in the Veda and the Tantra; / he alone is to be propitiated here by all who desire all ends.

1.63.s:
kairmantrairbhagavānviṣṇuḥ samārādhyo munīśvarāḥ /
ke devāḥ pūjanīyāśca viṣṇupādaparāyaṇaiḥ //
1.63.d:
कैर्मन्त्रैर्भगवान्विष्णुः समाराध्यो मुनीश्वराः ।
के देवाः पूजनीयाश्च विष्णुपादपरायणैः ॥
1.63.m: With which mantras is the Blessed Viṣṇu to be propitiated, O best of sages? / And which deities are to be worshipped by those devoted to Viṣṇu's feet?

1.63.s:
tantraṃ bhāgavataṃ viprā guruśiṣyaprayojakam /
dīkṣaṇaṃ prātarādyaṃ ca kṛtyaṃ syādyattaducyatām //
1.63.d:
तन्त्रं भागवतं विप्रा गुरुशिष्यप्रयोजकम् ।
दीक्षणं प्रातराद्यं च कृत्यं स्याद्यत्तदुच्यताम् ॥
1.63.m: O brāhmaṇas, explain the Bhāgavata tantra regarding the preceptor and disciple, / the initiation, and what the duty beginning in the morning should be.

1.63.s:
yairmāsaiḥ karmabhiryairvā japyairhemādibhistathā /
prīyeta paramātmā vai tadbrūta mama mānadāḥ //
1.63.d:
यैर्मासैः कर्मभिर्यैर्वा जप्यैर्हेमादिभिस्तथा ।
प्रीयेत परमात्मा वै तद्ब्रूत मम मानदाः ॥
1.63.m: Tell me, O givers of honor, through which months, which rites, / which recitations, and such [rites] as fire oblations, the Supreme Self is pleased.'"

1.63.s:
sūta uvāca
etacchrutvā vacastasya nāradasya mahātmanaḥ /
sanatkumāro bhagavānuvācārkasamadyutiḥ //
1.63.d:
सूत उवाच
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य नारदस्य महात्मनः ।
सनत्कुमारो भगवानुवाचार्कसमद्युतिः ॥
1.63.m: Sūta said: / Having heard these words of the great-souled Nārada, / the blessed Sanatkumāra, radiant as the sun, spoke:

1.63.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi tantraṃ bhāgavataṃ tava /
yajjñātvāmalayā bhaktyā sādhayedviṣṇumavyayam //
1.63.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि तन्त्रं भागवतं तव ।
यज्ज्ञात्वामलया भक्त्या साधयेद्विष्णुमव्ययम् ॥
1.63.m: Sanatkumāra said: / "Listen, Nārada; I shall declare to you the Bhāgavata tantra, / knowing which with pure devotion one may attain the imperishable Viṣṇu.

1.63.s:
tripadārthaṃ catuṣpādaṃ mahātantraṃ pracakṣate /
bhogamokṣakriyācaryāhvayā pādāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
1.63.d:
त्रिपदार्थं चतुष्पादं महातन्त्रं प्रचक्षते ।
भोगमोक्षक्रियाचर्याह्वया पादाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.63.m: They declare the great tantra to have three subject matters and four quarters; / enjoyment, liberation, ritual practice, and conduct are proclaimed as the names of the quarters.

1.63.s:
pādārthāstu paśupatiḥ paśupāśāstraya eva hi /
patistatra śivohyeko jīvāstu paśavaḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.63.d:
पादार्थास्तु पशुपतिः पशुपाशास्त्रय एव हि ।
पतिस्तत्र शिवोह्येको जीवास्तु पशवः स्मृताः ॥
1.63.m: The categories of the padas are indeed just three: the Lord of the bound (Paśupati), the bound souls (paśu), and the fetters (pāśa). / There, the Lord is Śiva alone, whereas living beings are remembered as the bound souls.

1.63.s:
yāvanmohādisaṃyogāḥ svarūpābodhalakṣaṇāḥ /
tāvatpaśutvameteṣāṃ dvaitavatpaśya nārada //
1.63.d:
यावन्मोहादिसंयोगाः स्वरूपाबोधलक्षणाः ।
तावत्पशुत्वमेतेषां द्वैतवत्पश्य नारद ॥
1.63.m: As long as there are connections with delusion and the like, characterized by ignorance of one's essential nature, / for that long does their state of being a bound soul endure; look upon them as characterized by duality, O Nārada.

1.63.s:
pāśāḥ pañcavidhāstveṣāṃ pratyekaṃ teṣu lakṣaṇam /
paśavastrividhāścāpi vijñātāḥ kalasaṃjñikāḥ //
1.63.d:
पाशाः पञ्चविधास्त्वेषां प्रत्येकं तेषु लक्षणम् ।
पशवस्त्रिविधाश्चापि विज्ञाताः कलसंज्ञिकाः ॥
1.63.m: Their fetters are of five kinds, each having its own characteristic definition among them; / and the bound souls are understood to be threefold, designated according to their association with the limiting principles (kala):

1.63.s:
talapākalasaṃjñaśca sakalaśceti nāmataḥ /
tatrādyo malasaṃyukto malakarmayutaḥ paraḥ //
1.63.d:
तलपाकलसंज्ञश्च सकलश्चेति नामतः ।
तत्राद्यो मलसंयुक्तो मलकर्मयुतः परः ॥
1.63.m: Known by the names Vijñānākala, Pralayākala, and Sakala. / Among them, the first is endowed with impurity (mala); the second is endowed with impurity and karma;

1.63.s:
malamāyākarmayutastṛtīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
ādyastu dvividhastatra samāsakaluṣastathā //
1.63.d:
मलमायाकर्मयुतस्तृतीयः परिकीर्तितः ।
आद्यस्तु द्विविधस्तत्र समासकलुषस्तथा ॥
1.63.m: The third is declared to be endowed with impurity, māyā, and karma. / There, the first is of two kinds: having compounded blemish,

1.63.s:
asamāsamalaśceti dvitīyo 'pi punastathā /
pakvāpakvamalenaiva dvividhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
1.63.d:
असमासमलश्चेति द्वितीयो ऽपि पुनस्तथा ।
पक्वापक्वमलेनैव द्विविधः परिकीर्तितः ॥
1.63.m: And having uncompounded blemish; and the second is also likewise / declared to be of two kinds according to mature and immature impurity.

1.63.s:
śuddhe 'dhvani gatāvetau vijñānapralayākalau /
kalāditattvaniyataḥ sakalaḥ paryaṭatyayam //
1.63.d:
शुद्धे ऽध्वनि गतावेतौ विज्ञानप्रलयाकलौ ।
कलादितत्त्वनियतः सकलः पर्यटत्ययम् ॥
1.63.m: These two, the Vijñānākala and the Pralayākala, have entered the pure course (śuddhādhvan); / [while] this Sakala soul, constrained by the tattvas beginning with kalā, wanders about

1.63.s:
karmānugaśarīreṣu tattadbhuvanageṣu ca /
pāśāḥ pañca tathā tatra prathamau malakarmajau //
1.63.d:
कर्मानुगशरीरेषु तत्तद्भुवनगेषु च ।
पाशाः पञ्च तथा तत्र प्रथमौ मलकर्मजौ ॥
1.63.m: In bodies conforming to karma, and in the various worlds. / Likewise, the fetters there are five, the first two being produced from mala and karma;

1.63.s:
māyeyaśca tirodhānaśaktijo bindujaḥ paraḥ /
eko 'pyanekaśaktirdṛkkriyācchādanakomalaḥ //
1.63.d:
मायेयश्च तिरोधानशक्तिजो बिन्दुजः परः ।
एको ऽप्यनेकशक्तिर्दृक्क्रियाच्छादनकोमलः ॥
1.63.m: The next arise from māyā, from the power of concealment (tirodhānaśakti), and from bindu. / [Mala,] though single, possesses manifold powers, concealing sight and action softly;

1.63.s:
tuṣakañcukavaddehanimittaṃ cātmanāmiha /
dharmādharmātmakaṃ karma vicitraphalabhogadam //
1.63.d:
तुषकञ्चुकवद्देहनिमित्तं चात्मनामिह ।
धर्माधर्मात्मकं कर्म विचित्रफलभोगदम् ॥
1.63.m: Like a husk or a sheath, it is the cause of embodiment for souls here. / Karma consists of merit and demerit, granting the experience of diverse fruits;

1.63.s:
pravāhanityaṃ tadbījāṅkuranyāyena saṃsthitam /
ityetau prathamau cātha māyeyādyān śṛṇudvija //
1.63.d:
प्रवाहनित्यं तद्बीजाङ्कुरन्यायेन संस्थितम् ।
इत्येतौ प्रथमौ चाथ मायेयाद्यान् शृणुद्विज ॥
1.63.m: It is eternal as a stream, continuing according to the maxim of the seed and the sprout. / Thus these two are the first; now hear of those beginning with māyā, O twice-born one.

1.63.s:
sañcidānandavibhavaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ /
patirjayati sarveṣāmeko bījaṃ vibhuḥ param //
1.63.d:
सञ्चिदानन्दविभवः परमात्मा सनातनः ।
पतिर्जयति सर्वेषामेको बीजं विभुः परम् ॥
1.63.m: The eternal supreme Self, whose magnificence is consciousness and bliss, / the one Lord over all, the supreme omnipresent seed, reigns supreme.

1.63.s:
manasyati na codeti nivṛttiṃ ca prayacchati /
varvarti dṛkkriyārūpaṃ tattejaḥ śāṃbhavaṃ param //
1.63.d:
मनस्यति न चोदेति निवृत्तिं च प्रयच्छति ।
वर्वर्ति दृक्क्रियारूपं तत्तेजः शांभवं परम् ॥
1.63.m: He neither desires nor rises, and grants cessation; / that supreme splendor belonging to Śambhu perpetually exists in the form of seeing and acting.

1.63.s:
śakto mayā harau bhukto paśugaṇasya hi /
tacchaktimādyāmekāntāṃ vidrūpākhyāṃ vadanti hi //
1.63.d:
शक्तो मया हरौ भुक्तो पशुगणस्य हि ।
तच्छक्तिमाद्यामेकान्तां विद्रूपाख्यां वदन्ति हि ॥
1.63.m: It is capable of granting experience to the host of bound souls in Hari; / indeed, they speak of His primal, exclusive power as consisting of consciousness.

1.63.s:
tayā cojjṛṃbhito bindurdikkriyātmā śivābhidhaḥ /
aśeṣatattvajātasya kāraṇaṃ vibhuravyayam //
1.63.d:
तया चोज्जृंभितो बिन्दुर्दिक्क्रियात्मा शिवाभिधः ।
अशेषतत्त्वजातस्य कारणं विभुरव्ययम् ॥
1.63.m: And awakened by Her, the bindu, which is the nature of vision and action, is named Śiva, / the omnipresent, imperishable cause of the entire collection of tattvas.

1.63.s:
asminnilīnā nikhilā icchāyāḥ śaktayaḥ svakam /
kṛtyaṃ kurvanti tenedaṃ sarvānugrāhakaṃ mune //
1.63.d:
अस्मिन्निलीना निखिला इच्छायाः शक्तयः स्वकम् ।
कृत्यं कुर्वन्ति तेनेदं सर्वानुग्राहकं मुने ॥
1.63.m: All the powers of will, merged within this [bindu], perform their own / task; therefore, O sage, this is the bestower of grace upon all.

1.63.s:
cijjaḍānugrahārthāya yasya viśvaṃ sisṛkṣataḥ /
ādyonmeṣo 'sya nādātmā śāntyādibhuvanātmakaḥ //
1.63.d:
चिज्जडानुग्रहार्थाय यस्य विश्वं सिसृक्षतः ।
आद्योन्मेषो ऽस्य नादात्मा शान्त्यादिभुवनात्मकः ॥
1.63.m: For Him who wishes to emanate the universe in order to bestow grace upon the conscious and the insentient, / His initial unfoldment consists of nāda, comprising the worlds beginning with Śānti.

1.63.s:
tacchaktitattvaṃ viprendra proktaṃ sāvayavaṃ param /
tato jñānakriyāśaktyostathotkarṣāpakarṣayoḥ //
1.63.d:
तच्छक्तितत्त्वं विप्रेन्द्र प्रोक्तं सावयवं परम् ।
ततो ज्ञानक्रियाशक्त्योस्तथोत्कर्षापकर्षयोः ॥
1.63.m: That power-principle (śaktitattva), O best of brahmins, is declared to be composite and supreme. / Then, from the increase and decrease of the powers of knowledge and action,

1.63.s:
prasaraścāpyabhāvena tattvaṃ caitatsadāśivam /
dṛkśaktiryatra nyagbhūtā kriyāśaktirviśiṣyate //
1.63.d:
प्रसरश्चाप्यभावेन तत्त्वं चैतत्सदाशिवम् ।
दृक्शक्तिर्यत्र न्यग्भूता क्रियाशक्तिर्विशिष्यते ॥
1.63.m: And their unfolding without absence, arises this tattva named Sadāśiva. / Where the power of seeing is subordinated and the power of action is prominent,

1.63.s:
īśvarākhyaṃ tu tattattvaṃ proktaṃ sarvārthakartṛkam /
yatra kriyā hi nyagbhūtā jñānākhyodrekamaśnute //
1.63.d:
ईश्वराख्यं तु तत्तत्त्वं प्रोक्तं सर्वार्थकर्तृकम् ।
यत्र क्रिया हि न्यग्भूता ज्ञानाख्योद्रेकमश्नुते ॥
1.63.m: That tattva is indeed called Īśvara, the agent of all purposes. / Where action is subordinated and [the power] called knowledge attains prominence,

1.63.s:
tattattvaṃ caiva vidyākhyaṃ jñānarūpaṃ prakāśakam /
nādo binduśca sakalaḥ sadākhyaṃ tattvamāśritau //
1.63.d:
तत्तत्त्वं चैव विद्याख्यं ज्ञानरूपं प्रकाशकम् ।
नादो बिन्दुश्च सकलः सदाख्यं तत्त्वमाश्रितौ ॥
1.63.m: That tattva is known as Vidyā, having the nature of knowledge, illuminating. / Nāda and bindu, possessing parts, have resorted to the tattva called Sadāśiva.

1.63.s:
vidyeśāḥ punaraiśaṃ tu mantrā vidyābhidhaṃ punaḥ /
imāni caiva tattvāni śuddhādhveti prakīrtitam //
1.63.d:
विद्येशाः पुनरैशं तु मन्त्रा विद्याभिधं पुनः ।
इमानि चैव तत्त्वानि शुद्धाध्वेति प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.63.m: The lords of knowledge (vidyeśas) belong to Īśa, and the mantras belong to the Vidyā tattva. / And these tattvas are proclaimed as the pure course (śuddhādhvan).

1.63.s:
sākṣānnimittamīśo 'tretyupādānasabindurāṭ /
pañcānāṃ kālarāhityākramo nāstīti niścitam //
1.63.d:
साक्षान्निमित्तमीशो ऽत्रेत्युपादानसबिन्दुराट् ।
पञ्चानां कालराहित्याक्रमो नास्तीति निश्चितम् ॥
1.63.m: Here, the Lord is the direct efficient cause, and the king of bindus is the material cause. / Due to the absence of time among the five, it is certain that there is no temporal sequence.

1.63.s:
vyāpāravasato hyeṣāṃ vihitā khalu kalpanā /
tattvaṃ vastuta ekaṃ tu śivākhyaṃ citraśaktikam //
1.63.d:
व्यापारवसतो ह्येषां विहिता खलु कल्पना ।
तत्त्वं वस्तुत एकं तु शिवाख्यं चित्रशक्तिकम् ॥
1.63.m: Indeed, their conceptual distinction is made only on account of their activities; / in reality, the principle is one, named Śiva, possessing manifold powers.

1.63.s:
śaktaṃ yāṃ vṛttibhedāttuvihitāḥ khalu kalpanāḥ /
cijjaḍānugrahārthāya kṛtvā rūpāṇi vai prabhuḥ //
1.63.d:
शक्तं यां वृत्तिभेदात्तुविहिताः खलु कल्पनाः ।
चिज्जडानुग्रहार्थाय कृत्वा रूपाणि वै प्रभुः ॥
1.63.m: According to the differences in Her activities, conceptual distinctions are made. / Having assumed forms in order to bestow grace upon the conscious and the insentient, the Lord

1.63.s:
anādimalaruddhānāṃ kurute 'nugrahaṃ citām /
muktiṃ ca viśveṣāṃ svavyāpāre samarthetām //
1.63.d:
अनादिमलरुद्धानां कुरुते ऽनुग्रहं चिताम् ।
मुक्तिं च विश्वेषां स्वव्यापारे समर्थेताम् ॥
1.63.m: Bestows grace upon conscious souls obstructed by beginningless impurity; / and liberation for all souls that are capable in their own activity

1.63.s:
vidhatte jaḍavargasya sarvānugrāhakaḥ śivaḥ /
śivasāmānyarūpo hi mokṣastu cidanugrahaḥ //
1.63.d:
विधत्ते जडवर्गस्य सर्वानुग्राहकः शिवः ।
शिवसामान्यरूपो हि मोक्षस्तु चिदनुग्रहः ॥
1.63.m: Śiva, the gracious bestower of all, arranges for the category of the insentient. / For liberation, which has the common nature of Śiva, is grace upon the conscious soul.

1.63.s:
so 'nāditvātkarmaṇo hi tattadbhogaṃ vinā bhavet /
tenānugrāhakaḥ śambhustadbhuktyai prabhurvyayaḥ //
1.63.d:
सो ऽनादित्वात्कर्मणो हि तत्तद्भोगं विना भवेत् ।
तेनानुग्राहकः शम्भुस्तद्भुक्त्यै प्रभुर्व्ययः ॥
1.63.m: Because karma is beginningless, that [grace] comes to be only through the experiencing of its fruits; / therefore Śambhu, the imperishable Lord, in order that they may experience it,

1.63.s:
kurute sūkṣmakaraṇabhuvanotpattimañjasā /
karttopādānakaraṇairvinā kārye na dṛśyate //
1.63.d:
कुरुते सूक्ष्मकरणभुवनोत्पत्तिमञ्जसा ।
कर्त्तोपादानकरणैर्विना कार्ये न दृश्यते ॥
1.63.m: Effectively brings about the creation of subtle instruments and worlds. / An effect is never observed without an agent, material cause, and instruments:

1.63.s:
śaktayaḥ karaṇaṃ cātra māyopādānamiṣyate /
nityaikā ca śivā śaktyā hyanādinidhanā satī //
1.63.d:
शक्तयः करणं चात्र मायोपादानमिष्यते ।
नित्यैका च शिवा शक्त्या ह्यनादिनिधना सती ॥
1.63.m: The powers are the instrument here, and māyā is accepted as the material cause. / Eternal and one, auspicious through His power, beginningless and endless, real,

1.63.s:
sādhāraṇī narāṇāṃ vai bhuvanānāṃ ca kāraṇam /
svabhāvānmohajananī svacitājanakarmabhiḥ //
1.63.d:
साधारणी नराणां वै भुवनानां च कारणम् ।
स्वभावान्मोहजननी स्वचिताजनकर्मभिः ॥
1.63.m: Common to all men, it is indeed the cause of the worlds; / by its very nature it generates delusion, through the karma born of each soul's consciousness.

1.63.s:
viśvī sūkṣmā parā māyā vikṛtaiḥ parattu sā /
karmāṇyāvekṣya vidyeśo māyāṃ vikṣobhya śaktibhiḥ //
1.63.d:
विश्वी सूक्ष्मा परा माया विकृतैः परत्तु सा ।
कर्माण्यावेक्ष्य विद्येशो मायां विक्षोभ्य शक्तिभिः ॥
1.63.m: Universal, subtle, supreme is māyā, yet it is supreme through its transformations. / Perceiving their karmas, the Lord of Vidyā, agitating māyā with His powers,

1.63.s:
vidhatte jīvabhogārthaṃ vapūṃṣi karaṇāni ca /
sṛjatyādo kālatattvaṃ nānāśaktimayī ca sā //
1.63.d:
विधत्ते जीवभोगार्थं वपूंषि करणानि च ।
सृजत्यादो कालतत्त्वं नानाशक्तिमयी च सा ॥
1.63.m: Arranges bodies and instruments for the living beings' experience. / At the beginning, composed of diverse powers, He creates the time-principle (kālatattva);

1.63.s:
bhāvi bhūtaṃ mavañcedaṃ jagatkalayate layam /
sūte hyanantaraṃ māyā śaktiṃ niyamanātmikām //
1.63.d:
भावि भूतं मवञ्चेदं जगत्कलयते लयम् ।
सूते ह्यनन्तरं माया शक्तिं नियमनात्मिकाम् ॥
1.63.m: It computes the future, the past, and this present universe, and its dissolution. / Immediately thereafter, māyā produces the power consisting of restriction;

1.63.s:
sarvaṃ niyamayatyeṣā teneyaṃ niyatiḥ smṛtā /
anantaraṃ ca sā māyā nityā viśvavimohinī //
1.63.d:
सर्वं नियमयत्येषा तेनेयं नियतिः स्मृता ।
अनन्तरं च सा माया नित्या विश्वविमोहिनी ॥
1.63.m: It restricts everything, and is therefore remembered as niyati. / And immediately after, that eternal māyā, which deludes the universe,

1.63.s:
anādinidhanā tattvaṃ kalākhyaṃ janayatyapi /
ekatastu nṛṇāṃ yena kalayitvā malaṃ tataḥ //
1.63.d:
अनादिनिधना तत्त्वं कलाख्यं जनयत्यपि ।
एकतस्तु नृणां येन कलयित्वा मलं ततः ॥
1.63.m: Beginningless and endless, also gives birth to the tattva called kalā; / whereby, removing the impurity on one side from men,

1.63.s:
kartṛśaktiṃ vyañjayati tenedaṃ tu kalābhidham /
kālena ca niyatyopasargatāṃ samupetayā //
1.63.d:
कर्तृशक्तिं व्यञ्जयति तेनेदं तु कलाभिधम् ।
कालेन च नियत्योपसर्गतां समुपेतया ॥
1.63.m: It manifests the agentive power, and therefore it is named kalā. / Accompanied by time and by niyati that has become a modifier,

1.63.s:
vyāpāraṃ vidadhātyeṣā bhūparyantaṃ svakīyakam /
pradarśanātha vai puṃso viṣayāṇāṃ ca sā punaḥ //
1.63.d:
व्यापारं विदधात्येषा भूपर्यन्तं स्वकीयकम् ।
प्रदर्शनाथ वै पुंसो विषयाणां च सा पुनः ॥
1.63.m: It performs its own activity extending up to the earth-element. / Then, in order to show sense-objects to the puruṣa,

1.63.s:
prakāśarūpaṃ vidyākhyaṃ tattvaṃ sūte kalaiva hi /
vidyā tvāvaraṇaṃ bhitvā jñānaśakteḥ svakarmaṇā //
1.63.d:
प्रकाशरूपं विद्याख्यं तत्त्वं सूते कलैव हि ।
विद्या त्वावरणं भित्वा ज्ञानशक्तेः स्वकर्मणा ॥
1.63.m: Kalā itself gives birth to the illuminating tattva called vidyā. / Vidyā, piercing the veil of the power of knowledge by its own function,

1.63.s:
viṣayāndarśayatyeṣātmanāṃśākāraṇaṃ hyataḥ /
karoti bhogyaṃ yānāsau karaṇena pareṇa vai //
1.63.d:
विषयान्दर्शयत्येषात्मनांशाकारणं ह्यतः ।
करोति भोग्यं यानासौ करणेन परेण वै ॥
1.63.m: Shows sense-objects to the souls, for it is the cause of their partial manifestation; / hence, by means of that higher instrument, it makes objects fit for enjoyment.

1.63.s:
udbuddhaśaktiḥ puruṣaḥ pracodya mahadādikān /
bhogye bhogaṃ ca bhoktāraṃ tatparaṃ karaṇaṃ tu sā //
1.63.d:
उद्बुद्धशक्तिः पुरुषः प्रचोद्य महदादिकान् ।
भोग्ये भोगं च भोक्तारं तत्परं करणं तु सा ॥
1.63.m: With his power awakened, the puruṣa, impelling the principles beginning with mahat, / [experiences] experience in what is enjoyable, and the experiencer; that [vidyā] is the supreme instrument.

1.63.s:
bhogyesya bhogyatirmāsāñcidvyaktirbhoga ucyate /
sukhādirūpo viṣayākārā buddhiḥ samāsataḥ //
1.63.d:
भोग्येस्य भोग्यतिर्मासाञ्चिद्व्यक्तिर्भोग उच्यते ।
सुखादिरूपो विषयाकारा बुद्धिः समासतः ॥
1.63.m: The enjoyability of the object of experience is the manifestation of consciousness, which is called experience; / in short, the intellect, having assumed the form of sense-objects, consists of pleasure and pain.

1.63.s:
bhogyaṃ bhoktuśca svenaiva vidyākhyaṃ karaṇaṃ tu tat /
yadyarkavatprakāśā dhīḥ karmatvāñca tathāpi hi //
1.63.d:
भोग्यं भोक्तुश्च स्वेनैव विद्याख्यं करणं तु तत् ।
यद्यर्कवत्प्रकाशा धीः कर्मत्वाञ्च तथापि हि ॥
1.63.m: That instrument called vidyā belongs to the experiencer through itself, concerning what is enjoyed. / Even though the intellect is luminous like the sun, nevertheless, being an object of action,

1.63.s:
karaṇāntarasāpekṣā śaktā grāhayituṃ ca tam /
saṃbandhātkāraṇādyaistadbhogautsukyena codanāt //
1.63.d:
करणान्तरसापेक्षा शक्ता ग्राहयितुं च तम् ।
संबन्धात्कारणाद्यैस्तद्भोगौत्सुक्येन चोदनात् ॥
1.63.m: It depends upon another instrument and is capable of causing him to grasp it, / through contact with causes and the like, by impelling him out of an eagerness for experience.

1.63.s:
tañcaṣṭāphalayogāñca saṃsiddhā kartṛtāsya tu /
akartṛtvābhyupagame bhoktṛtvākhyā vṛthāsya tu //
1.63.d:
तञ्चष्टाफलयोगाञ्च संसिद्धा कर्तृतास्य तु ।
अकर्तृत्वाभ्युपगमे भोक्तृत्वाख्या वृथास्य तु ॥
