1.63.m: And because he is connected with the fruit of that effort, his agency is established; / if non-agency were accepted, calling him the experiencer would be meaningless.

1.63.s:
kiṃ ca pradhānacaritaṃ vyarthaṃ sarvaṃ bhavettataḥ /
kartṛtvarahite puṃsi karaṇādyaprayojake //
1.63.d:
किं च प्रधानचरितं व्यर्थं सर्वं भवेत्ततः ।
कर्तृत्वरहिते पुंसि करणाद्यप्रयोजके ॥
1.63.m: Moreover, all the activity of pradhāna would then become futile. / When the puruṣa is devoid of agency, not impelling instruments and the like,

1.63.s:
bhogasyāsaṃbhavastasmātsa evātra pravartakaḥ /
karaṇādiprayoktṛātvaṃ vidyayaivāsya saṃmatam //
1.63.d:
भोगस्यासंभवस्तस्मात्स एवात्र प्रवर्तकः ।
करणादिप्रयोक्तृआत्वं विद्ययैवास्य संमतम् ॥
1.63.m: Experience would be impossible; therefore he alone is the impeller here. / His state of being the employer of instruments and the like is acknowledged solely through vidyā.

1.63.s:
anantaraṃ kalārāgaṃ sūte bhidyaṅgarūpakam /
yena bhogyāya janitā bhidyaṅge puruṣe punaḥ //
1.63.d:
अनन्तरं कलारागं सूते भिद्यङ्गरूपकम् ।
येन भोग्याय जनिता भिद्यङ्गे पुरुषे पुनः ॥
1.63.m: Immediately thereafter, kalā produces attachment (rāga), having the form of an accessory; / by which desire for objects of experience is produced in the puruṣa.

1.63.s:
kriyāpravṛttirbhavati tenedaṃ rāgasaṃjñikam /
ebhistattvaiśca bhoktṛtvadaśāyāṃ kalito yadā //
1.63.d:
क्रियाप्रवृत्तिर्भवति तेनेदं रागसंज्ञिकम् ।
एभिस्तत्त्वैश्च भोक्तृत्वदशायां कलितो यदा ॥
1.63.m: from this, engagement in action arises; therefore, this is known as rāga (attachment). / When the eternal Self is enveloped by these principles in the state of being an experiencer,

1.63.s:
nityastadāyamātmā tu labhate puruṣābhidhām /
kalaiva praścādavyaktaṃ sūte bhogyāya cāsya tu //
1.63.d:
नित्यस्तदायमात्मा तु लभते पुरुषाभिधाम् ।
कलैव प्रश्चादव्यक्तं सूते भोग्याय चास्य तु ॥
1.63.m: it then obtains the designation of "puruṣa" (person). / Subsequently, kalā alone brings forth the unmanifest (avyakta) for its enjoyment,

1.63.s:
saptagranthividhānasya yattadgauṇasyakāraṇam /
guṇānāmavibhāgo 'tra hyādhāre kṣmādibhāgavat //
1.63.d:
सप्तग्रन्थिविधानस्य यत्तद्गौणस्यकारणम् ।
गुणानामविभागो ऽत्र ह्याधारे क्ष्मादिभागवत् ॥
1.63.m: which is the cause of the secondary arrangement of the seven knots. / Here, the non-differentiation of the guṇas is in the substratum, like the portions of earth and the other elements;

1.63.s:
ādhāro 'pi ca yasteṣāṃ tadavyaktaṃ ca gīyate /
traya eva guṇā hyaṣāmavyaktādeva saṃbhavaḥ //
1.63.d:
आधारो ऽपि च यस्तेषां तदव्यक्तं च गीयते ।
त्रय एव गुणा ह्यषामव्यक्तादेव संभवः ॥
1.63.m: and that which is their substratum is celebrated as the unmanifest (avyakta). / The guṇas are indeed only three; their arising is from the unmanifest alone:

1.63.s:
sattvaṃ rajastamaḥprakhyā vyāpāraniyamātmikā /
guṇato dhīśca viṣayādhyavasāyasvarūpiṇī //
1.63.d:
सत्त्वं रजस्तमःप्रख्या व्यापारनियमात्मिका ।
गुणतो धीश्च विषयाध्यवसायस्वरूपिणी ॥
1.63.m: sattva, rajas, and tamas, consisting of clarity, activity, and restraint respectively. / From the guṇas arises intellect (dhī), whose nature is the ascertainment of objects.

1.63.s:
guṇatastrividhā sāpi proktā karmānusārataḥ /
mahattattavādahṝṅkāro jātaḥ saṃraṃbhavṛttimān //
1.63.d:
गुणतस्त्रिविधा सापि प्रोक्ता कर्मानुसारतः ।
महत्तत्तवादहॄङ्कारो जातः संरंभवृत्तिमान् ॥
1.63.m: It too is said to be threefold according to the guṇas and in accordance with action. / From the principle of intellect (mahattattva) arises the ego (ahaṅkāra), which possesses the function of impetuosity.

1.63.s:
saṃbhodādasya viṣayaḥ prāpnoti vyavahāryatām /
sattvā dviguṇabhedena sa punastrividho bhavet //
1.63.d:
संभोदादस्य विषयः प्राप्नोति व्यवहार्यताम् ।
सत्त्वा द्विगुणभेदेन स पुनस्त्रिविधो भवेत् ॥
1.63.m: By contact with this, an object attains practical utility. / That ego, by the division of two guṇas, becomes threefold again:

1.63.s:
taijaso rājasaścaiva tāmasaśceti nāmataḥ /
tatra taijasato jñānendriyāṇi manasā saha //
1.63.d:
तैजसो राजसश्चैव तामसश्चेति नामतः ।
तत्र तैजसतो ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि मनसा सह ॥
1.63.m: namely taijasa, rājasa, and tāmasa by name. / There, from taijasa, the sense organs of knowledge arise along with the mind;

1.63.s:
prakāśānva yatastasmādvodhakāni bhavanti hi /
rājasāñca kriyāhetostathā karmendriyāṇi tu //
1.63.d:
प्रकाशान्व यतस्तस्माद्वोधकानि भवन्ति हि ।
राजसाञ्च क्रियाहेतोस्तथा कर्मेन्द्रियाणि तु ॥
1.63.m: for, possessing luminosity, they are indeed illuminators [of objects]. / From rājasa, as the cause of activity, arise the organs of action;

1.63.s:
tāmasāñcaiva jāyante tanmātrā bhūtayonayaḥ /
icchārūpaṃ ca saṃkalpavyāpāraṃ tatra vai manaḥ //
1.63.d:
तामसाञ्चैव जायन्ते तन्मात्रा भूतयोनयः ।
इच्छारूपं च संकल्पव्यापारं तत्र वै मनः ॥
1.63.m: and from tāmasa are born the subtle elements (tanmātras), which are the sources of the gross elements. / The mind there has the nature of desire and the function of volition.

1.63.s:
dvidhādhikāri tañcittaṃ bhoktṛbhogopapādakam /
bahiḥ karaṇabhāvena svocitena yataḥ sadā //
1.63.d:
द्विधाधिकारि तञ्चित्तं भोक्तृभोगोपपादकम् ।
बहिः करणभावेन स्वोचितेन यतः सदा ॥
1.63.m: That mind (citta) has a twofold authority, effecting both the experiencer and the experience, / since it always acts as an external instrument in its appropriate manner,

1.63.s:
indriyāṇāñca sāmarthyaṃ saṃkalpenātmavṛttinā /
karotyantaḥsthitaṃ bhūyastato 'ntaḥ karaṇaṃ manaḥ //
1.63.d:
इन्द्रियाणाञ्च सामर्थ्यं संकल्पेनात्मवृत्तिना ।
करोत्यन्तःस्थितं भूयस्ततो ऽन्तः करणं मनः ॥
1.63.m: and by its own function of volition it continually empowers the senses from within; / therefore the mind is the internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa).

1.63.s:
mano 'hṝṅkārabuddhyākhyamastyantaḥ kāraṇaṃ tridhā /
icchāsaṃraṃbhabodhākhyā vṛttayaḥ kramato 'sya tu //
1.63.d:
मनो ऽहॄङ्कारबुद्ध्याख्यमस्त्यन्तः कारणं त्रिधा ।
इच्छासंरंभबोधाख्या वृत्तयः क्रमतो ऽस्य तु ॥
1.63.m: The internal organ is threefold, called mind (manas), ego (ahaṅkāra), and intellect (buddhi); / and its functions are desire, impetuosity, and comprehension in order.

1.63.s:
jñānendriyāṇi śrotraṃ tvak cakṣurjihvā ca nāsikā /
grāhyāśca viṣayā hyeṣāṃ jñeyāḥ śabdādayo mune //
1.63.d:
ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुर्जिह्वा च नासिका ।
ग्राह्याश्च विषया ह्येषां ज्ञेयाः शब्दादयो मुने ॥
1.63.m: The organs of knowledge are the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose; / and their perceivable objects, O sage, should be known as sound and the rest.

1.63.s:
śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ śabdādayo matāḥ /
vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāstu karmendriyāṇyapi //
1.63.d:
शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धाः शब्दादयो मताः ।
वाक्पाणिपादपायूपस्थास्तु कर्मेन्द्रियाण्यपि ॥
1.63.m: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are regarded as sound and the rest. / Speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are the organs of action,

1.63.s:
vacanādānagamanotsargānandeṣu karmasu /
karaṇāni ca siddhinā na kṛtiḥ karaṇairvinā //
1.63.d:
वचनादानगमनोत्सर्गानन्देषु कर्मसु ।
करणानि च सिद्धिना न कृतिः करणैर्विना ॥
1.63.m: serving as instruments in the actions of speaking, grasping, walking, evacuation, and sexual pleasure, for accomplishing them; / no action is accomplished without instruments.

1.63.s:
daśadhā karaṇaiśceṣṭāṃ kāryamāviśya kāryate /
ceṣṭante kāryamālaṃbya vibhutvātkaraṇāni tu //
1.63.d:
दशधा करणैश्चेष्टां कार्यमाविश्य कार्यते ।
चेष्टन्ते कार्यमालंब्य विभुत्वात्करणानि तु ॥
1.63.m: Activity is caused to be done tenfold by the instruments, entering into the object; / resting upon the object, the instruments act on account of their pervasiveness.

1.63.s:
tanmātrāṇi tu khavāyustejo 'mbhaḥ kṣmeti pañca vai /
tebhyo bhūtānyekaguṇānyākhyātāni bhavanti hi //
1.63.d:
तन्मात्राणि तु खवायुस्तेजो ऽम्भः क्ष्मेति पञ्च वै ।
तेभ्यो भूतान्येकगुणान्याख्यातानि भवन्ति हि ॥
1.63.m: The subtle elements (tanmātras) are five: space, air, fire, water, and earth. / From them are produced the elements, possessing one [additional] quality each.

1.63.s:
iti pañcasu śabdo 'yaṃ sparśo bhūtacatuṣṭaye /
rūpaṃ triṣu rasaścaiva dvayorgandhaḥ kṣitau tathā //
1.63.d:
इति पञ्चसु शब्दो ऽयं स्पर्शो भूतचतुष्टये ।
रूपं त्रिषु रसश्चैव द्वयोर्गन्धः क्षितौ तथा ॥
1.63.m: Thus, this sound is in five, touch in four elements, / form in three, taste in two, and smell in earth.

1.63.s:
kāryāṇyeṣāṃ krameṇaivāvakāśo vyūhakalpanam /
pākaśca saṃgrahaścaiva dhāraṇaṃ ceti kathyate //
1.63.d:
कार्याण्येषां क्रमेणैवावकाशो व्यूहकल्पनम् ।
पाकश्च संग्रहश्चैव धारणं चेति कथ्यते ॥
1.63.m: Their effects are spoken of in order as: providing space, expansion/grouping, / cooking/ripening, cohesion, and holding/supporting.

1.63.s:
āśītoṣṇau mahā vādyau śītoṣṇau vāritejasoḥ /
bhāsvadagnau jale śuklaṃ kṣitau śuklādyanekadhā //
1.63.d:
आशीतोष्णौ महा वाद्यौ शीतोष्णौ वारितेजसोः ।
भास्वदग्नौ जले शुक्लं क्षितौ शुक्लाद्यनेकधा ॥
1.63.m: Neither cold nor hot is the supreme [space] and the first [air]; cold and hot are water and fire; / radiant is fire; white is water; in earth it is manifold, beginning with white.

1.63.s:
rūpaṃ triṣu rasoṃ'bhaḥ su madhuraḥ ṣaḍidhaḥ kṣitau /
gandhaḥ kṣitāvasurabhiḥ surabhiśca prakīrtitaḥ //
1.63.d:
रूपं त्रिषु रसोंऽभः सु मधुरः षडिधः क्षितौ ।
गन्धः क्षितावसुरभिः सुरभिश्च प्रकीर्तितः ॥
1.63.m: Form is in three; taste in water is sweet, and sixfold in earth; / smell in earth is proclaimed as unpleasant and pleasant.

1.63.s:
tanmātraṃ tadbhūtaguṇaṃ karaṇaṃ poṣaṇaṃ tathā /
bhūtasya tu viśeṣo 'yaṃ viśeṣarahitaṃ tu tat //
1.63.d:
तन्मात्रं तद्भूतगुणं करणं पोषणं तथा ।
भूतस्य तु विशेषो ऽयं विशेषरहितं तु तत् ॥
1.63.m: The tanmātra is the quality of that element, its instrument, and its nourisher. / This gross element has specific qualities, but that [tanmātra] is devoid of specific qualities.

1.63.s:
imāni pañcabhūtāni saṃniviṣṭāni sarvataḥ /
pañcabhūtātmakaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam //
1.63.d:
इमानि पञ्चभूतानि संनिविष्टानि सर्वतः ।
पञ्चभूतात्मकं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
1.63.m: These five elements are present everywhere; / the entire universe, both stationary and moving, consists of the five elements.

1.63.s:
śarīrasaṃniviṣṭatvameṣāṃ tāvannirūpyate /
dehe 'sthimāṃsakeśatvaṅnakhadantāśca pārthivāḥ //
1.63.d:
शरीरसंनिविष्टत्वमेषां तावन्निरूप्यते ।
देहे ऽस्थिमांसकेशत्वङ्नखदन्ताश्च पार्थिवाः ॥
1.63.m: Their presence in the body is now described: / in the body, bone, flesh, hair, skin, nails, and teeth are earthy;

1.63.s:
mūtraraktakaphasvedaśukrādiṣu jalasthitiḥ /
hṛdi paṅktau dṛśoḥ pitte tejastaddharmadarśanāt //
1.63.d:
मूत्ररक्तकफस्वेदशुक्रादिषु जलस्थितिः ।
हृदि पङ्क्तौ दृशोः पित्ते तेजस्तद्धर्मदर्शनात् ॥
1.63.m: the presence of water is in urine, blood, phlegm, sweat, semen, and so forth; / fire is in the heart, in digestion, in the eyes, and in bile, from the observation of its characteristics;

1.63.s:
prāṇādivṛttibhedena vāyuścaivātra saṃsthitaḥ /
viyatsarvāsu nāḍīṣu garbhavṛtyanuṣaṅgataḥ //
1.63.d:
प्राणादिवृत्तिभेदेन वायुश्चैवात्र संस्थितः ।
वियत्सर्वासु नाडीषु गर्भवृत्यनुषङ्गतः ॥
1.63.m: air is present here through the divisions of functions such as the prāṇa; / space is in all the channels (nāḍīs), connected with the inner cavity.

1.63.s:
prayoktyādimahīprāntametadaṇḍārthasādhanam /
pratyātmaniyataṃ bhogabhedato vyavasīyate //
1.63.d:
प्रयोक्त्यादिमहीप्रान्तमेतदण्डार्थसाधनम् ।
प्रत्यात्मनियतं भोगभेदतो व्यवसीयते ॥
1.63.m: This instrument for the purpose of the mundane egg, extending from the agent to the earth, / is determined as specific to each individual self according to the diversity of experience.

1.63.s:
tattvānyevaṃ kalādyāni pratipuṃniyatāni hi /
deheṣu karmavaśataḥ sarveṣu vicaranti hi //
1.63.d:
तत्त्वान्येवं कलाद्यानि प्रतिपुंनियतानि हि ।
देहेषु कर्मवशतः सर्वेषु विचरन्ति हि ॥
1.63.m: Thus the principles, beginning with kalā, are specific to each individual puruṣa; / under the sway of karma, they wander in all bodies.

1.63.s:
māyeyaścaiva pāśo 'yaṃ yenāvṛtamidaṃ jagat /
aśuddhādhvāmato hyeṣa dharaṇyādikalāvadhiḥ //
1.63.d:
मायेयश्चैव पाशो ऽयं येनावृतमिदं जगत् ।
अशुद्धाध्वामतो ह्येष धरण्यादिकलावधिः ॥
1.63.m: This bond, born of māyā, by which this world is enveloped, / is regarded as the impure path (aśuddhādhvan), extending from the earth up to kalā.

1.63.s:
tatra bhūmaṇḍalastho 'sau sthāvaro jaṅgamātmakaḥ /
sthāvarā girivṛkṣādyā jaṅgamastrividhaḥ punaḥ //
1.63.d:
तत्र भूमण्डलस्थो ऽसौ स्थावरो जङ्गमात्मकः ।
स्थावरा गिरिवृक्षाद्या जङ्गमस्त्रिविधः पुनः ॥
1.63.m: Standing in that earthly realm, it consists of stationary and moving beings. / The stationary are mountains, trees, and so forth; the moving are threefold:

1.63.s:
svedajāścāṇḍajāścaiva tathaiva ca jarāyujāḥ /
carācareṣu lakṣāṇāṃ caturāśītiyonayaḥ //
1.63.d:
स्वेदजाश्चाण्डजाश्चैव तथैव च जरायुजाः ।
चराचरेषु लक्षाणां चतुराशीतियोनयः ॥
1.63.m: sweat-born, egg-born, and womb-born. / Among the moving and stationary beings, there are eighty-four hundred thousand wombs.

1.63.s:
bhramamāṇasteṣu jīvaḥ kadācinmānuṣaṃ vapuḥ /
prāpnoti karmavaśataḥ paraṃ sarvārthasādhakam //
1.63.d:
भ्रममाणस्तेषु जीवः कदाचिन्मानुषं वपुः ।
प्राप्नोति कर्मवशतः परं सर्वार्थसाधकम् ॥
1.63.m: Wandering through them, the individual soul (jīva) by the force of karma / sometimes obtains a human body, which is supreme and achieves all ends.

1.63.s:
tatrāpi bhārate khaṇḍe brāhmaṇādikuleṣu ca /
mahāpuṇyavaśenaiva janirbhavati durlabhā //
1.63.d:
तत्रापि भारते खण्डे ब्राह्मणादिकुलेषु च ।
महापुण्यवशेनैव जनिर्भवति दुर्लभा ॥
1.63.m: Even there, in the land of Bhārata and in families of Brāhmaṇas and the rest, / birth is very hard to obtain, occurring only by the power of great merit.

1.63.s:
janiśca puṃstriyoryogaḥ śukraśoṇitayogataḥ /
bindurekaḥ praviśati yadā garbhe dvayātmakaḥ //
1.63.d:
जनिश्च पुंस्त्रियोर्योगः शुक्रशोणितयोगतः ।
बिन्दुरेकः प्रविशति यदा गर्भे द्वयात्मकः ॥
1.63.m: Birth is the union of male and female, through the mixture of semen and ovum; / when a single drop consisting of both enters the womb,

1.63.s:
tadā rajo 'dhike nārī bhavedreto 'dhike pumān /
malakarmādipāśena kaścidātmā niyantritaḥ //
1.63.d:
तदा रजो ऽधिके नारी भवेद्रेतो ऽधिके पुमान् ।
मलकर्मादिपाशेन कश्चिदात्मा नियन्त्रितः ॥
1.63.m: then, if menstrual blood is in excess, a female is formed; if semen is in excess, a male. / Bound by the fetter of impurity, karma, and so forth, some self,

1.63.s:
jīvabhāvaṃ tadā tasminsakalaḥ pratipadyate /
atha tatrāhṛtairmātrā pānānnādyaiśca poṣitaḥ //
1.63.d:
जीवभावं तदा तस्मिन्सकलः प्रतिपद्यते ।
अथ तत्राहृतैर्मात्रा पानान्नाद्यैश्च पोषितः ॥
1.63.m: embodied, then assumes the state of an individual soul (jīva) therein. / Then, nourished there by the drinks, food, and other things consumed by the mother,

1.63.s:
pakṣamāsādikālena vardhate vapuratra hi /
duḥkhādyaḥ pīḍitaścaivācchannadeho jarāyuṇā //
1.63.d:
पक्षमासादिकालेन वर्धते वपुरत्र हि ।
दुःखाद्यः पीडितश्चैवाच्छन्नदेहो जरायुणा ॥
1.63.m: the body here grows over time—by fortnights, months, and so on. / Distressed by pain and covered in the body by the amnion,

1.63.s:
evaṃ tatra sthito garbhe prāgjanmotthaṃ śubhāśubham /
smaraṃstiṣṭati duḥkhātmāpīḍyamāno muhurmuhuḥ //
1.63.d:
एवं तत्र स्थितो गर्भे प्राग्जन्मोत्थं शुभाशुभम् ।
स्मरंस्तिष्टति दुःखात्मापीड्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
1.63.m: remaining thus in the womb, remembering the good and evil arisen from previous births, / afflicted again and again, it remains full of sorrow.

1.63.s:
kālakrameṇa bālo 'sau mātaraṃ pīḍayannapi /
saṃpīḍito niḥsarati yoniyantrādavāṅmukhaḥ //
1.63.d:
कालक्रमेण बालो ऽसौ मातरं पीडयन्नपि ।
संपीडितो निःसरति योनियन्त्रादवाङ्मुखः ॥
1.63.m: In the course of time, that child, causing pain to the mother, / and itself being compressed, emerges head downward from the vaginal tract.

1.63.s:
kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭati niśceṣṭastato roditumicchati /
tataḥ krameṇa sa śiśurvardhamāno dinedine //
1.63.d:
क्षणं तिष्टति निश्चेष्टस्ततो रोदितुमिच्छति ।
ततः क्रमेण स शिशुर्वर्धमानो दिनेदिने ॥
1.63.m: It remains motionless for a moment, and then desires to cry. / Then, gradually growing day by day, that infant,

1.63.s:
bālapaugaṇḍabhedena yuvatvaṃ pratipadyate /
evaṃ krameṇa loke 'smindehināṃ dehasaṃbhavaḥ //
1.63.d:
बालपौगण्डभेदेन युवत्वं प्रतिपद्यते ।
एवं क्रमेण लोके ऽस्मिन्देहिनां देहसंभवः ॥
1.63.m: progressing through the stages of childhood and boyhood, reaches youth. / In this way, by degrees, the embodied state of beings comes to be in this world.

1.63.s:
mānuṣaṃ durlabhaṃ prāpya sarvalokopakārakam /
yastārayati nātmānaṃ tasmātpāpataro 'tra kaḥ //
1.63.d:
मानुषं दुर्लभं प्राप्य सर्वलोकोपकारकम् ।
यस्तारयति नात्मानं तस्मात्पापतरो ऽत्र कः ॥
1.63.m: Having obtained a human birth, which is rare to obtain and beneficial to all worlds, / who can be more sinful in this world than one who does not deliver oneself?

1.63.s:
āhāraścaiva nidrā ca bhayaṃ maithunameva ca /
paśvādīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ sādhāraṇamitīritam //
1.63.d:
आहारश्चैव निद्रा च भयं मैथुनमेव च ।
पश्वादीनां च सर्वेषां च सर्वेषां साधारणमितीरितम् ॥
1.63.m: Food, sleep, fear, and copulation / are declared to be common to all creatures, such as beasts.

1.63.s:
caturṣvevānurakto yaḥ sa mūrkho hyātmadhātakaḥ /
manuṣyāṇāmayaṃ dharmaḥ ravabandhacchedanātmakaḥ //
1.63.d:
चतुर्ष्वेवानुरक्तो यः स मूर्खो ह्यात्मधातकः ।
मनुष्याणामयं धर्मः रवबन्धच्छेदनात्मकः ॥
1.63.m: One who is attached only to these four is a fool and a destroyer of oneself. / This is the duty of human beings: that which consists in cutting the bonds of mundane existence.

1.63.s:
pāśabandhanavicchedo dīkṣayaiva prajāyate /
ato bandhanavicchittyai mantradīkṣāṃ samācaret //
1.63.d:
पाशबन्धनविच्छेदो दीक्षयैव प्रजायते ।
अतो बन्धनविच्छित्त्यै मन्त्रदीक्षां समाचरेत् ॥
1.63.m: The severing of the fetters of bondage is brought about only by initiation (dīkṣā); / therefore, for the cutting of bondage, one should undergo mantra initiation.

1.63.s:
dīkṣājñānākhyayā śaktyā hyapadhvaṃsitabandhanaḥ /
śuddhātmatattvanāmāsau nirvāṇapadamaśnute //
1.63.d:
दीक्षाज्ञानाख्यया शक्त्या ह्यपध्वंसितबन्धनः ।
शुद्धात्मतत्त्वनामासौ निर्वाणपदमश्नुते ॥
1.63.m: With bondage destroyed by the power called initiation-knowledge, / designated as the pure Self-principle, one reaches the state of nirvāṇa.

1.63.s:
svaśaktyātmikayā dṛṣṭyā śivaṃ dhyāyati paśyati /
yajate śivaṃ mantraiśca ravapareṣāṃ hitāya saḥ //
1.63.d:
स्वशक्त्यात्मिकया दृष्ट्या शिवं ध्यायति पश्यति ।
यजते शिवं मन्त्रैश्च रवपरेषां हिताय सः ॥
1.63.m: With vision consisting of his own power, he meditates upon and sees Śiva; / he worships Śiva with mantras for the welfare of others.

1.63.s:
śivārkaśaktidīdhityā samarthīkṛtacidṛśā /
śivaśaktyādibhiḥ sārddhaṃ paśyatyātmagatāvṛttiḥ //
1.63.d:
शिवार्कशक्तिदीधित्या समर्थीकृतचिदृशा ।
शिवशक्त्यादिभिः सार्द्धं पश्यत्यात्मगतावृत्तिः ॥
1.63.m: With consciousness's eye empowered by the rays of the power of the Śiva-sun, / one perceives without inner obstacles, along with the powers of Śiva and the rest.

1.63.s:
antaḥkaraṇavṛttiryā bodhākhyā sā maheśvaram /
na prakāśayituṃ śaktā pāśatvānnigaḍādivat //
1.63.d:
अन्तःकरणवृत्तिर्या बोधाख्या सा महेश्वरम् ।
न प्रकाशयितुं शक्ता पाशत्वान्निगडादिवत् ॥
1.63.m: The mental operation that is named knowledge is not capable of revealing the Great Lord, / because it is an impediment, like fetters and the like.

1.63.s:
dīkṣaiva paramo hetuḥ pāśavicchedane punaḥ /
ataḥ śāstroktavidhinā matradīkṣāṃ samācaret //
1.63.d:
दीक्षैव परमो हेतुः पाशविच्छेदने पुनः ।
अतः शास्त्रोक्तविधिना मत्रदीक्षां समाचरेत् ॥
1.63.m: Initiation alone is the supreme cause for severing the impediments; / therefore, according to the rule declared in the scriptures, one should perform initiation into mantras.

1.63.s:
dīkṣitastantravidhinā svavarṇācāratatparaḥ /
anuṣṭānaṃ prakurvīta nityanamittikātmakam //
1.63.d:
दीक्षितस्तन्त्रविधिना स्ववर्णाचारतत्परः ।
अनुष्टानं प्रकुर्वीत नित्यनमित्तिकात्मकम् ॥
1.63.m: Initiated according to the tantric rule, intent on the conduct of one's own caste, / one should perform practice consisting of obligatory and occasional rites.

1.63.s:
nijavarṇāśramācārānmanasāpi na laṅghayet /
yo yasminnāśrame tiṣṭandīkṣāṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ //
1.63.d:
निजवर्णाश्रमाचारान्मनसापि न लङ्घयेत् ।
यो यस्मिन्नाश्रमे तिष्टन्दीक्षां प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
1.63.m: One should not violate the duties of one's own caste and life-stage even in thought; / in whichever life-stage a person stands when obtaining initiation,

1.63.s:
sa tasminnāśrame tiṣṭhettaddharmānanupālayet /
kṛtānyapi na karmāṇi bandhanāya bhavanti hi //
1.63.d:
स तस्मिन्नाश्रमे तिष्ठेत्तद्धर्माननुपालयेत् ।
कृतान्यपि न कर्माणि बन्धनाय भवन्ति हि ॥
1.63.m: he should remain in that life-stage and uphold its duties; / for actions performed [by him] do not lead to bondage.

1.63.s:
ekaṃ tu phaladaṃ karma mantrānuṣṭhānasaṃbhavam /
dīkṣito 'bhilaṣedbhogānyadyallokagatānasau //
1.63.d:
एकं तु फलदं कर्म मन्त्रानुष्ठानसंभवम् ।
दीक्षितो ऽभिलषेद्भोगान्यद्यल्लोकगतानसौ ॥
1.63.m: Only one action bears fruit: that which arises from the practice of mantras; / whatever enjoyments pertaining to any realm the initiated person may desire,

1.63.s:
mantrārādhanasāmarthyāttadbhuktvā mokṣamaśnute /
nityaṃ naimittikaṃ dīkṣāṃ prāpya yo nācarennaraḥ //
1.63.d:
मन्त्राराधनसामर्थ्यात्तद्भुक्त्वा मोक्षमश्नुते ।
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं दीक्षां प्राप्य यो नाचरेन्नरः ॥
1.63.m: by virtue of the worship of mantras he enjoys them and attains liberation; / the person who, having obtained initiation, does not perform obligatory and occasional rites

1.63.s:
kañcitkālaṃ piśācatvaṃ prāpyānte mokṣamaśnute /
tasmāttu dīkṣitaḥ kuryyānnityanaimittikādikam //
1.63.d:
कञ्चित्कालं पिशाचत्वं प्राप्यान्ते मोक्षमश्नुते ।
तस्मात्तु दीक्षितः कुर्य्यान्नित्यनैमित्तिकादिकम् ॥
1.63.m: becomes a piśāca for some time and at last attains liberation; / therefore the initiated person should perform obligatory and occasional rites and the like,

1.63.s:
anuṣṭhānaṃ ca tenāsya dīkṣāṃ prāpyānumīyate /
nityanaimittikācāra pālakasya narasya tu //
1.63.d:
अनुष्ठानं च तेनास्य दीक्षां प्राप्यानुमीयते ।
नित्यनैमित्तिकाचार पालकस्य नरस्य तु ॥
1.63.m: and by that his practice is inferred after obtaining initiation; / for the person who observes the obligatory and occasional conduct,

1.63.s:
dīkṣāvaikalyavirahātsadyo muktistu jāyate /
tatrāpi gurubhaktasya gatirbhavati nānyathā //
1.63.d:
दीक्षावैकल्यविरहात्सद्यो मुक्तिस्तु जायते ।
तत्रापि गुरुभक्तस्य गतिर्भवति नान्यथा ॥
1.63.m: instant liberation arises due to the absence of deficiency in initiation; / there too, the path is open to one devoted to the guru, not otherwise.

1.63.s:
dīkṣayā gurumūrtisthaḥ sarvānugrāhakaḥ śivaḥ /
dṛṣṭādyarthatayā yasya gurubhaktistu kṛtrimā //
1.63.d:
दीक्षया गुरुमूर्तिस्थः सर्वानुग्राहकः शिवः ।
दृष्टाद्यर्थतया यस्य गुरुभक्तिस्तु कृत्रिमा ॥
1.63.m: Through initiation, Śiva, bestowing grace upon all, abides in the form of the guru; / but he whose devotion to the guru is artificial, meant for visible aims and the like,

1.63.s:
kṛte 'pi viphalaṃ tasya prāyaścittaṃ pade pade /
kāyena manasā vācā gurubhaktiparasya ca //
1.63.d:
कृते ऽपि विफलं तस्य प्रायश्चित्तं पदे पदे ।
कायेन मनसा वाचा गुरुभक्तिपरस्य च ॥
1.63.m: even when penance is performed, it is fruitless for him at every step; / whereas for one wholly devoted to the guru in body, mind, and speech,

1.63.s:
prāyaścittaṃ bhavennaiva siddhistasya pade pade /
gurubhaktiyute śiṣye sarvasvavinivedake //
1.63.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं भवेन्नैव सिद्धिस्तस्य पदे पदे ।
गुरुभक्तियुते शिष्ये सर्वस्वविनिवेदके ॥
1.63.m: no penance is required at all, and accomplishment is his at every step; / when the disciple is endowed with devotion to the guru and offers his all,

1.63.s:
mithyāprayuktamantrastu prāyāścittī bhavedguruḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde triṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.63.d:
मिथ्याप्रयुक्तमन्त्रस्तु प्रायाश्चित्ती भवेद्गुरुः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे त्रिषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
1.63.m:
if the mantra is improperly imparted, the guru must perform penance.

Thus ends the sixty-third chapter in the Third Part of the Great Narrative in the First Section of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.64.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
atha jīvasya pāśaughacchedanāyeṣṭasiddhidam /
dīkṣāvidhiṃ pravakṣyāmi mantrasāmarthyadāyakam //
1.64.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अथ जीवस्य पाशौघच्छेदनायेष्टसिद्धिदम् ।
दीक्षाविधिं प्रवक्ष्यामि मन्त्रसामर्थ्यदायकम् ॥
1.64.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Now I shall describe the rule of initiation that grants the accomplishment of desires, bestows the power of mantras, / and severs the mass of impediments of the individual soul.

1.64.s:
divyaṃ bhāvaṃ yato dadyātkṣiṇuyā dduritāni ca /
ato dīkṣeti sā proktā sarvāgamaviśāradaiḥ //
1.64.d:
दिव्यं भावं यतो दद्यात्क्षिणुया द्दुरितानि च ।
अतो दीक्षेति सा प्रोक्ता सर्वागमविशारदैः ॥
1.64.m: Because it gives (dā-) divine condition and destroys (kṣi-) sins, / it is therefore called dīkṣā by those skilled in all sacred traditions.

1.64.s:
mananaṃ sarvaveditvaṃ trāṇaṃ saṃkhāryanugrahaḥ /
mananātrāṇadharmattvānmantra ityabhidhīyate //
1.64.d:
मननं सर्ववेदित्वं त्राणं संखार्यनुग्रहः ।
मननात्राणधर्मत्त्वान्मन्त्र इत्यभिधीयते ॥
1.64.m: Contemplation (manana) is omniscience, and protection (trāṇa) is grace toward all that is to be accomplished; / because of the properties of contemplating and protecting, it is called a mantra.

1.64.s:
strīpuṃnapuṃsakātmānaste mantrāstu tridhā matāḥ /
strīmantrāstu dviṭhāntāḥ syuḥ puṃmantrā huṃphaḍantakāḥ //
1.64.d:
स्त्रीपुंनपुंसकात्मानस्ते मन्त्रास्तु त्रिधा मताः ।
स्त्रीमन्त्रास्तु द्विठान्ताः स्युः पुंमन्त्रा हुंफडन्तकाः ॥
1.64.m: These mantras are considered to be threefold: feminine, masculine, and neuter; / feminine mantras end in 'dviṭhā' (svāhā), masculine mantras end in 'huṃ phaṭ',

1.64.s:
klībāścaiva narmo 'tāḥ smurmantrāṇāṃ jātayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
pundaivatāstu mantrā syurvidyāḥ strīdaivatā matāḥ //
1.64.d:
क्लीबाश्चैव नर्मो ऽताः स्मुर्मन्त्राणां जातयः स्मृताः ।
पुन्दैवतास्तु मन्त्रा स्युर्विद्याः स्त्रीदैवता मताः ॥
1.64.m: and neuter mantras end in 'namaḥ'—these are taught as the classes of mantras; / masculine-deity mantras are called mantras, while feminine-deity ones are regarded as vidyās.

1.64.s:
ṣaṭ kramasu praśastāste manavastrividhāḥ punaḥ /
tārāntyarephaḥ svāhāstu tatrāgneyāḥ samīritāḥ //
1.64.d:
षट् क्रमसु प्रशस्तास्ते मनवस्त्रिविधाः पुनः ।
तारान्त्यरेफः स्वाहास्तु तत्राग्नेयाः समीरिताः ॥
1.64.m: They are praised in six rites; furthermore, mantras are of three kinds: / those having Oṃ, an ultimate repha, and svāhā are spoken of as fiery;

1.64.s:
saumyāstu bhṛgupīyūṣabījaḍhyāḥ kathitā mune /
agnīṣomātmakā hyevaṃ mantrā jñeyā manīṣibhiḥ //
1.64.d:
सौम्यास्तु भृगुपीयूषबीजढ्याः कथिता मुने ।
अग्नीषोमात्मका ह्येवं मन्त्रा ज्ञेया मनीषिभिः ॥
1.64.m: lunar ones are declared to be endowed with the seed-syllables of Bhṛgu and nectar, O sage; / thus mantras should be understood by the wise to consist of fire and soma.

1.64.s:
bodhamāyānti cāgneyāḥ śvasane piṅgalāśrite /
saumayāścaiva prabudhyante vāme vahati māruteḥ //
1.64.d:
बोधमायान्ति चाग्नेयाः श्वसने पिङ्गलाश्रिते ।
सौमयाश्चैव प्रबुध्यन्ते वामे वहति मारुतेः ॥
1.64.m: Fiery mantras attain awakening when breath resides in the piṅgalā; / and lunar ones awaken when the breath flows in the left channel;

1.64.s:
sarve mantrāḥ prabudhyante vāyau nāḍidvayāśrite /
svāpakāle tu mantrasya japo 'narthaphalapradaḥ //
1.64.d:
सर्वे मन्त्राः प्रबुध्यन्ते वायौ नाडिद्वयाश्रिते ।
स्वापकाले तु मन्त्रस्य जपो ऽनर्थफलप्रदः ॥
1.64.m: all mantras awaken when the breath resides in both channels; / recitation of a mantra during its sleep-time yields untoward results.

1.64.s:
pratyekaṃ mantramuñcārya nāvyānāṃ tānsamuñcaret /
anulobhe binduyuktānvilobhe sargasaṃyutān //
1.64.d:
प्रत्येकं मन्त्रमुञ्चार्य नाव्यानां तान्समुञ्चरेत् ।
अनुलोभे बिन्दुयुक्तान्विलोभे सर्गसंयुतान् ॥
1.64.m: Uttering each mantra, one should pronounce them among the letters: / endowed with the anusvāra in regular order, and with the visarga in reverse order.

1.64.s:
japto yadi sa vai devaṃ prabuddhaḥ kṣiprasiddhidaḥ /
anayā mālayā japto duṣṭamantro 'pi siddhyati //
1.64.d:
जप्तो यदि स वै देवं प्रबुद्धः क्षिप्रसिद्धिदः ।
अनया मालया जप्तो दुष्टमन्त्रो ऽपि सिद्ध्यति ॥
1.64.m: If it is recited thus, the deity is awakened and bestows quick success; / recited with this rosary [of letters], even a flawed mantra succeeds.

1.64.s:
krūre karmāṇi cāgneyāḥ saumyāḥ saumya phalapradāḥ /
śāntajñānetiraudreyaśāntijāti samanvitaḥ //
1.64.d:
क्रूरे कर्माणि चाग्नेयाः सौम्याः सौम्य फलप्रदाः ।
शान्तज्ञानेतिरौद्रेयशान्तिजाति समन्वितः ॥
1.64.m: In cruel rites, fiery mantras bear fruit, and lunar ones in mild rites; / endowed with peaceful knowledge, extremely fierce or peaceful species,

1.64.s:
śānto 'pi raudratāmeti huṃphaṭīpallavayojanāt /
chinnādidoṣayuktāste naiva rakṣanti sādhakam //
1.64.d:
शान्तो ऽपि रौद्रतामेति हुंफटीपल्लवयोजनात् ।
छिन्नादिदोषयुक्तास्ते नैव रक्षन्ति साधकम् ॥
1.64.m: even a peaceful mantra becomes fierce through the addition of the appendage 'huṃ phaṭ'; / affected by flaws such as severed and the like, they do not protect the practitioner at all:

1.64.s:
chinno ruddhaḥ śaktihīnastataścaiva parāṅmukhaḥ /
karmahīno netrahīnaḥ kīlitaḥ staṃbhitastathā //
1.64.d:
छिन्नो रुद्धः शक्तिहीनस्ततश्चैव पराङ्मुखः ।
कर्महीनो नेत्रहीनः कीलितः स्तंभितस्तथा ॥
1.64.m: severed (chinna), obstructed (ruddha), devoid of power (śaktihīna), averse (parāṅmukha), / devoid of ritual (karmahīna), eyeless (netrahīna), nailed (kīlita), paralyzed (staṃbhita),

1.64.s:
dagdhaḥ srastaśca bhītaśca malinaśca tiraskṛtaḥ /
bheditaśca suṣuptaśca madonmattaśca mūrcchitaḥ //
1.64.d:
दग्धः स्रस्तश्च भीतश्च मलिनश्च तिरस्कृतः ।
भेदितश्च सुषुप्तश्च मदोन्मत्तश्च मूर्च्छितः ॥
1.64.m: burnt (dagdha), displaced (srasta), frightened (bhīta), soiled (malina), slighted (tiraskṛta), / divided (bhedita), asleep (suṣupta), intoxicated (madonmatta), unconscious (mūrcchita),

1.64.s:
hatavīryo bhrāntasaṃjñaḥ pradhvasto bālakastathā /
kumāro 'tha yuvā prauḍho vṛddho nistriṃśakastathā //
1.64.d:
हतवीर्यो भ्रान्तसंज्ञः प्रध्वस्तो बालकस्तथा ।
कुमारो ऽथ युवा प्रौढो वृद्धो निस्त्रिंशकस्तथा ॥
1.64.m: deprived of potency (hatavīrya), confused (bhrāntasaṃjña), destroyed (pradhvasta), childish (bālaka), / youth (kumāra), young adult (yuvā), mature (prauḍha), old (vṛddha), heartless (nistriṃśa),

1.64.s:
nirbījaḥ sidvihīnaśca mandaḥ kūṭo niraṃśakaḥ /
sattvahīnaḥ kekaraśca bījahīnaśca dhṛmitaḥ //
1.64.d:
निर्बीजः सिद्विहीनश्च मन्दः कूटो निरंशकः ।
सत्त्वहीनः केकरश्च बीजहीनश्च धृमितः ॥
1.64.m: seedless (nirbīja), devoid of success (siddhivihīna), sluggish (manda), fraudulent (kūṭa), fractionless (niraṃśa), / devoid of sattva (sattvahīna), squinting (kekara), seedless (bījahīna), smoky (dhūmita),

1.64.s:
āliṅgito mohitaśca kṣudhārtaścātidīptakaḥ /
aṅgahīno 'tikruddhaścātikrūre vrīḍitastathā //
1.64.d:
आलिङ्गितो मोहितश्च क्षुधार्तश्चातिदीप्तकः ।
अङ्गहीनो ऽतिक्रुद्धश्चातिक्रूरे व्रीडितस्तथा ॥
1.64.m: embraced (āliṅgita), deluded (mohita), famished (kṣudhārta), excessively blazing (atidīpta), / limbless (aṅgahīna), furious (atikruddha), excessively cruel (atikrūra), ashamed (vrīḍita),

1.64.s:
praśāntamānasaḥ sthānabhraṣṭaśca vikalastathā /
ativṛddho 'tiniḥsnehaḥ pīḍitaśca tathā punaḥ //
1.64.d:
प्रशान्तमानसः स्थानभ्रष्टश्च विकलस्तथा ।
अतिवृद्धो ऽतिनिःस्नेहः पीडितश्च तथा पुनः ॥
1.64.m: tranquil-minded (praśāntamānasa), fallen from place (sthānabhraṣṭa), impaired (vikala), / overly aged (ativṛddha), devoid of affection (atiniḥsneha), and tormented (pīḍita).

1.64.s:
doṣā hyete samākhyātā vakṣyāmyeṣāṃ ca lakṣaṇam /
saṃyuktaṃ vā viyuktaṃ vā tridhā vā svarasaṃyutam //
1.64.d:
दोषा ह्येते समाख्याता वक्ष्याम्येषां च लक्षणम् ।
संयुक्तं वा वियुक्तं वा त्रिधा वा स्वरसंयुतम् ॥
1.64.m: These indeed are declared as the flaws; I shall declare their characteristics: / whether combined or separated, or threefold with vowels,

1.64.s:
manoryasyādimadhyanti vahnibījaṃ tathocyate /
caturddhā pañcadhā vāpi sa mantraśchinnasaṃjñakaḥ //
1.64.d:
मनोर्यस्यादिमध्यन्ति वह्निबीजं तथोच्यते ।
चतुर्द्धा पञ्चधा वापि स मन्त्रश्छिन्नसंज्ञकः ॥
1.64.m: a mantra in whose beginning, middle, or end the fire seed-syllable is stated, / whether fourfold or fivefold, is named 'severed' (chinna);

1.64.s:
manoryasyādimadhyānte bhūbījadvayamucyate /
sa tu ruddho manujñeyo hyatiklaśena siddhidaḥ //
1.64.d:
मनोर्यस्यादिमध्यान्ते भूबीजद्वयमुच्यते ।
स तु रुद्धो मनुज्ञेयो ह्यतिक्लशेन सिद्धिदः ॥
1.64.m: a mantra in whose beginning, middle, and end two earth seed-syllables are stated / is to be known as 'obstructed' (ruddha), granting success only with great trouble;

1.64.s:
tāravarmatrayā lakṣmīrevaṃ hīnastu yo manuḥ /
śaktihīnaḥ sa vijñeyaścirakālaphavapradhaḥ //
1.64.d:
तारवर्मत्रया लक्ष्मीरेवं हीनस्तु यो मनुः ।
शक्तिहीनः स विज्ञेयश्चिरकालफवप्रधः ॥
1.64.m: a mantra that is devoid of the three Oṃ, armor, and Lakṣmī syllables / is to be known as 'powerless' (śaktihīna), yielding fruit only after a long time;

1.64.s:
kāmabījaṃ mukhe māyāhyante caivāṅkuśaṃ tathā /
asau parāṅmukho jñeyo bhajatāṃ cirasiddhidaḥ //
1.64.d:
कामबीजं मुखे मायाह्यन्ते चैवाङ्कुशं तथा ।
असौ पराङ्मुखो ज्ञेयो भजतां चिरसिद्धिदः ॥
1.64.m: with the Kāma seed-syllable at the mouth, Māyā [in the middle], and the goad at the end, / that is to be known as 'averse' (parāṅmukha), granting success to practitioners after a long time;

1.64.s:
ādimadhyāvasāneṣu sakāro dṛśyate yadi /
sa mantro badhiraḥ proktaḥ kaṣṭenālpaphalapradaḥ //
1.64.d:
आदिमध्यावसानेषु सकारो दृश्यते यदि ।
स मन्त्रो बधिरः प्रोक्तः कष्टेनाल्पफलप्रदः ॥
1.64.m: if the letter 'sa' is seen at the beginning, middle, and end, / that mantra is declared 'deaf' (badhira), yielding little fruit with hardship;

1.64.s:
pañcārṇo yadi repharkabinduvarjitavigrahaḥ /
netrahīnastu vijñeyaḥ kleśenāpi na siddhidaḥ //
1.64.d:
पञ्चार्णो यदि रेफर्कबिन्दुवर्जितविग्रहः ।
नेत्रहीनस्तु विज्ञेयः क्लेशेनापि न सिद्धिदः ॥
1.64.m: a five-letter mantra whose body is devoid of the letter 'ra', the sun, and the bindu / is to be known as 'eyeless' (netrahīna), not yielding success even with trouble;

1.64.s:
ādimadhyāvasāneṣu haṃsaḥ prāsādavāgbhavau /
haṃseṃdurvā sakāro vā phakāro varma vā puna //
1.64.d:
आदिमध्यावसानेषु हंसः प्रासादवाग्भवौ ।
हंसेंदुर्वा सकारो वा फकारो वर्म वा पुन ॥
1.64.m: when at the beginning, middle, and end the haṃsa, prāsāda, and vāgbhava seed-syllables, / or haṃsa, the moon, the letter 'sa', the letter 'pha', or the armor,

1.64.s:
māprā namāmi ca padaṃ nāsti yasminsa kīlitaḥ /
evaṃ madhye dvayaṃ mūrghni yasminnasralakārakau //
1.64.d:
माप्रा नमामि च पदं नास्ति यस्मिन्स कीलितः ।
एवं मध्ये द्वयं मूर्घ्नि यस्मिन्नस्रलकारकौ ॥
1.64.m: or the word 'mātrā namāmi' is not present, it is 'nailed' (kīlita); / likewise, in whose middle two and head the weapon (astra) and the letter 'la'

1.64.s:
na vidyete sa mantrastu staṃbhitaḥ siddhirodhakṛt /
agniḥ pavanasaṃyukto manoryasya tu mūrddhani //
1.64.d:
न विद्येते स मन्त्रस्तु स्तंभितः सिद्धिरोधकृत् ।
अग्निः पवनसंयुक्तो मनोर्यस्य तु मूर्द्धनि ॥
1.64.m: are not found, that mantra is 'paralyzed' (staṃbhita), obstructing accomplishment; / when fire combined with wind is at the head of a mantra

1.64.s:
sa sārṇo dṛśyate yastu sa mantro dagdhasaṃjñakaḥ /
asraṃ dvābhyāṃ tribhiḥ ṣaḍbhiraṣṭābhirdṛśyate 'kṣareḥ //
1.64.d:
स सार्णो दृश्यते यस्तु स मन्त्रो दग्धसंज्ञकः ।
अस्रं द्वाभ्यां त्रिभिः षड्भिरष्टाभिर्दृश्यते ऽक्षरेः ॥
1.64.m: and is seen with its vowel, that mantra is named 'burnt' (dagdha); / if the weapon is seen with two, three, six, or eight letters,

1.64.s:
trastaḥ sa mantro vijñeyo mukhe tāravivarjitaḥ /
hakāraḥ śaktirathavā bhīto mantraḥ sa eva hi //
1.64.d:
त्रस्तः स मन्त्रो विज्ञेयो मुखे तारविवर्जितः ।
हकारः शक्तिरथवा भीतो मन्त्रः स एव हि ॥
1.64.m: that mantra is to be known as 'agitated' (trasta); devoid of Oṃ at the beginning, / or with the letter 'ha' or the Śakti seed-syllable, that very mantra is 'frightened' (bhīta).

1.64.s:
manoryasyādimadhyānte syānmakāracatuṣṭayam /
malinastu sa vijñeyo hyatikleśena siddhidaḥ //
1.64.d:
मनोर्यस्यादिमध्यान्ते स्यान्मकारचतुष्टयम् ।
मलिनस्तु स विज्ञेयो ह्यतिक्लेशेन सिद्धिदः ॥
1.64.m:
A mantra in whose beginning, middle, and end there are four [occurrences of the syllable] 'ma'
is to be known as 'defiled' (malina); indeed, it grants success only with excessive hardship.

1.64.s:
dārṇo yasya manormadhye mūrdhni krodhayugaṃ tathā /
asraṃ cāsti sa mantrastu tiraskṛta udīritaḥ //
1.64.d:
दार्णो यस्य मनोर्मध्ये मूर्ध्नि क्रोधयुगं तथा ।
अस्रं चास्ति स मन्त्रस्तु तिरस्कृत उदीरितः ॥
1.64.m:
A mantra in the middle of which is the syllable 'da', likewise a pair of 'krodha' syllables on its head,
and which has an astra, is declared to be 'rebuked' (tiraskṛta).

1.64.s:
myodvayaṃ hṛdayaṃ śīrṣe vaṣaḍvauṣaṭkamadhyamaḥ /
yasya syādbhedito mantrastyājyaḥ kliṣṭaphalapradaḥ //
1.64.d:
म्योद्वयं हृदयं शीर्षे वषड्वौषट्कमध्यमः ।
यस्य स्याद्भेदितो मन्त्रस्त्याज्यः क्लिष्टफलप्रदः ॥
1.64.m:
A mantra that has a pair of 'myo' syllables, 'hṛdaya' in its head, and 'vaṣaṭ' or 'vauṣaṭ' in its middle
is 'split' (bhedita); it is to be abandoned, as it yields painful results.

1.64.s:
tryakṣaro haṃsahīno yaḥ suṣuptaḥ kīrtitastu saḥ /
vidyā vāpyathavā mantro bhavetsaptadaśākṣaraḥ //
1.64.d:
त्र्यक्षरो हंसहीनो यः सुषुप्तः कीर्तितस्तु सः ।
विद्या वाप्यथवा मन्त्रो भवेत्सप्तदशाक्षरः ॥
1.64.m:
A three-syllable [mantra] devoid of 'haṃsa' is proclaimed 'asleep' (suṣupta).
A vidyā or a mantra may consist of seventeen syllables;

1.64.s:
ṣaṭkārapañcakādiryo madonmattastu sa smṛtaḥ /
yasya madhye sthitaṃ cāsraṃ sa mantro mūrcchitaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.64.d:
षट्कारपञ्चकादिर्यो मदोन्मत्तस्तु स स्मृतः ।
यस्य मध्ये स्थितं चास्रं स मन्त्रो मूर्च्छितः स्मृतः ॥
1.64.m:
one that begins with five or six syllables is considered 'madly intoxicated' (madonmatta).
A mantra in whose middle an astra is situated is considered 'fainted' (mūrcchita).

1.64.s:
virāmasthānagaṃ cāsraṃ hatavīryaḥ sa ucyate /
mantrasyādau ca madhye ca mūrdhni cāsracatuṣṭayam //
1.64.d:
विरामस्थानगं चास्रं हतवीर्यः स उच्यते ।
मन्त्रस्यादौ च मध्ये च मूर्ध्नि चास्रचतुष्टयम् ॥
1.64.m:
And when an astra is located at the point of pause, it is called 'bereft of potency' (hatavīrya).
When there are four astras at the beginning, middle, and head of the mantra,

1.64.s:
jñātavyo bhrānta ityeṣa yaḥ syādaṣṭā daśākṣaraḥ /
punarviśativarṇo vā yo mantraḥ smarasaṃyutaḥ //
1.64.d:
ज्ञातव्यो भ्रान्त इत्येष यः स्यादष्टा दशाक्षरः ।
पुनर्विशतिवर्णो वा यो मन्त्रः स्मरसंयुतः ॥
1.64.m:
it should be known as 'confounded' (bhrānta); so too one that has eighteen syllables,
or again twenty syllables, which is joined with the 'smara' seed-syllable,

1.64.s:
hṛllekhākuṃśabījāḍhyaḥ pradhvastaḥ sa kathyate /
saptārṇo bālamantrastu kumāro vasuvarṇavān //
1.64.d:
हृल्लेखाकुंशबीजाढ्यः प्रध्वस्तः स कथ्यते ।
सप्तार्णो बालमन्त्रस्तु कुमारो वसुवर्णवान् ॥
1.64.m:
and endowed with the 'hṛllekhā' and 'aṅkuśa' seed-syllables, is called 'destroyed' (pradhvasta).
A mantra of seven syllables is an infant (bāla), one of eight syllables a youth (kumāra),

1.64.s:
ṣoḍaśārṇo yuvā prauḍhaścatvāriṃśativarṇakaḥ /
triṃśadvarṇaścatuḥṣaṣṭivarṇaścāpi śatākṣaraḥ //
1.64.d:
षोडशार्णो युवा प्रौढश्चत्वारिंशतिवर्णकः ।
त्रिंशद्वर्णश्चतुःषष्टिवर्णश्चापि शताक्षरः ॥
1.64.m:
one of sixteen syllables a young adult (yuvan), one of forty syllables mature (prauḍha),
and a mantra of thirty syllables, sixty-four syllables, or a hundred syllables,

1.64.s:
catuḥśatākṣaro mantro vṛddha ityabhidhīyate /
navārṇastārasaṃyukto mantro nistriṃśa ucyate //
1.64.d:
चतुःशताक्षरो मन्त्रो वृद्ध इत्यभिधीयते ।
नवार्णस्तारसंयुक्तो मन्त्रो निस्त्रिंश उच्यते ॥
1.64.m:
or of four hundred syllables, is designated 'aged' (vṛddha).
A nine-syllable mantra conjoined with the tāra is called 'pitiless' (nistriṃśa),

1.64.s:
yasyānte hṛdayaṃ proktaṃ śiromantro 'tha madhyagaḥ /
śikhā varma ca yasyānte netramasraṃ ca dṛśyate //
1.64.d:
यस्यान्ते हृदयं प्रोक्तं शिरोमन्त्रो ऽथ मध्यगः ।
शिखा वर्म च यस्यान्ते नेत्रमस्रं च दृश्यते ॥
1.64.m:
at whose end 'hṛdaya' is spoken, with the 'śiras' mantra in the middle,
and at whose end 'śikhā' and 'varman' as well as 'netra' and 'astra' are seen.

1.64.s:
śiva śaktyārṇahīno vā nirbījaḥ sa manuḥ smṛtaḥ /
ādyantamadhye phaṭkāraḥ ṣoḍhā yasminpradṛśyate //
1.64.d:
शिव शक्त्यार्णहीनो वा निर्बीजः स मनुः स्मृतः ।
आद्यन्तमध्ये फट्कारः षोढा यस्मिन्प्रदृश्यते ॥
1.64.m:
Or if it lacks the letters of Śiva and Śakti, that mantra is considered seedless.
One in which the sound 'phaṭ' is observed six times at the beginning, middle, and end,

1.64.s:
sa manuḥ siddhihīnaḥ syānmandaḥ paṅktyakṣaro manuḥ /
kūṭa ekākṣaro mantraḥ sa evokto niraṃśakaḥ //
1.64.d:
स मनुः सिद्धिहीनः स्यान्मन्दः पङ्क्त्यक्षरो मनुः ।
कूट एकाक्षरो मन्त्रः स एवोक्तो निरंशकः ॥
1.64.m:
that mantra is destitute of accomplishment. A ten-syllable mantra is sluggish.
A single-syllable mantra is an enigma; that very one is declared to be without parts.

1.64.s:
dvivarṇaḥ sattvahīnaḥ syātkekaraścaturakṣaraḥ /
ṣaḍvarṇo bījahīno vā sārddhasaptākṣaro 'pi vā //
1.64.d:
द्विवर्णः सत्त्वहीनः स्यात्केकरश्चतुरक्षरः ।
षड्वर्णो बीजहीनो वा सार्द्धसप्ताक्षरो ऽपि वा ॥
1.64.m:
A two-syllable mantra is devoid of vital essence, and a four-syllable one is squint-eyed.
A six-syllable one is seedless, or one of seven and a half syllables,

1.64.s:
sārddhadvādaśavarṇo vā dhūmito rniditastu saḥ /
sārddhabījatrayayuto mantro viṃśativarṇavān //
1.64.d:
सार्द्धद्वादशवर्णो वा धूमितो र्निदितस्तु सः ।
सार्द्धबीजत्रययुतो मन्त्रो विंशतिवर्णवान् ॥
1.64.m:
or one of twelve and a half syllables is said to be smoky and censured.
A mantra with three and a half seed-syllables, possessing twenty syllables,

1.64.s:
triṃśadvarṇaścaikaviṃśadvarṇaścārliṅgitastu saḥ /
yo mantro dantavarṇastu mohitaḥ sa tu kīrtitaḥ //
1.64.d:
त्रिंशद्वर्णश्चैकविंशद्वर्णश्चार्लिङ्गितस्तु सः ।
यो मन्त्रो दन्तवर्णस्तु मोहितः स तु कीर्तितः ॥
1.64.m:
thirty syllables, or twenty-one syllables is embraced.
Whatever mantra has thirty-two syllables is proclaimed to be bewildered.

1.64.s:
caturviśativarṇo vā saptaviṃśativarṇavān /
kṣudhārtaḥ sa tu vijñeyo mantrasiddhivivarjitaḥ //
1.64.d:
चतुर्विशतिवर्णो वा सप्तविंशतिवर्णवान् ।
क्षुधार्तः स तु विज्ञेयो मन्त्रसिद्धिविवर्जितः ॥
1.64.m:
One with twenty-four syllables or twenty-seven syllables
is to be known as afflicted by hunger, devoid of mantra-accomplishment.

1.64.s:
ekādaśākṣaro vāpi pañcaviṃśativarṇakaḥ /
trayorviṃśativarṇo vā sa manurdṛptasaṃjñakaḥ //
1.64.d:
एकादशाक्षरो वापि पञ्चविंशतिवर्णकः ।
त्रयोर्विंशतिवर्णो वा स मनुर्दृप्तसंज्ञकः ॥
1.64.m:
Whether of eleven syllables or twenty-five syllables,
or of twenty-three syllables, that mantra is named arrogant.

1.64.s:
ṣaḍviṃśatyakṣaro vāpi ṣaṭtriṃśadvarṇaṅko 'pi vā /
ekona triṃśadarṇo vā mantro hīnāṅgakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.64.d:
षड्विंशत्यक्षरो वापि षट्त्रिंशद्वर्णङ्को ऽपि वा ।
एकोन त्रिंशदर्णो वा मन्त्रो हीनाङ्गकः स्मृतः ॥
1.64.m:
Whether of twenty-six syllables, or of thirty-six syllables,
or of twenty-nine syllables, the mantra is considered deficient in limbs.

1.64.s:
aṣṭāviṃśativarṇo vā tathaikatriṃśadarṇakaḥ /
atikrūraḥ sa vijñeyo 'khilakarmasu garhitaḥ //
1.64.d:
अष्टाविंशतिवर्णो वा तथैकत्रिंशदर्णकः ।
अतिक्रूरः स विज्ञेयो ऽखिलकर्मसु गर्हितः ॥
1.64.m:
Whether of twenty-eight syllables, or likewise of thirty-one syllables,
it is to be known as exceedingly cruel, censured in all rites.

1.64.s:
catvāriṃśatsamārabhya triṣaṣṭyantastu yo manuḥ /
vrīḍitaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ sarvakarmasu na kṣamaḥ //
1.64.d:
चत्वारिंशत्समारभ्य त्रिषष्ट्यन्तस्तु यो मनुः ।
व्रीडितः स तु विज्ञेयः सर्वकर्मसु न क्षमः ॥
1.64.m:
Starting from forty up to sixty-three [syllables], whatever mantra [there is]
is to be known as bashful, incapable in all rites.

1.64.s:
pañcaṣaṣṭyakṣarā mantrā jñeyā vai śāntamānasāḥ /
pañcaṣaṣaaṭyarṇamārabhya navanandākṣarāvadhi //
1.64.d:
पञ्चषष्ट्यक्षरा मन्त्रा ज्ञेया वै शान्तमानसाः ।
पञ्चषषअट्यर्णमारभ्य नवनन्दाक्षरावधि ॥
1.64.m:
Mantras of sixty-five syllables are to be known as peaceful in mind.
Starting from sixty-five syllables up to ninety-nine syllables,

1.64.s:
ye mantrāste tu vijñeyāḥ sthānabhraṣṭā munīśvara /
trayodaśārṇā ye mantrāstithyarṇāśca tathā punaḥ //
1.64.d:
ये मन्त्रास्ते तु विज्ञेयाः स्थानभ्रष्टा मुनीश्वर ।
त्रयोदशार्णा ये मन्त्रास्तिथ्यर्णाश्च तथा पुनः ॥
1.64.m:
those mantras are to be known as fallen from their station, O lord of sages.
Those mantras which have thirteen syllables, and likewise those of fifteen syllables,

1.64.s:
vikasāsteṃ samākhyātāḥ sarvatantraviśāradaiḥ /
śataṃ sārddhaśataṃ vāpi śatadvayamathāpi vā //
1.64.d:
विकसास्तें समाख्याताः सर्वतन्त्रविशारदैः ।
शतं सार्द्धशतं वापि शतद्वयमथापि वा ॥
1.64.m:
are proclaimed to be blown open by those learned in all tantras.
One hundred, or one hundred and fifty, or even two hundred,

1.64.s:
dvinavatyekahīno vā śatatrayamathāpi vā /
ye mantrā varṇasaṃkhyākā niḥsnehāste prakīrtitāḥ //
1.64.d:
द्विनवत्येकहीनो वा शतत्रयमथापि वा ।
ये मन्त्रा वर्णसंख्याका निःस्नेहास्ते प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.64.m:
or ninety-nine, or even three hundred:
those mantras with such numbers of syllables are proclaimed to be devoid of affection.

1.64.s:
catuḥśataṃ samārabhya sahasrārṇāvadhi dvija /
ativṛddhāḥ prayogeṣu śithilāste samīritāḥ //
1.64.d:
चतुःशतं समारभ्य सहस्रार्णावधि द्विज ।
अतिवृद्धाः प्रयोगेषु शिथिलास्ते समीरिताः ॥
1.64.m:
Beginning from four hundred up to a thousand syllables, O twice-born,
they are said to be too old, slack in ritual applications.

1.64.s:
sahasravarṇadadhikā mantrāste pīḍitāhvayāḥ /
tadvarddhvaṃ caiva ye mantrāḥ stotrarūpāstu te smṛtāḥ //
1.64.d:
सहस्रवर्णदधिका मन्त्रास्ते पीडिताह्वयाः ।
तद्वर्द्ध्वं चैव ये मन्त्राः स्तोत्ररूपास्तु ते स्मृताः ॥
1.64.m:
Mantras having more than a thousand syllables are called afflicted.
And whatever mantras are above that are considered to be of the nature of hymns of praise.

1.64.s:
evaṃ vidhāḥ samākhyātā manavo doṣa saṃyutāḥ /
doṣānetānavijñāya mantrānetāñjapanti ye //
1.64.d:
एवं विधाः समाख्याता मनवो दोष संयुताः ।
दोषानेतानविज्ञाय मन्त्रानेताञ्जपन्ति ये ॥
1.64.m:
Mantras endowed with faults have been described in this manner.
Those who, without understanding these faults, recite these mantras,

1.64.s:
siddhirna jāyate teṣāṃ kalpakoṭiśatairapi /
chinnādidoṣaduṣṭānāṃ mantrāṇāṃ sādhanaṃ bruve //
1.64.d:
सिद्धिर्न जायते तेषां कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ।
छिन्नादिदोषदुष्टानां मन्त्राणां साधनं ब्रुवे ॥
1.64.m:
accomplishment does not arise for them even in hundreds of millions of cosmic ages.
I shall declare the purification of mantras defiled by defects such as being broken.

1.64.s:
yonimudrāsane sthitvā prajapedyaḥ samāhitaḥ /
yaṃ kañcidapi vā mantraṃ tasya syuḥ sarvasiddhayaḥ //
1.64.d:
योनिमुद्रासने स्थित्वा प्रजपेद्यः समाहितः ।
यं कञ्चिदपि वा मन्त्रं तस्य स्युः सर्वसिद्धयः ॥
1.64.m:
Stationed in the yonimudrā posture, he who recites with concentrated mind
any mantra whatsoever, to him belong all accomplishments.

1.64.s:
savyapāṣṇi gude sthāpya dakṣiṇaṃ ca dhvajopari /
yonimudrābandha evaṃ bhavedāsanamuttamam //
1.64.d:
सव्यपाष्णि गुदे स्थाप्य दक्षिणं च ध्वजोपरि ।
योनिमुद्राबन्ध एवं भवेदासनमुत्तमम् ॥
1.64.m:
Placing the left heel at the anus and the right upon the penis—
this bind of the yonimudrā becomes an excellent seat.

1.64.s:
anyo 'pyatra prakāro 'sti yonimudrānibandhane /
tadagre sarahasyaṃ te kathayiṣyāmi nārada //
1.64.d:
अन्यो ऽप्यत्र प्रकारो ऽस्ति योनिमुद्रानिबन्धने ।
तदग्रे सरहस्यं ते कथयिष्यामि नारद ॥
1.64.m:
There is another method as well in binding the yonimudrā;
I will tell it to you further on along with its secret, O Nārada.

1.64.s:
pāraṃparyakramaprāpto nityānuṣṭānatatparaḥ /
gurvanujñārataḥ śrīmānabhiṣekasamanvitaḥ //
1.64.d:
पारंपर्यक्रमप्राप्तो नित्यानुष्टानतत्परः ।
गुर्वनुज्ञारतः श्रीमानभिषेकसमन्वितः ॥
1.64.m:
Having attained it through ancestral lineage, intent upon daily observance,
devoted to the guru's permission, glorious, endowed with consecration,

1.64.s:
suṃdaraḥ sumukhaḥ śāntaḥ kulīnaḥ sulabho vaśī /
mantratantrārthatattvajño nigrahānugrahakṣamaḥ //
1.64.d:
सुंदरः सुमुखः शान्तः कुलीनः सुलभो वशी ।
मन्त्रतन्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञो निग्रहानुग्रहक्षमः ॥
1.64.m:
handsome, pleasant-faced, tranquil, well-born, accessible, self-controlled,
knowing the reality of the meaning of mantras and tantras, capable of restraining and blessing,

1.64.s:
nirapekṣo munirdānto hitavādī vicakṣaṇaḥ /
tattvaniṣkāsane dakṣo vinayī ca suveṣavān //
1.64.d:
निरपेक्षो मुनिर्दान्तो हितवादी विचक्षणः ।
तत्त्वनिष्कासने दक्षो विनयी च सुवेषवान् ॥
1.64.m:
indifferent to desire, an ascetic, restrained, speaking beneficial words, discerning,
skilled in extracting truth, modest, and well-attired,

1.64.s:
āśramī dhyānanirataḥ saṃśayacchitsuvuddhimān /
nityānuṣṭānasaṃyuktastvācāryaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
1.64.d:
आश्रमी ध्याननिरतः संशयच्छित्सुवुद्धिमान् ।
नित्यानुष्टानसंयुक्तस्त्वाचार्यः परिकीर्तितः ॥
1.64.m:
belonging to an order of life, intent on meditation, cutting through doubts, very wise,
engaged in daily observances—such a spiritual teacher is proclaimed.

1.64.s:
śānto vinītaḥ śuddhātmā sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutaḥ /
śamādisādhanopetaḥ śraddhāvān susthirāśayaḥ //
1.64.d:
शान्तो विनीतः शुद्धात्मा सर्वलक्षणसंयुतः ।
शमादिसाधनोपेतः श्रद्धावान् सुस्थिराशयः ॥
1.64.m:
Tranquil, modest, pure of soul, endowed with all auspicious marks,
equipped with the means such as composure, full of faith, of very steadfast disposition,

1.64.s:
śuddhadeho 'nnapānadyairddhārmikaḥ śuddhamānasaḥ /
dṛḍhavratasamācāraḥ kṛtajñaḥ pāpabhīrukaḥ //
1.64.d:
शुद्धदेहो ऽन्नपानद्यैर्द्धार्मिकः शुद्धमानसः ।
दृढव्रतसमाचारः कृतज्ञः पापभीरुकः ॥
1.64.m:
pure of body through food and drink, righteous, of pure mind,
firm in vows and conduct, grateful, fearing sin,

1.64.s:
gurudhyānastutikathāsevanāsaktamānasaḥ /
evaṃvidho bhavecchiṣyastvanyathā guruduḥkhadaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde catuḥṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.64.d:
गुरुध्यानस्तुतिकथासेवनासक्तमानसः ।
एवंविधो भवेच्छिष्यस्त्वन्यथा गुरुदुःखदः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे चतुःषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
1.64.m:
with a mind attached to meditating on, praising, speaking of, and serving the guru—
such should a disciple be; otherwise, he causes sorrow to the guru.

Thus ends the sixty-fourth chapter in the third quarter of the Bṛhadupākhyāna in the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.65.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
parīkṣya śiṣyaṃ tu gururmantraśodhanamācaret /
prākpratyagdakṣiṇodakcapañcasūtrāṇi pātayet //
1.65.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
परीक्ष्य शिष्यं तु गुरुर्मन्त्रशोधनमाचरेत् ।
प्राक्प्रत्यग्दक्षिणोदक्चपञ्चसूत्राणि पातयेत् ॥
1.65.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Having tested the disciple, the guru should perform the purification of the mantra.
He should cast five lines east-to-west and south-to-north.

1.65.s:
catuṣṭayaṃ catuṣkānāṃ syādevaṃ nṛpakoṣṭake /
tatrādyaprathame tvādyaṃ dvitīyādye dvitīyakam //
1.65.d:
चतुष्टयं चतुष्कानां स्यादेवं नृपकोष्टके ।
तत्राद्यप्रथमे त्वाद्यं द्वितीयाद्ये द्वितीयकम् ॥
1.65.m:
Thus there will be a group of four tetrads in the sixteen grid-squares.
There, in the first [cell] of the first, the first [letter of the alphabet]; in the first of the second, the second;

1.65.s:
tṛtīyādye tṛtīyaṃ syāñca turthādye turīyakam /
tattadāgneyakoṣṭeṣu tattatpañcamamakṣaram //
1.65.d:
तृतीयाद्ये तृतीयं स्याञ्च तुर्थाद्ये तुरीयकम् ।
तत्तदाग्नेयकोष्टेषु तत्तत्पञ्चममक्षरम् ॥
1.65.m:
in the first of the third will be the third; in the first of the fourth, the fourth;
and in the respective south-east cells, the respective fifth letter.

1.65.s:
vilikhya kramato dhīmānmanuṃ saṃśodhayettataḥ /
nāmādyakṣaramārabhya yāvanmantrādi varṇakam //
1.65.d:
विलिख्य क्रमतो धीमान्मनुं संशोधयेत्ततः ।
नामाद्यक्षरमारभ्य यावन्मन्त्रादि वर्णकम् ॥
1.65.m:
Having written them in order, the wise man should then purify the mantra,
beginning from the first letter of the name up to the initial letter of the mantra.

1.65.s:
catuṣke yatra nāmārṇastatsyātsiddhicatuṣkakam /
prādakṣiṇyāttaddvitīyaṃ sādhyākhyaṃ parikīrtitam //
1.65.d:
चतुष्के यत्र नामार्णस्तत्स्यात्सिद्धिचतुष्ककम् ।
प्रादक्षिण्यात्तद्द्वितीयं साध्याख्यं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
1.65.m:
In the tetrad where the name's letter is, that is the 'accomplished' tetrad.
Clockwise, the second is declared as named 'to be accomplished'.

1.65.s:
tṛtīyaṃ puṃsi siddhākhyaṃ turīyamarisaṃjñakam /
dvayorvarṇāvekakoṣṭe siddhasiddheti tanmatam //
1.65.d:
तृतीयं पुंसि सिद्धाख्यं तुरीयमरिसंज्ञकम् ।
द्वयोर्वर्णावेककोष्टे सिद्धसिद्धेति तन्मतम् ॥
1.65.m:
The third is called 'well-accomplished' for a man; the fourth is named 'enemy'.
If both letters are in one cell, it is regarded as 'accomplished-accomplished'.

1.65.s:
taddvitīye tu mantrārṇe siddhasādhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
tṛtīye tatsusiddhaḥ syātsiddhāristañcaturthake //
1.65.d:
तद्द्वितीये तु मन्त्रार्णे सिद्धसाध्यः प्रकीर्तितः ।
तृतीये तत्सुसिद्धः स्यात्सिद्धारिस्तञ्चतुर्थके ॥
1.65.m:
When the mantra's letter is in the second [tetrad], it is declared as 'accomplished-to be accomplished'.
In the third, it becomes 'accomplished-well-accomplished'; in the fourth, 'accomplished-enemy'.

1.65.s:
nāmārṇānyacatuṣkāttu dvitīye mantravarṇake /
catuṣke cettadā pūrvaṃ yatra nāmākṣaraṃ sthitam //
1.65.d:
नामार्णान्यचतुष्कात्तु द्वितीये मन्त्रवर्णके ।
चतुष्के चेत्तदा पूर्वं यत्र नामाक्षरं स्थितम् ॥
1.65.m:
If the letter of the mantra is in a second tetrad other than the tetrad of the name's letter,
then from the previous place where the name's letter stood,

1.65.s:
tatra tatkoṣṭamārabhya gaṇayetpūrvavatkramāt /
sādhyasiddhaḥ sādhyasādhyastatsusiddhaśca tadripruḥ //
1.65.d:
तत्र तत्कोष्टमारभ्य गणयेत्पूर्ववत्क्रमात् ।
साध्यसिद्धः साध्यसाध्यस्तत्सुसिद्धश्च तद्रिप्रुः ॥
1.65.m:
starting from that cell, he should count in sequence as before:
'to be accomplished-accomplished', 'to be accomplished-to be accomplished', 'to be accomplished-well-accomplished', and 'to be accomplished-enemy'.

1.65.s:
tṛtīye ceñcatuṣke tu yadi syānmantravarṇakaḥ /
tadā pūrvoktarītyā tu kramāddveyaṃ manīṣibhiḥ //
1.65.d:
तृतीये चेञ्चतुष्के तु यदि स्यान्मन्त्रवर्णकः ।
तदा पूर्वोक्तरीत्या तु क्रमाद्द्वेयं मनीषिभिः ॥
1.65.m:
If, however, the letter of the mantra should be in the third tetrad,
then according to the method previously stated, the wise should know in sequence:

1.65.s:
susiddhasiddhastatsādhyastatsusiddhaśca tadṛṣiḥ /
turīye ceñcatuṣke tu tadaivaṃ gaṇayetsudhīḥ //
1.65.d:
सुसिद्धसिद्धस्तत्साध्यस्तत्सुसिद्धश्च तदृषिः ।
तुरीये चेञ्चतुष्के तु तदैवं गणयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.65.m:
'well-accomplished-accomplished', 'well-accomplished-to be accomplished', 'well-accomplished-well-accomplished', and 'well-accomplished-enemy'.
If, however, it is in the fourth tetrad, then the wise man should calculate thus:

1.65.s:
arisiddho 'risādhyaśca tatsusiddhaśca tadripuḥ /
riddhasiddho yathoktena dviguṇātsiddhisādhyakaḥ //
1.65.d:
अरिसिद्धो ऽरिसाध्यश्च तत्सुसिद्धश्च तद्रिपुः ।
रिद्धसिद्धो यथोक्तेन द्विगुणात्सिद्धिसाध्यकः ॥
1.65.m:
'enemy-accomplished', 'enemy-to be accomplished', 'enemy-well-accomplished', and 'enemy-enemy'.
'Accomplished-accomplished' [yields success] as stated; 'accomplished-to be accomplished' by twice the amount.

1.65.s:
siddhaḥ susiddhorddhatayātsiddhārirhati gotrajān /
dviguṇātsādhyasiddhastu sādhyasādhyo vilaṃbataḥ //
1.65.d:
सिद्धः सुसिद्धोर्द्धतयात्सिद्धारिर्हति गोत्रजान् ।
द्विगुणात्साध्यसिद्धस्तु साध्यसाध्यो विलंबतः ॥
1.65.m:
'Accomplished-well-accomplished' by half [the recitation]; 'accomplished-enemy' destroys kinsmen.
'To be accomplished-accomplished' [succeeds] by double; 'to be accomplished-to be accomplished' with delay.

1.65.s:
sādhyaḥ susiddho dviguṇātsādhyārirhanti bāndhavān /
susiddhasiddhorddhatayā tatsādhyo dviguṇājjapāt //
1.65.d:
साध्यः सुसिद्धो द्विगुणात्साध्यारिर्हन्ति बान्धवान् ।
सुसिद्धसिद्धोर्द्धतया तत्साध्यो द्विगुणाज्जपात् ॥
1.65.m:
'To be accomplished-well-accomplished' by double; 'to be accomplished-enemy' slays relatives.
'Well-accomplished-accomplished' by half; 'well-accomplished-to be accomplished' by twice the recitation.

1.65.s:
tatsusiddhaprāptimātrātsusiddhāriḥ kuṭuṃbahṛt /
arisiddhastu putradhno 'riśādhyaḥ kanyakāpahaḥ //
1.65.d:
तत्सुसिद्धप्राप्तिमात्रात्सुसिद्धारिः कुटुंबहृत् ।
अरिसिद्धस्तु पुत्रध्नो ऽरिशाध्यः कन्यकापहः ॥
1.65.m:
'Well-accomplished-well-accomplished' [succeeds] merely upon acquisition; 'well-accomplished-enemy' takes away the family.
'Enemy-accomplished' slays sons; 'enemy-to be accomplished' carries off daughters.

1.65.s:
tatsusiddhaḥ kalatradhnaḥ sādhakadhnore 'pyariḥ smṛtaḥ /
anye 'pyatra prakārā hi saṃti vai bahavoṃ mune //
1.65.d:
तत्सुसिद्धः कलत्रध्नः साधकध्नोरे ऽप्यरिः स्मृतः ।
अन्ये ऽप्यत्र प्रकारा हि संति वै बहवों मुने ॥
1.65.m:
'Enemy-well-accomplished' slays the wife; and 'enemy-enemy' is regarded as slaying the practitioner.
There are also indeed many other methods here, O sage.

1.65.s:
sarveṣu mukhyo 'yaṃ te 'tra kathito kathahābhidhaḥ /
evaṃ saṃśodhya mantraṃ tu śuddhe kāle sthale tathā //
1.65.d:
सर्वेषु मुख्यो ऽयं ते ऽत्र कथितो कथहाभिधः ।
एवं संशोध्य मन्त्रं तु शुद्धे काले स्थले तथा ॥
1.65.m:
Among all of them, this primary one named 'ka-tha-ha' has been told to you here.
Having thus purified the mantra, at a pure time and place,

1.65.s:
dīkṣayeñca guruḥ śiṣyaṃ tadvidhānamudīryate /
nityakṛtyaṃ vidhāyātha praṇamyagurupādukām //
1.65.d:
दीक्षयेञ्च गुरुः शिष्यं तद्विधानमुदीर्यते ।
नित्यकृत्यं विधायाथ प्रणम्यगुरुपादुकाम् ॥
1.65.m:
the guru should initiate the disciple. The rule for that is declared.
Having performed the daily duty, and bowed to the guru's sandals,

1.65.s:
prārthayetsadguruṃ bhaktyābhīṣaaṭārthamādṛtaḥ /
saṃpūjya vastrālaṅkāragohiraṇyadharādibhiḥ //
1.65.d:
प्रार्थयेत्सद्गुरुं भक्त्याभीषअटार्थमादृतः ।
संपूज्य वस्त्रालङ्कारगोहिरण्यधरादिभिः ॥
1.65.m:
One should earnestly petition a true guru with devotion for the desired object,
having worshipped him with garments, ornaments, cows, gold, lands, and the like.

1.65.s:
kṛtvā svasti vidhānaṃ tu maṇḍalādi ca tuṣṭimān /
guruḥ śiṣyeṇa sahitaḥ śuciryāgagṛhaṃ viśet //
1.65.d:
कृत्वा स्वस्ति विधानं तु मण्डलादि च तुष्टिमान् ।
गुरुः शिष्येण सहितः शुचिर्यागगृहं विशेत् ॥
1.65.m:
Having performed the auspicious rite and made the maṇḍala and other preparations, the guru, satisfied
and purified, should enter the sacrificial chamber together with the disciple.

1.65.s:
sāmānyārghodakenātha saṃprokṣya dvāramastrataḥ /
divyānutsārayedvighnānnabhasthānarcya vāriṇā //
1.65.d:
सामान्यार्घोदकेनाथ संप्रोक्ष्य द्वारमस्त्रतः ।
दिव्यानुत्सारयेद्विघ्नान्नभस्थानर्च्य वारिणा ॥
1.65.m:
Then, having sprinkled the doorway with water from the ordinary offering using the astra mantra,
he should drive away divine obstacles situated in the sky by sprinkling with water.

1.65.s:
pārṣṇighātaistribhirbhauṃmāṃstataḥ karma samācaret /
varṇakaiḥ sarvatobhadre yathoktaparikalpite //
1.65.d:
पार्ष्णिघातैस्त्रिभिर्भौंमांस्ततः कर्म समाचरेत् ।
वर्णकैः सर्वतोभद्रे यथोक्तपरिकल्पिते ॥
1.65.m:
With three strikes of the heel, he should drive away the earthly [obstacles], and then perform the ritual action
upon a sarvatobhadra [maṇḍala] designed as prescribed with coloured powders.

1.65.s:
vahnimaṇḍalamabhyarcya tatkalāḥ paripūjya ca /
astraprakṣālitaṃ kuṃbhaṃ yathāśakti vinirmitam //
1.65.d:
वह्निमण्डलमभ्यर्च्य तत्कलाः परिपूज्य च ।
अस्त्रप्रक्षालितं कुंभं यथाशक्ति विनिर्मितम् ॥
1.65.m:
Having worshipped the maṇḍala of fire and thoroughly worshipped its portions (kalās),
he should ritually place there a pot washed with the astra [mantra], fashioned according to capacity,

1.65.s:
tatra saṃsthāpya vidhivattatra bhānoḥ kalāṃ yajet /
vilomamātṛkāmūlamuñcaran śuddhavāriṇā //
1.65.d:
तत्र संस्थाप्य विधिवत्तत्र भानोः कलां यजेत् ।
विलोममातृकामूलमुञ्चरन् शुद्धवारिणा ॥
1.65.m:
and worship there in due order the portions of the sun,
reciting the fundamental mantra with the mātṛkā in reverse order while filling [it] with pure water.

1.65.s:
āpūrya kuṃbhaṃ tatrārcetsomasya vidhivatkalāḥ /
dhūmrārcirūṣmā jvalinī jvālinī visphuliṅginī //
1.65.d:
आपूर्य कुंभं तत्रार्चेत्सोमस्य विधिवत्कलाः ।
धूम्रार्चिरूष्मा ज्वलिनी ज्वालिनी विस्फुलिङ्गिनी ॥
1.65.m:
Having filled the pot, he should worship there according to rule the portions of the moon:
Dhūmrārci, Ūṣmā, Jvalinī, Jvālinī, Visphuliṅginī,

1.65.s:
suśrīḥ surūpā kapilā havyakavyavahā tathā /
vahnerdaśa kalāḥ proktāḥ procyante 'tha raveḥ kalāḥ //
1.65.d:
सुश्रीः सुरूपा कपिला हव्यकव्यवहा तथा ।
वह्नेर्दश कलाः प्रोक्ताः प्रोच्यन्ते ऽथ रवेः कलाः ॥
1.65.m:
Suśrī, Surūpā, Kapilā, and Havyakavyavahā—
these are proclaimed the ten portions of fire; next the portions of the sun are proclaimed:

1.65.s:
tapinī tāpinī dhūmrā marīcijvālinī ruciḥ /
suṣumṇā bhogadā viśvā bodhinī dhāriṇī kṣamā //
1.65.d:
तपिनी तापिनी धूम्रा मरीचिज्वालिनी रुचिः ।
सुषुम्णा भोगदा विश्वा बोधिनी धारिणी क्षमा ॥
1.65.m:
Tapinī, Tāpinī, Dhūmrā, Marīci, Jvālinī, Ruci,
Suṣumṇā, Bhogadā, Viśvā, Bodhinī, Dhāriṇī, and Kṣamā.

1.65.s:
athendrośca kalā jñeyā hyamṛtā mānadā punaḥ /
pūṣā tuṣṭiśca puṣṭiśca ratiśca dhṛtisaṃjñikāḥ //
1.65.d:
अथेन्द्रोश्च कला ज्ञेया ह्यमृता मानदा पुनः ।
पूषा तुष्टिश्च पुष्टिश्च रतिश्च धृतिसंज्ञिकाः ॥
1.65.m:
Now the portions of the moon are to be known: Amṛtā, Mānadā, further
Pūṣā, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Rati, Dhṛti,

1.65.s:
śaśinī candrikā kātirjyotsnā śrīḥ prītiraṅgadā /
pūrṇāpūrṇāmṛtā ceti proktāścandramasaḥ kalāḥ //
1.65.d:
शशिनी चन्द्रिका कातिर्ज्योत्स्ना श्रीः प्रीतिरङ्गदा ।
पूर्णापूर्णामृता चेति प्रोक्ताश्चन्द्रमसः कलाः ॥
1.65.m:
Śaśinī, Candrikā, Kānti, Jyotsnā, Śrī, Prīti, Aṅgadā,
Pūrṇā, and Pūrṇāmṛtā—these are proclaimed the portions of the moon.

1.65.s:
vasrayugmena saṃveṣṭya tasminsarvaiṣadhīḥ kṣipet /
navaratnāni nikṣipya vinyasetpañcapallavān //
1.65.d:
वस्रयुग्मेन संवेष्ट्य तस्मिन्सर्वैषधीः क्षिपेत् ।
नवरत्नानि निक्षिप्य विन्यसेत्पञ्चपल्लवान् ॥
1.65.m:
Having wrapped [the pot] with a pair of cloths, he should cast all medicinal herbs into it;
having dropped in the nine gems, he should place the five sprouts upon it.

1.65.s:
panasāmravaṭāśvatthavakuleti ca tān viduḥ /
muktāmāṇikyavaiḍūryagomedānvajravidrumau //
1.65.d:
पनसाम्रवटाश्वत्थवकुलेति च तान् विदुः ।
मुक्तामाणिक्यवैडूर्यगोमेदान्वज्रविद्रुमौ ॥
1.65.m:
Those are known as breadfruit, mango, banyan, sacred fig, and bakula;
pearl, ruby, cat's-eye, zircon, diamond, and coral,

1.65.s:
padmarāgaṃ marakataṃ nīlaṃ ceti yathākram /
evaṃ ratnāni nikṣipya tatrāvāhyeṣṭadevatām //
1.65.d:
पद्मरागं मरकतं नीलं चेति यथाक्रम् ।
एवं रत्नानि निक्षिप्य तत्रावाह्येष्टदेवताम् ॥
1.65.m:
ruby (padmarāga), emerald, and sapphire—in due sequence.
Having placed these gems thus, and having invoked the chosen deity there

1.65.s:
saṃpūjya vidhivanmantrī tataḥ śiṣyaṃ svalaṅkṛtam /
vedyāṃ saṃveśya saṃprokṣya prokṣaṇīsthena vāriṇā //
1.65.d:
संपूज्य विधिवन्मन्त्री ततः शिष्यं स्वलङ्कृतम् ।
वेद्यां संवेश्य संप्रोक्ष्य प्रोक्षणीस्थेन वारिणा ॥
1.65.m:
and worshipped [it] according to rule, the mantra-practitioner then seats the well-adorned disciple
upon the altar and sprinkles him with the water remaining in the sprinkling vessel.

1.65.s:
bhūtaśuddhyādikaṃ katvā taccharīre vidhānataḥ /
nyāsajālena saṃśodhya mūrdhni vinyasya pallavān //
1.65.d:
भूतशुद्ध्यादिकं कत्वा तच्छरीरे विधानतः ।
न्यासजालेन संशोध्य मूर्ध्नि विन्यस्य पल्लवान् ॥
1.65.m:
Having performed the purification of elements and other rites upon his body according to rule,
and having purified him by the network of nyāsas, placing the sprouts upon his head,

1.65.s:
aṣṭottaraśatenātha mūlamantreṇa mantritaiḥ /
abhiṣiñcetpriyaṃ śiṣyaṃ japanmūlamanuṃ hṛdi //
1.65.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतेनाथ मूलमन्त्रेण मन्त्रितैः ।
अभिषिञ्चेत्प्रियं शिष्यं जपन्मूलमनुं हृदि ॥
1.65.m:
he should then consecrate his dear disciple with waters consecrated one hundred and eight times
with the fundamental mantra, reciting the fundamental mantra in his heart.

1.65.s:
śiṣṭodakena vācamya paridhāyāṃbaraṃ śiśuḥ /
guruṃ praṇamya vidhivatsaṃviśetpurataḥ śuciḥ //
1.65.d:
शिष्टोदकेन वाचम्य परिधायांबरं शिशुः ।
गुरुं प्रणम्य विधिवत्संविशेत्पुरतः शुचिः ॥
1.65.m:
Having sipped the remaining water and put on a garment, the young [disciple],
purified, should prostrate before the guru according to rule and sit down before him.

1.65.s:
atha śiṣyasya śirasi hastaṃ datvā gurustataḥ /
japedaṣṭottaraśataṃ deyamantraṃ vidhānataḥ //
1.65.d:
अथ शिष्यस्य शिरसि हस्तं दत्वा गुरुस्ततः ।
जपेदष्टोत्तरशतं देयमन्त्रं विधानतः ॥
1.65.m:
Then, placing his hand upon the head of the disciple, the guru
should recite one hundred and eight times according to rule the mantra to be imparted.

1.65.s:
samo 'stvityakṣarāndadyāttataṛ śiṣyor'cayedgurum /
tataḥ sacandanaṃ hastaṃ datvā śiṣyasya mastake //
1.65.d:
समो ऽस्त्वित्यक्षरान्दद्यात्ततऋ शिष्योर्ऽचयेद्गुरुम् ।
ततः सचन्दनं हस्तं दत्वा शिष्यस्य मस्तके ॥
1.65.m:
He should impart the syllables: 'May you be equal [to me]'; then the disciple should worship the guru.
Thereafter, placing his sandalwood-anointed hand upon the disciple's head,

1.65.s:
tatkarṇe pravadedvidyāmaṣṭavāraṃ samāhitaḥ /
saṃprāptavidyaḥ śiṣyo 'pi nipatedgurupādayoḥ //
1.65.d:
तत्कर्णे प्रवदेद्विद्यामष्टवारं समाहितः ।
संप्राप्तविद्यः शिष्यो ऽपि निपतेद्गुरुपादयोः ॥
1.65.m:
he should carefully recite the vidyā into his ear eight times;
and the disciple, having received the vidyā, should fall at the guru's feet:

1.65.s:
uttiṣṭha vatsa mukte 'si samyagācāravānbhava /
kīrtiśrīkāntiputrāyurbalārogya sadāstu te //
1.65.d:
उत्तिष्ठ वत्स मुक्ते ऽसि सम्यगाचारवान्भव ।
कीर्तिश्रीकान्तिपुत्रायुर्बलारोग्य सदास्तु ते ॥
1.65.m:
'Arise, my child, you are liberated! Be of proper conduct;
may fame, splendour, lustre, sons, longevity, strength, and health be yours forever!'

1.65.s:
tataḥ śiṣyaḥ samutthāya gandhādyairgurumarcayet /
dadyāñca dakṣiṇāṃ tasmai vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ //
1.65.d:
ततः शिष्यः समुत्थाय गन्धाद्यैर्गुरुमर्चयेत् ।
दद्याञ्च दक्षिणां तस्मै वित्तशाठ्यविवर्जितः ॥
1.65.m:
Then the disciple, rising up, should worship the guru with perfumes and other offerings,
and should give him a sacrificial fee, free of crookedness regarding wealth.

1.65.s:
saṃprāpyaivaṃ gurormantraṃ tadārabhya dhanādibhiḥ /
dehaputrakalatraiśca gurusevāparo bhavet //
1.65.d:
संप्राप्यैवं गुरोर्मन्त्रं तदारभ्य धनादिभिः ।
देहपुत्रकलत्रैश्च गुरुसेवापरो भवेत् ॥
1.65.m:
Having thus received the mantra from the guru, he should from then on be devoted
to the service of the guru with wealth, his own body, sons, and wife.

1.65.s:
svaṣṭadevaṃ yajenmadhye datvā puṣpāñjaliṃ tataḥ /
agninairṛtivāgīśān krameṇa paripījayet //
1.65.d:
स्वष्टदेवं यजेन्मध्ये दत्वा पुष्पाञ्जलिं ततः ।
अग्निनैरृतिवागीशान् क्रमेण परिपीजयेत् ॥
1.65.m:
Having offered a handful of flowers, he should worship his chosen deity in the centre;
then he should worship in sequence [the deities of] Agni, Nirṛti, and the Lord of Speech.

1.65.s:
yadā madhye yajedviṣṇuṃ bāhyādiṣu vināyakam /
raviṃ śivāṃ śivaṃ caiva yadā madhye tu śaṅkaram //
1.65.d:
यदा मध्ये यजेद्विष्णुं बाह्यादिषु विनायकम् ।
रविं शिवां शिवं चैव यदा मध्ये तु शङ्करम् ॥
1.65.m:
When he worships Viṣṇu in the centre, [he should worship] Vināyaka, the Sun, Śivā, and Śiva in the outer [positions];
when, however, he worships Śaṅkara in the centre,

1.65.s:
raviṃ gaṇeśamaṃbāṃ ca hariṃ cātha yadā śivām /
īśaṃ vighnārkagovindānmadhye cedgaṇanāyakam //
1.65.d:
रविं गणेशमंबां च हरिं चाथ यदा शिवाम् ।
ईशं विघ्नार्कगोविन्दान्मध्ये चेद्गणनायकम् ॥
1.65.m:
[he should worship] the Sun, Gaṇeśa, the Mother, and Hari; when [he worships] Śivā,
[he should worship] Īśa, Vighna, Arka, and Govinda; if he worships Gaṇanāyaka in the centre,

1.65.s:
śivaṃ śivāṃ raviṃ viṣṇuṃ ravau madhyagate punaḥ /
gaṇeṣaṃ viṣṇumaṃbāṃ ca śivaṃ ceti yathākramam //
1.65.d:
शिवं शिवां रविं विष्णुं रवौ मध्यगते पुनः ।
गणेषं विष्णुमंबां च शिवं चेति यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.65.m:
[he should worship] Śiva, Śivā, the Sun, and Viṣṇu; and when the Sun is placed in the centre,
[he should worship] Gaṇeśa, Viṣṇu, the Mother, and Śiva, in due sequence.

1.65.s:
evaṃ nitya samabhyarcya devapañcakamādṛtaḥ /
brāhme muhūrtte hyutthāya kṛtvācā vaśyakaṃ budhaḥ //
1.65.d:
एवं नित्य समभ्यर्च्य देवपञ्चकमादृतः ।
ब्राह्मे मुहूर्त्ते ह्युत्थाय कृत्वाचा वश्यकं बुधः ॥
1.65.m:
Having thus daily and attentively worshipped the pentad of deities,
the wise man, rising in the brāhma muhūrta and performing the necessary duties,

1.65.s:
aśaṅkito vā śayyāyāṃ svakīyaśirasi smaret /
sahasradalaśuklābjakārṃṇakāsthadumaṇḍale //
1.65.d:
अशङ्कितो वा शय्यायां स्वकीयशिरसि स्मरेत् ।
सहस्रदलशुक्लाब्जकार्ंणकास्थदुमण्डले ॥
1.65.m:
free from doubt, or while in bed, should meditate upon his own head,
in the circle situated in the pericarp of the thousand-petalled white lotus,

1.65.s:
akathāditrikoṇasthaṃ varābhayakaraṃ gurum /
dvinetraṃ dvibhujaṃ śuklagandhamālyānuṃlepanam //
1.65.d:
अकथादित्रिकोणस्थं वराभयकरं गुरुम् ।
द्विनेत्रं द्विभुजं शुक्लगन्धमाल्यानुंलेपनम् ॥
1.65.m:
upon the guru seated in the triangle beginning with 'a', 'ka', and 'tha', making the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness,
two-eyed, two-armed, anointed with white perfumes, ointments, and garlands,

1.65.s:
vāme śaktyā yutaṃ dhyātvā mānasairupacārakaiḥ /
ārādhya pādukāmantraṃ daśadhāprajapetsudhīḥ //
1.65.d:
वामे शक्त्या युतं ध्यात्वा मानसैरुपचारकैः ।
आराध्य पादुकामन्त्रं दशधाप्रजपेत्सुधीः ॥
1.65.m:
accompanied by his Śakti on his left; having meditated [upon him] and worshipped him with mental offerings,
the wise practitioner should recite the pādukā mantra ten times:

1.65.s:
vā māyā śrīrbhagendvāḍhyā viyaddhaṃsakhakāgnayaḥ /
hasakṣamalavāryagnivāmakarṇaiduyugmarut //
1.65.d:
वा माया श्रीर्भगेन्द्वाढ्या वियद्धंसखकाग्नयः ।
हसक्षमलवार्यग्निवामकर्णैदुयुग्मरुत् ॥
1.65.m:
'vā', māyā, śrī, joined with bhaga and indu; space, haṃsa, ether, and fire;
'ha-sa-kṣa-ma-la-va-ra-ya-ūṃ', with the left ear, paired with the moon and wind;

1.65.s:
tato bhṛgvākāśaravāgnibhagendvāḍhyāḥ parantimaḥ /
sahakṣamalatoyāgnicandraśāntiyuto marut //
1.65.d:
ततो भृग्वाकाशरवाग्निभगेन्द्वाढ्याः परन्तिमः ।
सहक्षमलतोयाग्निचन्द्रशान्तियुतो मरुत् ॥
1.65.m:
then Bhṛgu, space, sound, fire, joined with bhaga and indu; the subsequent, final [syllables]:
'sa-ha-kṣa-ma-la-toya-agni', conjoined with moon, śānti, and wind;

1.65.s:
tataḥ śrīścāmukānte tu nandanāthāmukī punaḥ /
devyaṃbānte śrīpāndukāṃ pūjayāmi hṛdantime //
1.65.d:
ततः श्रीश्चामुकान्ते तु नन्दनाथामुकी पुनः ।
देव्यंबान्ते श्रीपान्दुकां पूजयामि हृदन्तिमे ॥
1.65.m:
then 'śrī', and at the end of [the guru's name] 'amuka' [the word] 'nandanātha', then [for the Śakti's name] 'amukī',
and at the end of 'devyambā' [the phrase] 'I worship the holy sandals' (śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi), concluding with 'hṛd'.

1.65.s:
ayaṃ śrīpādukāmantraḥ sarvasiddhiprado nṛṇām /
guhyeti ca samarpyātha mantrairetairnametsudhīḥ //
1.65.d:
अयं श्रीपादुकामन्त्रः सर्वसिद्धिप्रदो नृणाम् ।
गुह्येति च समर्प्याथ मन्त्रैरेतैर्नमेत्सुधीः ॥
1.65.m:
This holy pādukā mantra bestows all siddhis upon men;
having dedicated it [with the words] 'You are the secret...', the wise man should bow with these mantras.

1.65.s:
akhaṇḍamaṇḍalākāraṃ vyāptaṃ yena carācaram /
tatpadaṃ darśitaṃ yena tasmai śrīgurave namaḥ //
1.65.d:
अखण्डमण्डलाकारं व्याप्तं येन चराचरम् ।
तत्पदं दर्शितं येन तस्मै श्रीगुरवे नमः ॥
1.65.m: By whom the entire circular universe of moving and unmoving beings is pervaded, / by whom that state has been shown, homage to that glorious guru.

1.65.s:
ajñānatimirāndhasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā /
cakṣurunmīlitaṃ yena tasmai śrīgurave namaḥ //
1.65.d:
अज्ञानतिमिरान्धस्य ज्ञानाञ्जनशलाकया ।
चक्षुरुन्मीलितं येन तस्मै श्रीगुरवे नमः ॥
1.65.m: By whom the eyes of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance / were opened with the collyrium-stick of knowledge, homage to that glorious guru.

1.65.s:
namo 'stu gurave tasmā iṣṭadevasvarūpiṇe /
yasya vāgamṛtaṃ hṝnti viṣaṃ saṃsārasaṃjñakam //
1.65.d:
नमो ऽस्तु गुरवे तस्मा इष्टदेवस्वरूपिणे ।
यस्य वागमृतं हॄन्ति विषं संसारसंज्ञकम् ॥
1.65.m: Homage be to that guru whose form is the chosen deity, / the nectar of whose speech destroys the poison known as worldly existence.

1.65.s:
iti natvā paṭhetstotraṃ sadyaḥ pratyayakārakam /
oṃ namaste nātha bhagavān śivāya gururūpiṇe //
1.65.d:
इति नत्वा पठेत्स्तोत्रं सद्यः प्रत्ययकारकम् ।
ओं नमस्ते नाथ भगवान् शिवाय गुरुरूपिणे ॥
1.65.m: Having bowed thus, one should recite the hymn that instantly creates conviction: / 'Oṃ, homage to you, O Lord, who are Śiva in the form of the guru,

1.65.s:
vidyāvatārasaṃsiddhyai svīkṛtānekavigraha /
navāya tanarūpāya paramārthaikarūpiṇe //
1.65.d:
विद्यावतारसंसिद्ध्यै स्वीकृतानेकविग्रह ।
नवाय तनरूपाय परमार्थैकरूपिणे ॥
1.65.m: who have assumed manifold bodies for the perfection of the incarnation of wisdom, / who are new, whose form is the body, whose single nature is the ultimate reality,

1.65.s:
sarvājñānatamobhedabhānave ciddhanāya te /
statantrāya dayākḷptavigrahāya śivātmane //
1.65.d:
सर्वाज्ञानतमोभेदभानवे चिद्धनाय ते ।
स्ततन्त्राय दयाकॢप्तविग्रहाय शिवात्मने ॥
1.65.m: the sun that dispels all the darkness of ignorance, a mass of consciousness, / independent, whose body is fashioned out of compassion, whose nature is Śiva,

1.65.s:
paratra trāya bhaktānāṃ bhavyānāṃ bhāvarūpiṇe /
vivekināṃ vivekāya vimarśāya vimarśinām //
1.65.d:
परत्र त्राय भक्तानां भव्यानां भावरूपिणे ।
विवेकिनां विवेकाय विमर्शाय विमर्शिनाम् ॥
1.65.m: the protector in the beyond for devotees, the essence of being for the auspicious, / discernment for the discerning, reflective awareness for the reflective,

1.65.s:
prakāśānāṃ prakāśāya jñānināṃ jñānarūpiṇe /
purastātpārśvayoḥ pṛṣṭe namastubhyamuparyadhaḥ //
1.65.d:
प्रकाशानां प्रकाशाय ज्ञानिनां ज्ञानरूपिणे ।
पुरस्तात्पार्श्वयोः पृष्टे नमस्तुभ्यमुपर्यधः ॥
1.65.m: the light of lights, whose nature is knowledge for the wise! / Homage to you in front, on both flanks, behind, above, and below!

1.65.s:
sadā sañcitsvarūpeṇa vidhehi bhavadāsanam /
tvatprasādādahaṃ deva kṛtākṛtyo 'smi sarvataḥ //
1.65.d:
सदा सञ्चित्स्वरूपेण विधेहि भवदासनम् ।
त्वत्प्रसादादहं देव कृताकृत्यो ऽस्मि सर्वतः ॥
1.65.m: Always establish your seat with the nature of pure existence and consciousness. / By your grace, O God, I have accomplished all that was to be done in every way.

1.65.s:
māyāmṛtyumahāpāśādvimukto 'smi śivo 'smi vaḥ /
iti stutvā tataḥ sarva gurave vinivedayet //
1.65.d:
मायामृत्युमहापाशाद्विमुक्तो ऽस्मि शिवो ऽस्मि वः ।
इति स्तुत्वा ततः सर्व गुरवे विनिवेदयेत् ॥
1.65.m: I am freed from the great snare of illusion and death; I am Śiva, indeed.' / Having praised thus, one should then dedicate everything to the guru:

1.65.s:
prātaḥ prabhṛti sāyāntaṃ sāṃyādiprātarantataḥ /
yatkaromi jagannātha tadastu tava pūjanam //
1.65.d:
प्रातः प्रभृति सायान्तं सांयादिप्रातरन्ततः ।
यत्करोमि जगन्नाथ तदस्तु तव पूजनम् ॥
1.65.m: 'From morning until evening, and from evening until morning, / whatever I do, O Lord of the universe, let that be your worship.'

1.65.s:
tataśca gurupādābjagalitāmṛtadhārayā /
kṣālitaṃ nijamātmānaṃ lirmalaṃ bhāvayetsudhīḥ //
1.65.d:
ततश्च गुरुपादाब्जगलितामृतधारया ।
क्षालितं निजमात्मानं लिर्मलं भावयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.65.m: Then the wise person should contemplate oneself as cleansed and spotless / by the stream of nectar trickling from the lotus feet of the guru.

1.65.s:
mūlādibrahmarandhrāntaṃ mūlavidyāṃ vibhāvayet /
mūlādhārādadho bhāge vartulaṃ vāyumaṇḍalam //
1.65.d:
मूलादिब्रह्मरन्ध्रान्तं मूलविद्यां विभावयेत् ।
मूलाधारादधो भागे वर्तुलं वायुमण्डलम् ॥
1.65.m: One should contemplate the root-knowledge from the mūlādhāra up to the brahmarandhra. / Below the mūlādhāra is the circular maṇḍala of wind.

1.65.s:
tatrasthavāyubījotthavāyunā ca tadrūrddhvakam /
trikoṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vahnestatrasthavahnibījataḥ //
1.65.d:
तत्रस्थवायुबीजोत्थवायुना च तद्रूर्द्ध्वकम् ।
त्रिकोणं मण्डलं वह्नेस्तत्रस्थवह्निबीजतः ॥
1.65.m: Above it, through the wind arisen from the wind-seed-syllable situated there, / is the triangular maṇḍala of fire. By the fire arisen from the fire-seed-syllable situated there,

1.65.s:
utpannenāgninā mūlādhārāvasthitavigrahām /
prasuptabhujagākārāṃ svayaṃbhūliṅgaveṣṭinīm //
1.65.d:
उत्पन्नेनाग्निना मूलाधारावस्थितविग्रहाम् ।
प्रसुप्तभुजगाकारां स्वयंभूलिङ्गवेष्टिनीम् ॥
1.65.m: having contemplated the Kulakuṇḍalinī, whose form resides in the mūlādhāra, / who has the form of a sleeping serpent, coiling around the self-existent liṅga,

1.65.s:
visatantunibhāṃ koṭividyudābhāṃ tanīyasīm /
kulakuṇḍalinīṃ dhyātvā kūrcenotthāpayeñca tām //
1.65.d:
विसतन्तुनिभां कोटिविद्युदाभां तनीयसीम् ।
कुलकुण्डलिनीं ध्यात्वा कूर्चेनोत्थापयेञ्च ताम् ॥
1.65.m: resembling a lotus filament, radiant as ten million flashes of lightning, extremely subtle, / one should awaken her with the kūrca-bīja.

1.65.s:
suṣumṇāvartmanātāṃ ca ṣaṭcakrakramabhedinīm /
gurupadiṣṭavidhinā brahmarandhraṃ nayetsudhīḥ //
1.65.d:
सुषुम्णावर्त्मनातां च षट्चक्रक्रमभेदिनीम् ।
गुरुपदिष्टविधिना ब्रह्मरन्ध्रं नयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.65.m: And the wise person, by the method taught by the guru, / should lead her, piercing through the sequence of the six cakras, along the path of the suṣumṇā to the brahmarandhra.

1.65.s:
tatrasthāmṛtasaṃmagnīkṛtyātmānaṃ vibhāvayet /
tatprabhāpaṭalavyāptaivimalaṃ cinmayaṃ param //
1.65.d:
तत्रस्थामृतसंमग्नीकृत्यात्मानं विभावयेत् ।
तत्प्रभापटलव्याप्तैविमलं चिन्मयं परम् ॥
1.65.m: One should contemplate oneself submerged in the nectar situated there, / stainless, consisting of consciousness, supreme, pervaded by her mass of splendor.

1.65.s:
punastāṃ svasthalaṃ nītvā hṛdidevaṃ vicintayan /
dṛṣṭvā ca mānasairdravyaiḥ prārthayenmanunāmunā //
1.65.d:
पुनस्तां स्वस्थलं नीत्वा हृदिदेवं विचिन्तयन् ।
दृष्ट्वा च मानसैर्द्रव्यैः प्रार्थयेन्मनुनामुना ॥
1.65.m: Having brought her back to her own place, meditating on the deity in the heart, / and having beheld [him], one should pray with mental offerings using this mantra:

1.65.s:
trailokyacaita nyamayādideva śrīnātha viṣṇo bhavadājñayaiva /
prātaḥ samutthāya tava priyārthaṃ saṃsārayātrāṃ tvanuvartayiṣye //
1.65.d:
त्रैलोक्यचैत न्यमयादिदेव श्रीनाथ विष्णो भवदाज्ञयैव ।
प्रातः समुत्थाय तव प्रियार्थं संसारयात्रां त्वनुवर्तयिष्ये ॥
1.65.m: 'O Primordial Deity consisting of the consciousness of the three worlds, O Śrīnātha, O Viṣṇu, only by your command, / having risen in the morning, I shall pursue worldly activity for your pleasure.'

1.65.s:
viṣṇoriti sthale vipra kārya ūho 'nyadaivate /
tatataḥ kuryātsarvasiddhyai tvajapāyā nivedanam //
1.65.d:
विष्णोरिति स्थले विप्र कार्य ऊहो ऽन्यदैवते ।
तततः कुर्यात्सर्वसिद्ध्यै त्वजपाया निवेदनम् ॥
1.65.m: In place of 'Viṣṇu', O Brahmin, an adaptation should be made for another deity. / Then, for the attainment of all perfections, one should make the offering of the ajapā.

1.65.s:
ṣaṭśatāni divā rātrau sahasrāṇyekaviṃśatiḥ /
ajapākhyāṃ tu gāyatrīṃ jīvojapati sarvadā //
1.65.d:
षट्शतानि दिवा रात्रौ सहस्राण्येकविंशतिः ।
अजपाख्यां तु गायत्रीं जीवोजपति सर्वदा ॥
1.65.m: Six hundred and twenty-one thousand times / during day and night, the living soul constantly recites the gāyatrī named ajapā.

1.65.s:
ṛṣirhaṃsastathāvyaktagātrīchanda īritam /
devatā paramohaṃsaścādyante bījaśaktikam //
1.65.d:
ऋषिर्हंसस्तथाव्यक्तगात्रीछन्द ईरितम् ।
देवता परमोहंसश्चाद्यन्ते बीजशक्तिकम् ॥
1.65.m: Its seer is Haṃsa, its meter is said to be the unmanifest Gāyatrī, / its deity is Paramahaṃsa, and the seed and energy are at the beginning and the end.

1.65.s:
tataḥ ṣaḍaṅgaṃ kurvīta sūryaḥ somonirañjanaḥ /
nirābhāsaśca dharmaśca jñānaṃ ceti tathā punaḥ //
1.65.d:
ततः षडङ्गं कुर्वीत सूर्यः सोमोनिरञ्जनः ।
निराभासश्च धर्मश्च ज्ञानं चेति तथा पुनः ॥
1.65.m: Then one should perform the six limbs: Sūrya, Soma, Nirañjana, / Nirābhāsa, Dharma, and again Jñāna.

1.65.s:
kramādetānhaṃsapūrvānātmanepadapaścimān /
jātayuktānsādhakendra ṣaḍaṅgeṣu niyojayet //
1.65.d:
क्रमादेतान्हंसपूर्वानात्मनेपदपश्चिमान् ।
जातयुक्तान्साधकेन्द्र षडङ्गेषु नियोजयेत् ॥
1.65.m: Having preceded these in order with 'haṃsa' and followed them with the word 'ātmane', / endowed with the case-endings, O best of practitioners, one should assign them to the six limbs.

1.65.s:
hakāraḥ sūryasaṃkāśatejāḥ saṃgacchate bahiḥ /
sakārastādṛśaścaiva praveśe dhyānamīritam //
1.65.d:
हकारः सूर्यसंकाशतेजाः संगच्छते बहिः ।
सकारस्तादृशश्चैव प्रवेशे ध्यानमीरितम् ॥
1.65.m: The syllable 'ha', having the brilliance of the sun, goes outside; / the syllable 'sa' is likewise upon inhalation: this is declared to be the meditation.

1.65.s:
evaṃ dhyātvārpayeddhīmānvahnyarkeṣu vibhāgaśaḥ /
mūlādhāre vādisāṃtabījayukte caturdale //
1.65.d:
एवं ध्यात्वार्पयेद्धीमान्वह्न्यर्केषु विभागशः ।
मूलाधारे वादिसांतबीजयुक्ते चतुर्दले ॥
1.65.m: Having meditated thus, the wise person should apportion it to the fires and suns: / In the four-petaled mūlādhāra endowed with the seed-syllables from 'va' to 'sa',

1.65.s:
bandhūkābhe svaśaktyā tu sahitāpāsvagāya ca /
pāśāṅkuśasudhāpātramodakollāsapāṇaye //
1.65.d:
बन्धूकाभे स्वशक्त्या तु सहितापास्वगाय च ।
पाशाङ्कुशसुधापात्रमोदकोल्लासपाणये ॥
